items.name: "Ballphin Free" Tuna
items.description: "Ballphin Free" Tuna is an item found in the Shipwrecked DLC. When opened, it gives the player a Fish Steak. It cannot be crafted, but can be found either in treasure chests from Messages in Bottles or from breaking Crates with a Hammer for a small chance to drop.
items.beginnerTip: Can be opened for Fish Steak.

items.name: 'The Sty' Oddities Emporium
items.description: Where else can you get a shriveled head.
items.beginnerTip: Sells rare Crafting materials.

items.name: A Smashing Pot
items.description: A Smashing Pot is a naturally spawning decoration exclusive to the Hamlet DLC. They are found both in the Rainforest Biome and in the Pig Ruins, usually in groups. They take two hits with a Hammer to be destroyed, and drop 0-2 Items on destruction.

items.name: Abigail
items.description: Abigail Lillian Carter is Wendy's older twin sister, now dead and thus, a ghost. Wendy can manifest her using her unique starting item, Abigail's Flower. Abigail defends herself and Wendy against attacking Mobs, and she attacks anything that Wendy attacks (even if Wendy withdraws).

items.name: Abigail's Flower
items.description: Abigail's Flower is a character-specific item used by Wendy to summon the Ghost of her twin sister, Abigail.
items.beginnerTip: Summons Abigail.

items.name: Abigail's Flower/DST
items.description: A magical keepsake.
items.beginnerTip: Summons and unsummons Abigail. Control Abigail's aggressiveness.

items.name: Accomploshrine
items.description: Prove your worth as a human being.
items.beginnerTip: A sense of accomplishment for those with nothing else to live for.

items.name: Alarming Clock
items.description: This clock strikes YOU.

items.name: Alchemy Engine
items.description: Unlock even more crafting recipes.
items.beginnerTip: Unlock additional crafting recipes

items.name: Alchemy Engine/DST
items.description: Unlock even more crafting recipes.
items.beginnerTip: Unlock additional crafting recipes

items.name: Alloy
items.description: Alloy is a resource exclusive to the Hamlet DLC. It is obtained by refining Iron Ore in a Smelter and is required for several Crafting recipes. There is a 16.67% chance to spawn a single Alloy in the Secret Bandit Camp.

items.name: Aloe
items.description: Aloe is a Vegetable Food Item exclusive to the Hamlet DLC. It can be obtained from the planted version of Aloe

items.name: Amberosia
items.description: Thulecite's secret ingredient.
items.beginnerTip: Feed

items.name: Ancient Brickwork
items.description: Brick flooring, decorated with a magical technique lost to time.

items.name: Ancient Flooring
items.description: Ancient stone flooring, decorated with a magical technique lost to time.

items.name: Ancient Fuelweaver
items.description: The Ancient Fuelweaver is a Boss Monster exclusive to Don't Starve Together, introduced in A New Reign.

items.name: Ancient Guardian
items.description: The Ancient Guardian is a Boss Monster found within the Labyrinth region of the Ruins. It looks and acts similarly to a Clockwork Rook, but appears as a living creature covered in fur.

items.name: Ancient Key
items.description: The Ancient Key is an item exclusive to Don't Starve Together, introduced in A New Reign. The Ancient Key can be obtained from a Large Ornate Chest after killing the Ancient Guardian.
items.beginnerTip: Activates the Ancient Gateway.

items.name: Ancient Pseudoscience Station
items.description: An Ancient Pseudoscience Station is a special Crafting Structure, found only in the Military and Sacred biomes in the Ruins. It emits enough light to ward off Charlie, and grants access to the Ancient Tab when nearby.
items.beginnerTip: Grant access to Ancient Tab.

items.name: Ancient Pseudoscience Station/DST
items.description: An Ancient Pseudoscience Station is a Crafting Structure found only in the Ruins. It gives access to the Ancient Pseudoscience Filter and emits enough light to protect from Charlie when nearby.
items.beginnerTip: Grant access to Ancient Pseudoscience Filter.

items.name: Ancient Sanctum Stonework
items.description: Ancient stonework from the Sanctum.

items.name: Ancient Statue
items.description: Ancient Statues are structures found in the Ruins and part of the remnants of the Ancient Civilization.

items.name: Ancient Statue/DST
items.description: Ancient Statues are structures found in the Ruins and part of the remnants of the Ancient Civilization.

items.name: Ancient Stonework
items.description: Ancient stonework from an unsealed archive.

items.name: Ancient Tilework
items.description: Tile flooring, decorated with a magical technique lost to time.

items.name: Anenemy
items.description: The Anenemy is a naturally-spawning object exclusive to Don't Starve Together, introduced in Return of Them. It is found on the Rocky Beach and Lunar Archipelago biomes of the Lunar Island.
items.beginnerTip: Deals 60 damage when triggered

items.name: Anti Venom
items.description: Cures that not-so-fresh poison.
items.beginnerTip: Cures poison.

items.name: Arboretum Experiment
items.description: Spine-chilling saplings.
items.beginnerTip: Can be planted to grow into a Totally Normal Tree.

items.name: Armored Boat
items.description: Shell out for this hearty vessel.
items.beginnerTip: Sailing Speed: 6

items.name: Ash Tree
items.description: Ash Trees are a variety of Tree found in the Volcano biome in the Shipwrecked DLC. When chopped down with an Axe, they will yield Ashes. They do not have a life cycle and do not leave a stump behind. Ash Trees are renewable, after they are destroyed, a new one has a chance to spawn at the same location during Dry Season.

items.name: Ashy Turf
items.description: Ashy Turf is one of the Turf items that appears in the Shipwrecked DLC, acquired by digging Volcano tiles with a Pitchfork. Like other Turfs, it can be placed on any bare ground tile or used as fuel.

items.name: Asparagazpacho
items.description: Asparagazpacho is a Warly-specific Food item cooked in the Portable Crock Pot, exclusive to Don't Starve Together. It requires two Asparagus and two Ice to cook.
items.beginnerTip: Lowers temperature by 20 degrees for 5 minutes

items.name: Asparagus
items.description: Asparagus is a Vegetable Food Item introduced in the Hamlet DLC. It can both be found growing naturally in the world and be obtained through Farming. Asparagus restores 12.5 Hunger when eaten raw, compared to 25 hunger eaten cooked, which makes it a much better item cooked than raw (as both restore 3 health anyway). The only disadvantage is that the spoilage time is cut in half after being cooked, which makes it advisable to cook asparagus when around halfway through its perishing time to preserve the beneficial properties of cooked asparagus for as long as possible.

items.name: Asparagus Soup
items.description: Asparagus Soup is a Crock Pot dish introduced in the Hamlet DLC. It requires at least one raw or cooked Asparagus, and at least another 0.5 Vegetables. Asparagus Soup takes 10 seconds to cook and restores 20 Health, 18.75 Hunger and 5 Sanity when eaten.

items.name: Asparagus Soup/DST
items.description: Asparagus Soup is also included in Don't Starve Together. However, it requires more Vegetables (1.5). Filler cannot be Meats or Inedible. Using Ice will result in Vegetable Stinger. Asparagus Soup takes 10 seconds to cook and restores 20 Health, 18.75 Hunger and 5 Sanity when eaten.

items.name: Asparagus/DST
items.description: Asparagus is present in Don't Starve Together where it can only be obtained through Farming. Planting a Tubular Seed will produce Asparagus. Warly requires Asparagus to cook Asparagazpacho in his Portable Crock Pot. Asparagus restores 12.5 Hunger when eaten raw, compared to 25 Hunger eaten cooked, which makes it a much better item cooked than raw (as both restore 3 health anyway). The only disadvantage is that the spoilage time is cut in half after being cooked, which makes it advisable to cook Asparagus when around halfway through its perishing time to preserve the beneficial properties of Cooked Asparagus for as long as possible.

items.name: Astral Detector
items.description: What secrets will it unearth?

items.name: Astroggles
items.description: Utilize potato eyes to see through storms.
items.beginnerTip: Lets players see through Moonstorms and Sandstorms. Shows the location of Wagstaff in the Moonstorm.

items.name: Axe
items.description: Chop down trees!
items.beginnerTip: Chops wood.

items.name: Axe/DST
items.description: Chop down trees!
items.beginnerTip: Chops wood.

items.name: B.U.D.D.Y.
items.description: Where is that signal coming from?

items.name: Backpack
items.description: Carry more stuff.
items.beginnerTip: +8 inventory slots

items.name: Backpack/DST
items.description: Carry more stuff.
items.beginnerTip: +8 inventory slots

items.name: Bacon and Eggs
items.description: Bacon and Eggs is a Meat Food item cooked in the Crock Pot by adding 2.0 units of Eggs and more than 1 unit of Meats. It takes 40 seconds to cook.

items.name: Bacon and Eggs/DST
items.description: Bacon and Eggs is a Meat Food item cooked in the Crock Pot by adding 2.0 units of Eggs and 1.25 units of Meats. It takes 40 seconds to cook.

items.name: Ball Pein Hammer
items.description: For when you wanna wreck things gently.
items.beginnerTip: Can chisel ancient statues for gold and relics.

items.name: Ballphin Palace
items.description: EeEe! EeEe!

items.name: Bamboo
items.description: Bamboo is a renewable resource that can be gathered by hacking down a Bamboo Patch with a Machete in the Shipwrecked DLC. It can also be obtained by hammering a Wildbore House or a Wildbore Head.

items.name: Bamboo Patch
items.description: Bamboo Patches are plants introduced in the Shipwrecked DLC. They are found commonly in the Jungle biome and can be cut down with a Machete to yield one Bamboo. They take 4 days to regrow and not affected by Winter cold.

items.name: Banana
items.description: Bananas (or Cave Bananas in the base game) are Food Items found on Cave Banana Trees. These trees grow underground and will regrow after 4 days once picked. Splumonkeys will pick Bananas from Cave Banana Trees on sight, which has no effect on the 4-day regrowth period of Bananas. Splumonkeys also are more likely to follow and steal from a player if the player is carrying any number of Bananas. __NOTOC__

items.name: Banana Pop
items.description: Banana Pop is a Crock Pot recipe introduced in the Shipwrecked DLC. It is made from 1 Raw Banana, 1 Ice, and 1 Twig or Dorsal Fin. It is a great Sanity restoring food, as Ice can be plentiful from refining Hail during the Hurricane Season or using an Ice Maker 3000.
items.beginnerTip: Lowers temperature by 10 degrees over 10 seconds.

items.name: Banana Pop/DST
items.description: Banana Pop is a Crock Pot recipe that is made from 1 Banana, 1 Ice, and 1 Twig. Its cooking ingredients cannot contain any kind of Meats or Fish. Adding Wobster, Fishes or Meats will result in Lobster Bisque, Fishsticks and Kabobs respectively.
items.beginnerTip: Lowers temperature by 10 degrees over 10 seconds.

items.name: Banana/DST
items.description: Bananas are Food Items found on Banana Bushes on the Moon Quay and Cave Banana Trees found in Caves and Ruins. Splumonkeys drop one Banana on death and are more likely to follow and steal from a player carrying any number of Bananas.

items.name: Bandit Stash Map
items.description: The Bandit Stash Map is an Item exclusive to Hamlet DLC that is dropped by the Masked Pig upon death. If the player reads it, a red X appears on their Map indicating the location of a Secret Bandit Camp.

items.name: Barbed Helm
items.description: The Barbed Helm is an item added to The Forge in Don't Starve Together.
items.beginnerTip: +10% physical damage

items.name: Basalt Eruption
items.description: The Basalt Eruption is an object exclusive to the Hamlet DLC. When fighting the Large Iron Hulk, it will encircle itself with a barrier made of Basalt Eruptions, potentially trapping the player. It can be mined for Rocks and Flint.

items.name: Bat Bat
items.description: All this science is so... draining.
items.beginnerTip: Leeches 6.8 of target's on hit.

items.name: Bat Bat/DST
items.description: All this science is so... draining.
items.beginnerTip: Leeches 6.8 of target's on hit.

items.name: Bat Cave
items.description: Bat Caves are Don't Starve Together exclusive objects found in the Caves. They spawn Batilisks, thus allowing players to determine if the area contains Batilisks while also making them renewable in the Caves.

items.name: Bat Hat
items.description: The Bat Hat is Hat Item exclusive to Don't Starve Together, dropped by the Hound Batilisk.
items.beginnerTip: Causes attacks to regenerate HP. Makes Batilisks and Naked Mole Bats neutral towards the wearer.

items.name: Batilisk Wing
items.description: A Batilisk Wing is a Meat food Item dropped by Batilisks when killed. It can be cooked to make a Cooked Batilisk Wing or dried on a Drying Rack for 2 days to give Small Jerky. It can be traded to the Pig King for a Gold Nugget. It is also the essential item in crafting the Bat Bat.

items.name: Batilisk Wing/DST
items.description: A Batilisk Wing is a Meat Food Item dropped by Batilisks when killed. It can be cooked to make a Cooked Batilisk Wing or dried on a Drying Rack for 2 days to give Small Jerky. It can be traded to the Pig King for a Gold Nugget. It is also the essential item in crafting the Bat Bat.

items.name: Battle Helm
items.description: The unicorn is what protects you.|protection=80%

items.name: Battle Helm/DST
items.description: The unicorn is what protects you.

items.name: Battle Paddle
items.description: The Battle Paddle is an item exclusive to Don't Starve Together, introduced in The Curse of Moon Quay update. It can be obtained by killing a Prime Mate. The item can be used as an Oar or as a Melee weapon and cannot be crafted by the player. The Battle Paddle has up to 100 uses when used as a weapon or up to 500 uses when used as an oar, and the force applied to the Boat it is used on is ×0.6 units. As a weapon it does 51 damage, matching that of a Tentacle Spike.

items.name: Battle Spear
items.description: The gold makes it sharper.

items.name: Battle Spear/DST
items.description: The gold makes it sharper.

items.name: Bean Bugs
items.description: Bean Bugs are a Food Item exclusive to the Hamlet DLC. They can be found under Stone Slabs. Eating them raw or cooked will restore Hunger, but at the cost of Sanity loss.

items.name: Beard
items.description: Beard may refer to:

items.name: Beard Hair
items.description: Beard Hair is a resource mainly acquired by shaving Wilson's Beard with a Razor. It can also be acquired by killing Beardlings and Beardlords, creatures that replace Rabbits and Bunnymen, respectively, when Sanity drops below 40% (48 for Willow, 40 to 120 for WX-78, 100 for Wickerbottom, 60 for Wes, 40 for Webber, 60 for Wortox, and 80 for all other characters) and Shadow Splumonkeys, which replace Splumonkeys during the Nightmare Phase.

items.name: Beard Hair Rug
items.description: Some people just like to do art.

items.name: Beard Hair Rug/DST
items.description: Some people just like to do art.

items.name: Beard Hair/DST
items.description: Beard Hair is a resource mainly acquired by shaving Wilson's Beard with a Razor. It can also be acquired by killing Beardlings and Beardlords, creatures that replace Rabbits and Bunnymen, respectively, when Sanity drops below 40% (48 for Willow, 40 to 120 for WX-78, 100 for Wickerbottom, 60 for Wes, 40 for Webber, 60 for Wortox, and 80 for all other characters) and Shadow Splumonkeys, which replace Splumonkeys during the Nightmare Phase.

items.name: Bed Roll
items.description: Bed Rolls are craftable items that can be used to sleep through the night. There are two types of bed rolls: Straw Rolls and Fur Rolls.

items.name: Bed Roll/DST
items.description: Bed Rolls are craftable items that can be used to sleep through the night. There are two types of bed rolls: Straw Rolls and Fur Rolls.

items.name: Bee Box
items.description: Store your own bees.

items.name: Bee Box/DST
items.description: Store your own bees.

items.name: Bee Mine
items.description: Weaponized bees. What could go wrong?

items.name: Bee Mine/DST
items.description: Weaponized bees. What could go wrong?

items.name: Bee Queen
items.description: The Bee Queen is a Boss Monster exclusive to Don't Starve Together, introduced in A New Reign. She has the appearance of a gigantic Bee with two large wings, a stinger, black and yellow stripes on her thorax and a beehive on her abdomen. The Bee Queen is spawned after a Gigantic Beehive is Hammered sufficiently. She will emerge from the hive, leaving a honey blotch behind. She immediately spawns Grumble Bees, and will auto-target any player that approaches.

items.name: Bee Queen Crown
items.description: The Bee Queen Crown is a head slot Armor Item exclusive to Don't Starve Together, introduced in A New Reign. It is obtained by killing the Bee Queen or from Gifts dropped by the Loot Stash. The Bee Queen Crown has 945 durability and absorbs 70% of physical damage. It also provides 20% Wetness resistance.
items.beginnerTip: Converts insanity auras into sanity auras at half the rate.

items.name: Beefalo
items.description: Beefalo are neutral Animals that spawn in the Savanna and Mandrake Forest biomes. Upon death, they drop 4 Meat, 3 Beefalo Wool, & 1 Beefalo Horn (33% chance). Shaving them while asleep also drops 3 Beefalo Wool, which will regrow in three days. When blown, Beefalo Horn causes up to 5 grown Beefalo to follow during daytime.

items.name: Beefalo Hat
items.description: Be one with the herd! Smell included.
items.beginnerTip: Delays Freezing. Lowers Beefalo aggression during mating season.

items.name: Beefalo Hat/DST
items.description: Be one with the herd! Smell included.
items.beginnerTip: Delays Freezing. Lowers Beefalo aggression during mating season.

items.name: Beefalo Horn
items.description: thumb|Wilson using a Beefalo Horn. thumb|Using the Beefalo Horn to lead Beefalo into a pen. A Beefalo Horn is an Item dropped 33% of the time after killing a Beefalo. When blown, the Beefalo Horn uses 10% of its durability and causes up to 5 grown Beefalo to follow the character for the rest of the current day or until they meet up with the player, as at night Beefalo will stop following and go to sleep. They will move at their walking speed and will not fight hostile creatures the way that following Pigs do. Baby Beefalo still follow their parents, which means that they will also move; however, the Horn will not cause them to leave their parents.

items.name: Beefalo Horn/DST
items.description: thumb|Wilson using a Beefalo Horn. thumb|Using the Beefalo Horn to lead Beefalo into a pen. A Beefalo Horn is an Item dropped 33% of the time after killing a Beefalo. When blown, the Beefalo Horn uses 10% of its durability and causes up to 5 grown Beefalo to follow the character for the rest of the current day or until they meet up with the player, as at night Beefalo will stop following and go to sleep. They will move at their walking speed and will not fight hostile creatures the way that following Pigs do. Baby Beefalo still follow their parents, which means that they will also move; however, the Horn will not cause them to leave their parents.

items.name: Beefalo Wool
items.description: Beefalo Wool is an Item obtained by either killing a Beefalo or a Baby Beefalo, or by shaving a sleeping Beefalo with a Razor (by clicking them with a Razor held by the mouse cursor). It is used to make a Saddle, Winter Hat, Beefalo Hat, Puffy Vest, and Carpeted Flooring.

items.name: Beefalo Wool/DST
items.description: Beefalo Wool is an Item obtained by killing a Beefalo or a Baby Beefalo, by shaving a sleeping Beefalo with a Razor (by clicking them with a Razor held by the mouse cursor), or using a Brush on a Beefalo. It is used to make a Saddle, Winter Hat, Beefalo Hat, Puffy Vest, and Carpeted Flooring.

items.description: -|Generic=

items.name: Beefy Greens
items.description: Beefy Greens is a Food Item exclusive to Don't Starve Together introduced in Return of Them. It is cooked in a Crock Pot by combining at least 1 Leafy Meat and a Vegetable value of at least 3.0. It has a Crock Pot Priority of 25 and it takes 40 seconds to cook.

items.name: Beehive
items.description: Beehives are naturally occurring structures only found in Grassland Biomes, holding up to 6 Bees or Killer Bees. They have 200 health, and drop 1 Honeycomb and 3 Honey when destroyed. Unlike Bee Boxes, Bees have no effect on the items dropped. Beehives do not respawn, making Honeycomb a non-renewable resource.

items.name: Beehive/DST
items.description: Beehives are naturally occurring structures only found in Grassland Biomes, holding up to 6 Bees or Killer Bees. They have 200 health, and drop 1 Honeycomb and 3 Honey when destroyed. Unlike Bee Boxes, Bees have no effect on the items dropped. Beehives do not respawn.

items.name: Beekeeper Hat
items.description: Protection against angry bees.

items.name: Beekeeper Hat/DST
items.description: Protection against angry bees.

items.name: Beeswax
items.description: A useful preservative wax.
items.beginnerTip: Melts near heat.

items.name: Beeswax/DST
items.description: A useful preservative wax.

items.name: Belt of Hunger
items.description: Keep that belly full.
items.beginnerTip: Reduces hunger loss by 40%. Restores sanity over time.

items.name: Belt of Hunger/DST
items.description: Keep that belly full.
items.beginnerTip: Reduces hunger loss by 40%. Restores sanity over time.

items.name: Benevolent Rabbit King
items.description: The Benevolent Rabbit King is summoned by giving 12 to 16 Carrots to a Rabbit Hole. There is also a small chance that the player can find a Fortuitous Rabbit that will then turn into a Benevolent Rabbit King when caught. When standing next to Benevolent Rabbit King, the player can access to Trading Hutch Filter.
items.beginnerTip: Grant access to Trading Hutch Filter

items.name: Bernie
items.description: A familiar face in this mad world.

items.name: Berries
items.description: Berries are Fruit Food Items that can be found on Berry Bushes. Berries restore 9.375 when eaten, and take 6 days to spoil. Juicy berries are the alternative of berries, and provide a faster rotting but larger quantity of food to snack on.

items.name: Berries/DST
items.description: Berries are Fruit Food Items that can be found on Berry Bushes. Berries restore 9.375 when eaten, and take 6 days to spoil. Juicy berries are the alternative of berries, and provide a faster rotting but larger quantity of food to snack on.

items.name: Berry Bush
items.description: Berry Bushes are Plants commonly found in Grasslands and occasionally Forests. They can be harvested to receive 1 Berries, after which they will need from 3 to 5 Days to regrow (Rain will reduce this time). Berry Bushes can be dug up with a Shovel and replanted in a new location. Doing this will require the bush to be fertilized before it will regrow any new Berries. If the player tries to dig up a Berry Bush without fertilizing it, it will result in 2 Twigs and the bush's destruction.

items.name: Berry Bush/DST
items.description: Berry Bushes are Plants commonly found in Grasslands and occasionally Forests. They can be harvested to receive 1 Berries, after which they will need from 3 to 5 Days to regrow (Rain will reduce this time). Berry Bushes can be dug up with a Shovel and replanted in a new location. Doing this will require the bush to be fertilized before it will regrow any new Berries. If the player tries to dig up a Berry Bush without fertilizing it, it will result in 2 Twigs and the bush's destruction.

items.name: Big Bat Cave
items.description: -|Generic=

items.name: Bile-Covered Slop
items.description: Bile-Covered Slop is a Meat Food Item found in the Shipwrecked DLC. The Tiger Shark will spit some every now and then near its Den to feed Sharkittens.

items.name: Bio Data
items.description: Bio Data is an item that is exclusive to Don't Starve Together. It is dropped by the Bio Scanalyzer after scanning a mob and can be used to craft Circuits exclusive to WX-78. Mobs can be re-scanned after one day to get more Bio Data.

items.name: Bioluminescence
items.description: Bioluminescence is a passive immobile Mob introduced in the Shipwrecked DLC. It is found in Deep Oceans in groups of 12. It can be considered the aquatic version of Fireflies, and emits light during the night. It will not appear until dusk arrives, and will stay until dawn. It does however still persist during a Full Moon. Once found, it can be caught with Trawl Net or Net while it is visible. Unlike Fireflies, it won't disappear when player character approaches, so they can be used as a permanent protection against Charlie.

items.name: Birchnut
items.description: Birchnuts are Food items dropped from Birchnut Trees or Birchnutters in the Reign of Giants DLC. Like Pine Cones, Birchnuts can be planted to create a new Birchnut Tree. It takes from 2.5 to 5 minutes for them to grow from saplings into small trees. Birchnuts can alternatively be used as a food item by being cooked on a campfire and turned into a roasted Birchnut.
items.beginnerTip: Can be planted.

items.name: Birchnut Tree
items.description: Birchnut Trees are Plants found in the Reign of Giants DLC. They are found mainly in Grasslands and frequently in Deciduous Forests. When chopped, they will yield 1-3 Logs and up to 2 Birchnuts, depending on the season.

items.name: Birchnut Tree/DST
items.description: Birchnut Trees are Plants found in the Reign of Giants DLC. They are found mainly in Grasslands and frequently in Deciduous Forests. When chopped, they will yield 1-3 Logs and up to 2 Birchnuts, depending on the season.

items.name: Birchnut/DST
items.description: Birchnuts are Food items dropped from Birchnut Trees or Birchnutters. Like Pine Cones, Birchnuts can be planted to create a new Birchnut Tree. It takes from 2.5 to 5 minutes for them to grow from saplings into small trees. Birchnuts can alternatively be used as a food item by being cooked on a campfire and turned into a roasted Birchnut.
items.beginnerTip: Can be planted.

items.name: Bird Trap
items.description: Capture winged beasts.
items.beginnerTip: Captures Birds. Can be baited.

items.name: Bird Trap/DST
items.description: Capture winged beasts.
items.beginnerTip: Can catch Birds.

items.name: Bird Whistle
items.description: For calling birds. Did you make it too big?
items.beginnerTip: Spawns the BFB.

items.name: Birdcage
items.description: A happy home for your avian friends.

items.name: Birdcage/DST
items.description: A happy home for your avian friends.

items.name: Birds
items.description: When killed, birds drop a Morsel or a Feather, and all other birds nearby will fly away. They are considered innocent creatures and killing them directly adds points to the player's naughtiness level, which causes Krampus to appear. Killing a Crow adds 1 point to the player's naughtiness level while killing a Redbird, Snowbird or Canary adds 2 points to the player's naughtiness level.

items.name: Bisque
items.description: Bisque is a Crock Pot recipe introduced in the Don't Starve: Shipwrecked DLC. It is made by combining 3 raw Limpets and 1 Ice.

items.name: Blacksmith's Edge
items.description: The Blacksmith's Edge is a weapon added to The Forge event in Don't Starve Together (an unlockable item in the 2018 Crucible). Dropped by the last warrior of wave 9. It is a melee weapon that deals 35 damage. While under Wigfrid's Warcry or after landing 14 hits in a row, a character will jump up and deal 138 damage.

items.name: Blossomed Wreath
items.description: The Blossomed Wreath is an item added to The Forge in Don't Starve Together. It is dropped in the middle of wave 10 from a random enemy unit with a 50% chance, with a chance for a Magnificent Helm of Might instead. If not dropped, it is a guaranteed drop from the Great Crucible Hog Warrior.

items.name: Blubber
items.description: Blubber is an item in the Shipwrecked DLC. It is used to craft Blubber Suits and Windbreakers. Hacking a fully bloated Blue Whale Carcass or White Whale Carcass will drop 2 to 6 Blubber. Blubber cannot be Cooked or used in a Crock Pot. When eaten, it grants 10 Health, and 10 Hunger.

items.name: Blubber Suit
items.description: A disgusting way to stay dry.
items.beginnerTip: Provides 100% protection against Wetness. Delays freezing during Winter.

items.name: Blue Cap
items.description: Blue Caps are Vegetable Food Items that can be harvested on Blue Mushrooms or Blue Mushtrees. Raw Blue Caps have the most positive effects of all the Mushrooms. When eaten raw, they restore 20 and 12.5 at the cost of 15 . They can also be used as Crock Pot filler with a 0.5 vegetable value.

items.name: Blue Cap/DST
items.description: Blue Caps are Vegetable Food Items that can be harvested on Blue Mushrooms or Blue Mushtrees. Raw Blue Caps have the most positive effects of all the Mushrooms. When eaten raw, they restore 20 and 12.5 at the cost of 15 . They can also be used as Crock Pot filler with a 0.5 vegetable value. In Don't Starve Together, the Toadstool has a chance to drop Blue Cap upon death. Blue Caps are required to craft Nightflyer Lures and the Blue Funcap. A Mushroom Planter can be used to grow Blue Mushrooms by planting a Blue Cap or Blue Mushroom Spores in it.

items.name: Blue Gem

Additionally, Boulders may also provide Flint, Gold Nuggets, and Nitre. Boulders do not respawn; however, Rocks, Flint, Gold Nuggets, and Nitre are renewable resources because they can be found after Earthquakes while underground.

Boulders are renewable via a Meteor Shower on the surface, or the Cave-in Boulders from Antlion or an Earthquake when a Shadow Rift is active, in the caves.

items.name: Catcoon

It will also give the player 5 points of Naughtiness, which may result in spawning Krampus.

items.name: Cave Banana Tree
items.description: A Cave Banana Tree is a fruit-bearing plant which only grows in the Ruins and Caves, commonly in the Village Biome and occasionally in a Sunken Forest. It provides a Cave Banana when picked and regrows the fruit in four days.

items.description: Cave Lichen is a harvestable fungus found in the Ruins, commonly in the Wilds and occasionally Village Biomes. A small number can also be found in the Labyrinth near the Ancient Guardian. When harvested, it yields 1 Lichen and then takes 3-5 days to become harvestable again. It does not grow during Winter.

items.description: Caviar is a Food Item exclusive to the Shipwrecked DLC. It is cooked in the Crock Pot by adding 1 Vegetable and 1 Roe. Alternatively, 3 Cooked Roe can be used.

items.name: Celestial Orb
items.description: The Celestial Orb is a portable Crafting station exclusive to Don't Starve Together. It is obtained by mining a Suspicious Boulder. If dropped on the ground, the Celestial Orb can be used to access the Level 1 Celestial Filter, which unlocks the crafting recipe for the Moon Rock Idol and Portal Paraphernalia. Similar to Chester's Eye Bone, it will automatically drop from the Inventory of players when leaving the game or entering the Caves. Celestial Orb will sink in the water, however, it will return to the coast afterwards.
items.beginnerTip: Grants access to the Celestial Filter.

Since Freshwater Fish only counts as 0.5 Fish units, at least a large Ocean Fish or Raw Fish is required to make this recipe.
items.beginnerTip: Lowers temperature by 10 degrees over 10 seconds.

items.description: The Clockwork Rook is the third monster in the Chess Monster collection. Like the Clockwork Knight and Bishop, the Rook is a mechanical creature generally found around Maxwell's parts of the world (Chess terrain and the Wooden Thing). The Clockwork Rook is the combination of a rhino and a rook chess piece. __NOTOC__

items.name: Cloth
items.description: Bamboo is so versatile!

items.name: Cobblestones
items.description: Build your own road to nowhere.

items.name: Cobblestones/DST
items.description: Build your own road to nowhere.

items.name: Coconade
items.description: KA-BLAM!
items.beginnerTip: Explodes and sets nearby targets on fire.

items.name: Coconut
items.description: Coconuts are a Fruit Food resource found in the Shipwrecked DLC. They are mainly obtained by cutting down fully-grown Palm Trees with an Axe. They are dropped by Palm Treeguards upon death. Additionally, their ranged attack has a 1% chance to leave an intact Coconut. Rolling three carrots at the Slot Machine and, very rarely, digging Sandy Piles also has a chance to drop a Coconut.
items.beginnerTip: Can be planted to grow a Palm Tree

items.name: Codex Umbra
items.description: The Codex Umbra is a character-exclusive item that Maxwell starts the game with. When used, it sacrifices 15 health and 55 of maximum sanity to spawn a Shadow Puppet clone of Maxwell. It has infinite durability and requires 2 Nightmare Fuel to be used. For each puppet active, Maxwell's maximum sanity is reduced, similar to how Meat Effigies reduce maximum health. A maximum of 3 puppets can be active at one time and each one will disappear 2.5 days after it was summoned. If a Shadow Puppet is killed or despawns, Maxwell will get the used max sanity back.
items.beginnerTip: Can Only be used by Maxwell

items.name: Codex Umbra/DST
items.description: It'll blow your mind.

items.name: Coffee
items.description: Coffee is a Crock Pot recipe introduced in the Shipwrecked DLC. It is made by combining 3 Roasted Coffee Beans and 1 Dairy, Sweetener, or a fourth Roasted Coffee Bean.
items.beginnerTip: Increased movement speed for 4 minutes

items.name: Coffee Beans
items.description: Coffee Beans are Fruit Food items introduced in the Shipwrecked DLC. They can be harvested from Coffee Plants. When eaten, they restore 9.375 . Coffee Beans spoil in 6 Days and can be used in the Crock Pot and provide 0.5 fruit value.

items.name: Coffee Plant
items.description: Coffee Plants are plants introduced in the Shipwrecked DLC. They can be found only inside Volcano, but can be dug with a Shovel to be moved outside. They can be harvested to receive 1 Coffee Beans after which they will need 4 to 5 Days to regrow. Rain does not reduce this time.

items.name: Coin
items.description: There is a trade and market relationship in the Gorge. Humanoids of one kind or another may offer the survivalists items or resources that can help satisfy the insatiable Maw. The inhabitants of The Gorge use small disc-shaped objects as currency: coins, medallions, etc., given by the Mouth itself for various dishes. Swamp Pigs use other items for trade, however.

items.name: Compass
items.description: Points the way north.
items.beginnerTip: Shows the direction the map is rotated. Shows the location of other players carrying a compass.

items.name: Compass/DST
items.description: Points the way north.
items.beginnerTip: Shows the direction the map is rotated. Shows the location of other players carrying a compass.

items.name: Compost
items.description: Compost is an item exclusive to Don't Starve Together and introduced in Return of Them. It is produced by a Composting Bin.
items.beginnerTip: Fertilize Farm

items.name: Compost Wrap
items.description: 'Herbal' therapy.
items.beginnerTip: Heals the character when used.

items.name: Compost Wrap/DST
items.description: 'Herbal' therapy.
items.beginnerTip: Heals the character when used.

items.name: Construction Amulet
items.description: Craft with a discount!
items.beginnerTip: Halves crafting requirements Raises Sanity over time

items.name: Construction Amulet/DST
items.description: Craft with a discount!
items.beginnerTip: Halves crafting requirements Raises Sanity over time

items.name: Cookie Crumbles
items.description: The Cookie Crumbles were introduced in 2019. They appear when following a Gingerbread Pig and are dropped by Gingerbread Pigs, Gingerbread Pig Houses and Gingerbread Vargs. They can be eaten to restore 1 and spoil in 1 Day. Unlike most foods, Cookie Crumbles do not leave behind rot after spoiling.

items.name: Cookie Cutter Cap
items.description: One must always be sharply dressed.

items.name: Cooking
items.description: Cooking is the process of turning raw Food into cooked, or otherwise improved, food which, in general, adds a Health bonus and sometimes improves their Hunger or Sanity benefits as well. There are three types of cooking: Fire, Drying Rack, and Crock Pot.

items.name: Cookpot
items.description: The Cookpot is needed for cooking The Gorge Recipes. It can be obtained from the Cookpot Kit. The Cookpot has 3 slots for ingredients. Basically, soups, pasta and other dishes that require a bowl are prepared in the Cookpot.

items.name: Coral
items.description: Coral is a resource in the Shipwrecked DLC. It can be obtained by mining Coral Reefs. It is also frequently obtained when using a Trawl Net. Coral is used to craft Particulate Purifiers, Anti Venom, and Mussel Beds, and can also be Refined into Limestone.

items.name: Coral Larva
items.description: The Coral Larva is an Item introduced in the Shipwrecked DLC. It can be obtained by Hammering Coral Reefs and can be used to craft a Coral Nubbin.

items.name: Coral Nubbin
items.description: There's nubbin better!

items.name: Coral Reef
items.description: When mined with a Pickaxe, Coral Reefs drop 2-4 pieces of Coral total. After being mined, they can be Hammered to drop 1-3 Limestones and a Coral Larva. If the rock is not hammered, the Coral will fully grow back after 12 Days. It has a heavily increased grow rate during rain, similar to Mushrooms. It is also possible to replant Coral Reefs using Coral Nubbins. __NOTOC__

items.name: Cork Bat
items.description: Like a wiffle bat filled with pain.

items.name: Cork Bowl Canoe
items.description: Good for portage and tough as porridge.
items.beginnerTip: Sailing Speed: 4

items.name: Cork Candle Hat
items.description: Hands free spelunking on shoe string.
items.beginnerTip: Provides light while worn

items.name: Corn
items.description: Corn is a common Vegetable Food item that can be grown on a Farm Plot by planting Seeds or Corn Seeds (Clustered Seeds).

items.name: Corn/DST
items.description: Corn is a common Vegetable Food item that can be grown in Farm Soil by planting Seeds or Corn Seeds (Clustered Seeds).

items.name: Corvus Goodfeather
items.description: The Corvus Goodfeather allows the player to access items in Cawnival Creation Filter while standing close to him. The filter only has the Cawnival Sapling initially. After purchasing the Cawnival Sapling, the rest of the filter becomes available. The players can purchase Cawnival Tokens and Cawnival Games that are only available in this event.

items.name: Cowl
items.description: Harness the power of sonar.

items.name: Crab Meat
items.description: -| Crab Meat=

items.name: Crabbit Den
items.description: Crabbit Dens are naturally occurring objects from the Shipwrecked DLC. Crabbits spawn from the dens, and roam near them during the day and run to their den at dusk. Unlike Rabbits, they do not go back to their dens when being chased, instead burrowing into Shifting Sands. Crabbits go to sleep when they are outside of their dens at night and may be attacked.

items.name: Crabby Hermit
items.description: The Crabby Hermit, or Pearl, is a Mob exclusive to Don't Starve Together. She can be found on the Hermit Island.

items.name: Craftsmerm House
items.description: A home fit for a Merm.

items.name: Craggy Carapace
items.description: The Craggy Carapace is a body slot Armor Item exclusive to Don't Starve Together, dropped by the Rock Master.
items.beginnerTip: Ignores Knockback entirely. Slows wearer by -30%.

items.name: Crank Thing
items.description: The Crank Thing is an Item and one of four Things used on the Wooden Thing to travel to the next world. It spawns naturally in every world in its own Set Piece. It is surrounded by Evil Flowers in a small patch of Savanna Turf along with a Pig House surrounded by 3 Spiky Trees and an Axe at 100%.

items.name: Crashed Balloon
items.description: -| Deflated Balloon= |-| Wicker Basket=

items.name: Crate
items.description: Crates are naturally spawning structures introduced in the Shipwrecked DLC. They are occasionally found in the Beach Biome. They can be Hammered to yield one random Item in addition to one Board. Crates have their own Map icon, allowing them to be easily found later.

items.name: Creamy Potato Purée
items.description: Creamy Potato Purée is a Vegetable Food item exclusive to Don't Starve Together. It is cooked in the Crock Pot with 2 Potatoes, 1 Garlic, and 1 filler, and takes 20 seconds to cook.

items.name: Crop Seeds
items.description: Crop Seeds are a specialized version of Seeds, used primarily for Farming. When planted in a Basic/Improved Farm, they produce the crop they are named after (for example, Carrot Seeds produce Carrots).

items.name: Crop Seeds/DST
items.description: Crop Seeds are a specialized version of Seeds, used primarily for Farming. In Don't Starve Together, Crop Seeds have different visuals but they have the same functionality as in Don't Starve. Initially, Crop Seeds have an assumed name related to their shape. Once the player has accumulated enough knowledge by researching the Farm Plant with a Gardeneer Hat, their name changes to the regular name.

items.name: Crumbling Brazier
items.description: A Crumbling Brazier is a naturally occurring Structure introduced in the Hamlet DLC. They can be found in the Deep Rainforest, typically near Ruinous Entrances.
items.beginnerTip: Provides Light and Heat while burning.

items.name: Crustashine
items.description: Crustashines are passive Mobs exclusive to Don't Starve Together, introduced in The Curse of Moon Quay update. They are found roaming on Moon Quay and spawn from the Unnatural Portal. They provide a small amount of light while in their mob state. Similar to Rabbits they will run away from the player when approached but can be caught with a Trap, resulting in it being added to the player's inventory. In this state, the Crustashine will die after five in-game days, but can be fed with any kind of food.

items.name: Crystal Tiara
items.description: The Crystal Tiara is an item added to The Forge in Don't Starve Together. It is dropped by a random enemy.

items.name: Cultivated Turf
items.description: A civilized patch of dirt.

items.name: Curly Tails Mud Spa
items.description: The mud really cleans the pores.
items.beginnerTip: Sells Healing items.

items.name: Cut Grass
items.description: Cut Grass is a renewable resource Item harvested from Grass Tufts found naturally in the world. It can be used on numerous starter recipes and in even more advanced items when refined into Rope.

items.name: Cut Grass/DST
items.description: Cut Grass is a renewable resource Item harvested from Grass Tufts found naturally in the world. It can be used on numerous starter recipes and in even more advanced items when refined into Rope.

items.name: Cut Reeds
items.description: Cut Reeds are an item obtained by harvesting Reeds that grow in Swamps. Reeds can be refined into Papyrus and are a crafting ingredient for a Blow Dart, Sleep Dart, Fire Dart and Pan Flute. Reeds grow back after 3 days from being picked, but they will not grow in Winter.

items.name: Cut Reeds/DST
items.description: Cut Reeds are an item obtained by harvesting Reeds that grow in Swamps. Reeds can be refined into Papyrus and are a crafting ingredient for a Blow Dart, Sleep Dart, Fire Dart and Pan Flute. Reeds grow back after 3 days from being picked, but they will not grow in Winter.

items.name: Cutlass Supreme
items.description: Fish were harmed in the making of this.
items.beginnerTip: Deals additional 34 damage against Sealnado.

items.name: Cutless
items.description: The Cutless is a Melee weapon exclusive to Don't Starve Together, introduced in The Curse of Moon Quay update. It is used by aggressive Powder Monkeys who will drop the item on their death. The Cutless deals a small amount of damage equal to that of an axe. When hitting a creature that has an inventory, including another player, it will knock the leftmost item from it.
items.beginnerTip: Steals items

items.name: Dairy
items.description: There are 3 basic Dairy food items in-game, none of which have a cooked version.

items.name: Dapper Vest
items.description: Rugged, yet stylish.
items.beginnerTip: Restores sanity over time Delays freezing during Winter

items.name: Dapper Vest/DST
items.description: Rugged, yet stylish.
items.beginnerTip: Restores sanity over time Delays freezing during Winter

items.name: Dark Sword
items.description: Lucid dreaming damage.

items.name: Dark Sword/DST
items.description: Lucid dreaming damage.

items.name: Dark Tatters
items.description: Dark Tatters are a crafting item within both the Hamlet DLC and Don't Starve Together. In Hamlet, they are obtained from the Ancient Herald, spawned in during the Aporkalypse.

items.name: Dart
items.description: Spit teeth at your enemies.

items.name: Dart/DST
items.description: Spit teeth at your enemies.

items.name: Darts
items.description: Darts are an item added to The Forge in Don't Starve Together. Available immediately from characters such as Willow, Wilson, Wendy, Wes, and Webber.
items.beginnerTip: Fires off 8 darts in rapid succession.

items.name: Dead Jellyfish
items.description: Dead Jellyfish are a fish food item in the Shipwrecked DLC. Dead Jellyfish can be obtained by murdering Jellyfish. Both Dead Jellyfish and Cooked Jellyfish can be used in the Crock Pot and count as a berry.

items.name: Dead Rainbow Jellyfish
items.description: Dead Rainbow Jellyfish is a Fish Food Item introduced in the Shipwrecked DLC. It can be obtained by murdering Rainbow Jellyfish. It can be dried on a Drying Rack to obtain Dried Jellyfish. It can be used in Crock Pot, and counts for 1 Fish value and 1 Monster value. Eating a Dead Rainbow Jellyfish will make the character glow and give off colored light similar to that of a Rainbow Jellyfish. This glowing effect becomes visibly weaker as time goes on, and only lasts around 2 minutes. __NOTOC__

items.name: Debris
items.description: Debris are naturally spawning objects in the Shipwrecked DLC. They mark the player's spawn point and may be meant to infer the player has shipwrecked on their starting island. There are four different pieces: Two planks, a box, and a large broken mast.

items.name: Deciduous Turf
items.description: A chunk of deciduous forest floor.

items.name: Deciduous Turf/DST
items.description: A chunk of deciduous forest floor.

items.name: Deck Illuminator
items.description: The Deck Illuminator is a craftable Item exclusive to Don't Starve Together introduced in Return of Them. It is found in the Seafaring Filter and requires 1 set of Boards, 2 Ropes and 4 Flint to craft, and a Think Tank to prototype.

items.name: Decked-Out Dragonfly Boat Kit
items.description: Equipped with all the draconic fixings.

items.name: Deconstruction Staff
items.description: Clean and efficient destruction.
items.beginnerTip: Perfectly deconstruct nearly any craftable.

items.name: Deconstruction Staff/DST
items.description: Clean and efficient destruction.
items.beginnerTip: Perfectly deconstruct nearly any craftable.

items.name: Deed of Home Ownership
items.description: The Deed of home ownership is a purchasable Item exclusive to the Hamlet DLC. It can be purchased at the Swinesbury City Hall for 50 Oincs, making the Slanty Shanty available to access by the player. The Deed of home ownership can be read to reveal the Slanty Shanty's location on the Map.
items.beginnerTip: Grants access to the Slanty Shanty.

items.name: Deerclops Eyeball
items.description: Deerclops Eyeball is a food item dropped by the Deerclops. It is similar to a Guardian Horn. Both are dropped by a boss, unable to spoil, and restore health and hunger but decrease sanity.

items.name: Deerclops Eyeball/DST
items.description: Deerclops Eyeball is a food item dropped by the Deerclops. It is similar to a Guardian Horn. Both are dropped by a boss, unable to spoil, and restore health and hunger but decrease sanity.

items.name: Deflated Balloon
items.description: The Deflated Balloon is a naturally spawning structure found in Hamlet-compatible worlds. Only one spawns per world, and it can be Hammered to yield two Cut Grass and two Rope. It always spawns next to a Wicker Basket which has its own Map icon, allowing it to be easily found later.

items.name: Demolition Permit
items.description: Destroy that den you've always talked about.
items.beginnerTip: Allows the removal of a room in the Slanty Shanty.

items.name: Dense Turf
items.description: As tame as wild jungle can be.

items.name: Desert Stone
items.description: Desert Stones are Items exclusive to Don't Starve Together, introduced in A New Reign. They are given by the Antlion in exchange for Trinkets and Eggs and can be used to craft The Lazy Deserter and the Turf-Raiser Helm.

items.name: Dirt
items.description: Dirt - is a type of surface that can be founded under any type of Turf. You can't use Pitchfork on it. When you use Pitchfork on majority surface, it will drop Turf as an item and there will appear dirt surface instand. Dirt surface can be replaced by any Turf item.
items.beginnerTip: can be replaced by Turfs

items.name: Dirt/DST
items.description: Dirt - is a type of surface that can be found under any type of Turf. You can't use a Pitchfork on it. When you use Pitchforks on the majority of surfaces, they will drop a kind of Turf as an item and Dirt will appear under it instead. Dirt can be replaced by any Turf item. It also can be found near Sinkholes.
items.beginnerTip: can be replaced by any Turf

items.name: Disarming Tools
items.description: It's disarming.
items.beginnerTip: Disarms traps.

items.name: Divining Rod
items.description: There must be some way out of here...
items.beginnerTip: Helps locate Things and Maxwell's Door

items.name: Dock Kit
items.description: Get ready for your pier review.

items.name: Dogfish
items.description: Dogfish are passive Mobs found in the Shipwrecked DLC. They can be seen across the Ocean on their own, or in abundance in Coral Reefs. When the player's boat approaches a Dogfish's shadow, it will surface and attempt to swim away, before retreating to the water once more. Dogfishes are only spawned at world creation time, and they do not respawn once killed, making them a limited resource. They are considered innocent creatures, and killing one adds 2 points to the player's Naughtiness level, which can cause Krampus to appear.

items.name: Dorsal Fin
items.description: The Dorsal Fin is an Item introduced in the Shipwrecked DLC. It is dropped by killed Bottlenose Ballphins and can be used to craft Ballphin Palaces. Unlike Shark Fins, Dorsal Fins are not edible to the player. They can be used as a filler in the Crock Pot, falling under the same category as Twigs.

items.name: Down Feather
items.description: A Down Feather is an Item from the Reign of Giants DLC. It is dropped by both the Moose/Goose and her Moslings. Its only purpose is to craft a Luxury Fan or a Weather Pain.

items.name: Down Feather/DST
items.description: A Down Feather is an Item dropped by both the Moose/Goose and her Moslings. Its main purpose is to craft a Luxury Fan or a Weather Pain.

items.name: Doydoy
items.description: A Doydoy is a passive Mob in Don't Starve: Shipwrecked. It is a large blue and green colored bird that drops Meat, Drumsticks, and Doydoy Feathers when killed.

items.name: Doydoy Egg
items.description: A Doydoy Egg is a large spotted blue-green egg. They can be found by picking Doydoy Nests, which are spawned when Doydoys mate. Unlike Tallbirds, Doydoys will not chase the player if their egg is stolen. Doydoy Eggs will hatch into Baby Doydoys only when they are in a Doydoy Nest, and unlike Tallbird Eggs they cannot be made to hatch around Campfire. However, placing them in empty Nests allows them to hatch.

items.name: Doydoy Feather
items.description: The Doydoy Feather is an Item in the Shipwrecked DLC. It is dropped when Doydoys are killed or when a Doydoy Nest is Hammered. There is also a 20% chance for a Doydoy Feather to drop when Doydoys mate. The feather can be used to craft the Tropical Fan, Feather Lite Sail, and Doydoy Nest.

items.name: Doydoy Nest
items.description: Just doy it.
items.beginnerTip: Hatches Doydoy Eggs.

items.name: Dragon Fruit
items.description: A Dragon Fruit is a rare Fruit that has a 5% chance to be grown from Farm plots by planting Seeds (or 4.75% Reign of Giants or 3.7% Shipwrecked). Dragon Fruits can also be produced by feeding a caged Bird a Dragon Fruit to receive 1-2 Dragon Fruit Seeds and a 50% chance to get a generic seed.

items.name: Dragon Fruit/DST
items.description: A Dragon Fruit is a rare Fruit that has low chance to be grown from Farm Soils by planting Seeds.

items.name: Dragonfly
items.description: Dragonfly is one of the four Giants in the Reign of Giants DLC, representing the season of Summer. She is a large monster with both reptilian and insectoid traits. When killed, Dragonfly will drop Scales and 8 Meat.

items.name: Dragonfly Light
items.description: An illuminating mast attachment.
items.beginnerTip: Can be placed on a Mast. Emits Light.

items.name: Dragonfly/DST
items.description: Dragonfly is a boss monster in Don't Starve Together. Unlike in the Reign of Giants DLC, Dragonfly does not represent the Summer season and is instead present year-round at the Dragonfly Nest in the Badland Desert. Upon death, she will also drop all types of Gems, Gold Nuggets, up to one Lavae Egg, a rare Blueprint for the Scaled Furnace, and a Sketch for a Dragonfly Figure in addition to Meat and Scales.

items.name: Dragonpie
items.description: Dragonpie is a Fruit Food item cooked in the Crock Pot by using 1 Dragon Fruit and other fillers. It takes 40 seconds to cook.

items.name: Dragonpie/DST
items.description: Dragonpie is a Veggie Food item cooked in the Crock Pot by using 1 Dragon Fruit and other fillers. It takes 40 seconds to cook.

items.name: Dragoon Den
items.description: Enter the Dragoon's Den.

items.name: Dragoon Egg
items.description: Dragoon Eggs are the meteors that fall from the sky when Volcanic Eruption occurs during the Dry Season, if the Volcano Staff is used in the Shipwrecked DLC, or if Wickerbottom uses Joy of Volcanology.

items.name: Dragoon Heart
items.description: Dragoon Hearts are Meat Food Items introduced in the Shipwrecked DLC. They are obtained by killing Dragoons or by destroying Dragoon Dens. They can be used to craft Dragoon Dens and Volcanic Tab items. When eaten, they will restore 11 Health and 25 Hunger at the cost of 10 Sanity. Eating them causes the consumer to glow for 90 seconds, similar to the effect of the Glow Berry. This applies both to the player and to Mobs such as Wildbores. Dragoon Hearts cannot be used for cooking in a Crock Pot. When on the ground, they will produce enough light to ward off Charlie.

items.name: Dreaded Mudslinger
items.description: Bring home turf advantage to any fight, along with some writhing reinforcements.

items.name: Driftwood Piece
items.description: Driftwood Pieces are Items exclusive to Don't Starve Together, introduced in Return of Them.

items.name: Dripple Pipes
items.description: Make the world weep.
items.beginnerTip: Starts Rain.

items.name: Drumstick
items.description: A Drumstick is a Meat Food Item dropped when a Gobbler or Pengull is killed. Two raw drumsticks can be added to a Crock Pot along with another piece of meat, and 1 Fruit or Vegetable to produce a Turkey Dinner. A drumstick can also be used as a meat filler for other recipes, or dried on a Drying Rack for 1 day to produce a Small Jerky. Like other meats, a drumstick can be given to a Pig to have them follow the player, or to the Pig King in exchange for a Gold Nugget.

items.name: Drumstick/DST
items.description: A Drumstick is a Meat Food Item dropped when a Gobbler or Pengull is killed. Two raw drumsticks can be added to a Crock Pot along with another piece of meat, and 1 Fruit or Vegetable to produce a Turkey Dinner. A drumstick can also be used as a meat filler for other recipes, or dried on a Drying Rack for 1 day to produce a Small Jerky. Like other meats, a drumstick can be given to a Pig to have them follow the player, or to the Pig King in exchange for a Gold Nugget.

items.name: Drying Rack
items.description: The jerkiest of racks.
items.beginnerTip: Dry Food items.

items.name: Drying Rack/DST
items.description: The jerkiest of racks.
items.beginnerTip: Dry Food items.

items.name: Dubloons
items.description: Dubloons are an Item in the Shipwrecked DLC. They are randomly left behind by Parrot Pirates (similarly to Seeds left by normal Birds) or obtained from giving Trinkets or Fishes to Yaarctopus. The loot from the X Marks the Spot treasure chests also have a chance to include Dubloons. Using a Trawl Net may yield Dubloons, although in Mild Season and Monsoon Season Dubloons can only be caught in Medium and Deep Ocean. The Booty Bag will also periodically drop Dubloons while equipped and the Slot Machine has a chance to drop them.

items.name: Dumbrella
items.description: Definitely function over fashion.
items.beginnerTip: Delays overheating in Dry Season. Protects from Rain and Lightning. Protects from Jellyfish electrocution.

items.name: Dung Pile
items.description: A Dung Pile is a naturally spawning object introduced in the Hamlet DLC, which can mostly be found in Tall Grass biome.

items.name: Durability
items.description: Durability is a game-concept which limits the amount of usage an item or structure has. It generally applies to items which can be equipped, however there are some other items such as the Sewing Kit or Pan Flute which also have it. An item with durability can be identified by a percentage number in front of its inventory graphic. For example, an Axe will have a 100% over its icon when first created, and this number will change as the Axe is used. Different items use durability in different ways:

items.name: Durian
items.description: A Durian is a rare fruit food item. It can be cooked on a fire into an Extra Smelly Durian, and also used as an ingredient in Crock Pot recipes. Durians can be farmed from Farm Plots. Regular Seeds have a 5% chance of growing Durians. Durian Seeds can be gained by feeding a Durian to Birds in a Birdcage, which can produce 1–2 Durian Seeds as well as a 50% chance to get normal Seeds.

items.name: Durian/DST
items.description: A Durian is a rare fruit food item. It can be cooked on a fire into an Extra Smelly Durian, and also used as an ingredient in Crock Pot recipes. Durians can be grown using Farm Soil with Brittle Seed Pods or with regular Seeds (5% chance). Feeding a Durian to a Bird in a Birdcage produces 1 Brittle Seed Pods.

items.name: Eel
items.description: Eel is a Meat food item similar to Fish and can be fished in Wilds Ponds found in the Ruins and Ponds in the Toadstool setpiece. Drying an Eel on a Drying Rack will produce Small Jerky. It can also be used to replace Fish as a prerequisite in Crock Pot recipes.

items.name: Eel/DST
items.description: Live Eel is a Meat food item and can be caught from Cave Pond in the Ruins and Ponds in the Toadstool setpiece. Eels can be placed in Crock Pot for making Dishes, such as Seafood Gumbo and Unagi.

items.name: Egg
items.description: An Egg is a Food Item obtained by feeding an "Imprisoned" Bird any type of Meat, Fish or meat food item (except raw Monster Meat, with the exception of Don't Starve Together). Eggs can also be found at Pengull nesting areas. In the Shipwrecked DLC, Eggs can also be occasionally found when chopping down Jungle Trees. In the Hamlet DLC, Eggs can also be occasionally found when chopping down Rainforest Trees.

items.name: Egg/DST
items.description: An Egg is a Food Item obtained by feeding an Imprisoned Bird any type of Meat, Fish, Koalefant Trunks or meat food item. Eggs can also be found at Pengull nesting areas.

items.name: Eggplant
items.description: An Eggplant is an uncommon Vegetable that can be farmed from Basic Farms and Improved Farms by planting Seeds for a 11% chance of growing or using Eggplant Seeds (Swirly Seeds). It can be used as an ingredient in several Crock Pot recipes. Feeding an Eggplant to a bird in a Birdcage will produce 1–2 Eggplant Seeds, as well as a 50% chance to get a plain seed. In Don't Starve Together, you will always get 1 Eggplant Seed.

items.name: Eggplant/DST
items.description: An Eggplant is an uncommon Vegetable that can be farmed by planting Seeds for a 11% chance of growing or using Swirly Seeds. It can be used as an ingredient in several Crock Pot recipes. Feeding an Eggplant to a bird in a Birdcage will produce 1 Swirly Seeds.

items.name: Eggs
items.description: There are 2 basic Egg food items in-game, each with a cooked version. (There is one additional Egg item in the Shipwrecked 24px|link=Shipwrecked DLC.)

items.name: Electric Milk
items.description: Electric Milk is a Dairy Food item from the Reign of Giants DLC. It is dropped by killing a Volt Goat that has been charged, i.e. struck by Lightning, or attacked with a Morning Star or an Electric Dart. Electric Milk can be consumed as it is, or used as an ingredient for recipes in the Crock Pot, such as Ice Cream.

items.name: Electric Milk/DST
items.description: Electric Milk is a Dairy Food item. It is dropped by killing a Volt Goat that has been charged, i.e. struck by Lightning, or attacked with a Morning Star or an Electric Dart. Electric Milk can be consumed as is, or used as an ingredient in the Crock Pot for recipes such as Ice Cream.

items.name: Electrical Doodad
items.description: Science away! Bzzzt!

items.name: Electrical Doodad/DST
items.description: Science away! Bzzzt!

items.name: Elephant Cactus
items.description: Active=

items.name: Embalming Spritz
items.description: A petrifying preserver of plant life.

items.name: Empty Bottle
items.description: Don't forget to recycle!

items.name: Empty Bottle/DST
items.description: The Empty Bottle is an item in Don't Starve Together, introduced in Return of Them. One Empty Bottle is obtained after reading a Message in a Bottle.

items.name: Encrusted Boat
items.description: A tank on high seas!
items.beginnerTip: Sailing Speed: 4

items.name: Endothermic Fire
items.description: This fire is from opposite day.
items.beginnerTip: Provides light. Cools the player.

items.name: Endothermic Fire/DST
items.description: This fire is from opposite day.
items.beginnerTip: Provides light. Cools the player.

items.name: Enlightened Crown
items.description: The Enlightened Crown is an item exclusive to Don't Starve Together, introduced in Return of Them. It is dropped by the Celestial Champion. If a Deconstruction Staff is used to break this item, it will drop five Enlightened Shards.
items.beginnerTip: Restores Sanity over time. Provides light while worn (while Sanity is above 85%). Summons Minor Gestalts on hit at cost of 1 Sanity per hit (while Sanity is above 85%). Prevent natural Gestalt from attacking wearer.

items.name: Evergreen
items.description: Evergreens are Plants generated randomly with each new map and can be naturally found anywhere except in Rockyland or Savanna Biomes (although they may still be planted there). Evergreens are most commonly found in Forests and Grasslands.

items.name: Evergreen/DST
items.description: Evergreens are Plants generated randomly with each new map and can be naturally found anywhere except in Rockyland or Savanna Biomes (although they may still be planted there). Evergreens are most commonly found in Forests and Grasslands.

items.name: Executive Hammer
items.description: The Executive Hammer is an Item exclusive to the Hamlet DLC. It can be acquired by opening the respective Royal Gallery Exhibit with a Royal Gallery Key in the Pig Queen Palace. The Executive Hammer can be used to permanently destroy Town Houses, Pig Shops, Watch Towers, Lawn Decorations, Intricate Topiaries and Hedges as opposed to reducing them to a repairable pile of rubble with the Hammer. Destroying a Town House, Pig Shop or Watch Tower will drop half the resources required to build the object in the City Planning Tab, however any nearby Royal Guards will become hostile to the player.
items.beginnerTip: Destroys City Planning Tab structures.

items.name: Extra-Adorable Lavae
items.description: The Extra-Adorable Lavae is a follower exclusive to Don't Starve Together. She has 250 health and can be hatched from the Lavae Egg. The Lavae will follow the tooth that dropped from the same egg as she spawned from. She will provide light, heat and allows food to be cooked on her body, like a Campfire and Dwarf Star. The Extra-Adorable Lavae is smaller than the hostile Lavae, allowing them to be distinguished a little easier. Extra-Adorable Lavae is immune to fire.

items.name: Eye Bone
items.description: thumb|200px|Eye Bone as found naturally in the world
items.beginnerTip: Spawns

items.name: Eye Bone/DST
items.description: thumb|200px|Eye Bone as found naturally in the world
items.beginnerTip: Spawns

items.name: Eye Mask
items.description: The Eye Mask is a wearable head slot Armor exclusive to Don't Starve Together and introduced in the An Eye for An Eye update. It's dropped from the Eye of Terror upon death.
items.beginnerTip: Absorbs 80% of physical damage. Feed food to repair.

items.name: Eye of the Tiger Shark
items.description: The Eye of the Tiger Shark is a Food Item introduced in the Shipwrecked DLC. It is dropped by the Tiger Shark and can be used to craft the Super Spyglass. When eaten, it will restore 60 Health, and 75 hunger at the cost of 15 Sanity. It is considered Meat, therefore if left on the ground, nearby Wildbores, Spiders and Snakes will be attracted to it and will eat it.

items.name: Eyebrella
items.description: An eye on the sky keeps you dry.
items.beginnerTip: Delays overheating in Summer. Protects from rain and lightning.

items.name: Eyebrella/DST
items.description: An eye on the sky keeps you dry.
items.beginnerTip: Delays overheating in Summer. Protects from rain and lightning.

items.name: Eyeshot
items.description: The Eyeshot is a ranged weapon exclusive to the Shipwrecked DLC. It is dropped by Flups and is similar to a Blow Dart, except that it only deals 20 damage instead of 100 for characters with no damage modifiers. Since the damage is lower than a Bird's health, birds will be stunned when hit with an Eyeshot, making it useful for capturing birds if one lacks a Bird Trap or the materials for one. Each Eyeshot can be used only once.

items.name: Fancy Helmet
items.description: Strong, sturdy and classy.
items.beginnerTip: Slows down player by 10%.

items.name: Fancy Spiralled Tubers
items.description: Fancy Spiralled Tubers are Vegetable Food Items exclusive to Don't Starve Together. They are cooked in the Crock Pot by combining 1 Potato, Twigs and two fillers. It takes 15 seconds to cook.

items.name: Farm
items.description: Grows seeds.
items.beginnerTip: Allows the planting and growing of Seeds.

items.name: Farm Soil
items.description: Farm Soil is an object exclusive to Don't Starve Together, introduced in the Return of Them update.
items.beginnerTip: Support for farming

items.name: Farming
items.description: thumb|330px|Wilson with 6 Improved Farms

items.name: Farming/DST
items.description: Farming is the process of growing Farm Plants that provide Food in the form of Vegetables, Fruits, and to some extent Crop Seeds. Weeds can also grow.

items.name: Fashion Melon
items.description: Refreshing, but sticky.
items.beginnerTip: Lowers sanity over time. Increases wetness over time. Delays overheating in Summer or Dry Season.

items.name: Fashion Melon/DST
items.description: Refreshing, but sticky.
items.beginnerTip: Lowers sanity over time. Increases wetness over time. Delays overheating in Summer.

items.name: Feather
items.description: Feathers are Items obtained by killing Birds. There are three feather types; Jet Feather, Crimson Feather, and Azure Feather. They can be obtained by killing birds by weapons or by "Murdering" them in the inventory after capturing them alive. Each bird has a 50% chance to drop its feather, excluding Pengulls, which have only a 20% chance of dropping theirs.

items.name: Feather Hat
items.description: Dress for your head.
items.beginnerTip: Restores sanity over time. Increases Bird spawn rate. Decreases Bird spawn delay.

items.name: Feather/DST
items.description: Feathers are Items obtained by killing Birds. There are four feather types; Jet Feather, Crimson Feather, Azure Feather, and Saffron Feather. They can be obtained by killing birds by weapons or by "Murdering" them in the inventory after capturing them alive. Each bird has a 50% chance to drop its feather, excluding Pengulls, which have only a 20% chance of dropping theirs.

items.name: Feathered Wreath
items.description: The Feathered Wreath is an item added to The Forge in Don't Starve Together.

items.name: Feijoada
items.description: Feijoada (pronounced /fejʒuˈadɐ/ or "feyzhu-A-da") is a Meat Food Item exclusive to the Hamlet DLC. It is cooked in the Crock Pot by using 3 Bean Bugs and a Meat item. Feijoada does not require Meat if at least one of the Bean Bugs has been cooked.

items.name: Fencing Sword
items.description: A sword, used for fencing

items.name: Fire
items.description: thumb|300px

items.name: Fire Pump
items.description: Water, water everywhere!
items.beginnerTip: Can be placed as a Structure.

items.name: Fire Staff
items.description: Harness the power of combustion!
items.beginnerTip: Ignites mobs and flammable objects.

items.name: Fire Staff/DST
items.description: Harness the power of combustion!
items.beginnerTip: Ignites mobs and flammable objects.

items.name: Fireflies
items.description: Fireflies are passive light-producing Mobs that appear at night in Forest and Grassland Biomes and all the time in Caves, mainly in Mushtree Forests. They are used to make the Miner Hat and Pumpkin Lantern. Fireflies can also be used to refuel Miner Hats and Lanterns by 39%.
items.beginnerTip: Can be released to emit light.

items.name: Fireflies/DST
items.description: Fireflies are passive light-producing Mobs that appear at night in Forest and Grassland Biomes and all the time in Caves, mainly in Mushtree Forests. They are used to make the Miner Hat and Pumpkin Lantern. Fireflies can also be used to refuel Miner Hats and Lanterns by 39%.
items.beginnerTip: Can be released to emit light.

items.name: Fish
items.description: Fish is a Meat Food Item that typically comes from Ponds. It is also dropped by Merms. It restores 12.5 Hunger and stacks to 40 in the inventory. Fish can be dried on the Drying Rack for 1 day to produce Small Jerky, and are the main ingredient in Fishsticks and Fish Tacos using a Crock Pot. Fishing (like killing Gobblers) does not increase the player's Naughtiness level, meaning it is a safe food source for those fearing Krampus.

items.name: Fish Cordon Bleu
items.description: Fish Cordon Bleu is a Warly-specific Meat Food Item cooked in the Portable Crock Pot, exclusive to Don't Starve Together. It requires two Frog Legs and Fishes with a total Fish value of 1.0 or higher, and takes 40 seconds to cook. Fillers cannot be Inedible.
items.beginnerTip: Makes the player immune to Wetness for the duration of 5 min.

items.name: Fish Morsel
items.description: A Fish Morsel is a Food Item included in the Shipwrecked DLC.

items.name: Fish Morsel/DST
items.description: A Fish Morsel was introduced to Don't Starve Together in Return of Them. It is dropped by Fish, Runty Guppy, Needlenosed Squirt, Bitty Baitfish, Smolt Fry, Scorching Sunfish, Spittlefish and Crustashine when killed.

items.name: Fish Tacos
items.description: Fish Tacos is a Meat Food item made in the Crock Pot by combining 1 Corn and 1 Fishes. It takes 10 seconds to cook.

items.name: Fish Tacos/DST
items.description: Fish Tacos is a Meat Food item made in the Crock Pot by combining 1 Corn and 0.25 Fishes. It takes 10 seconds to cook.

items.name: Fishbone
items.description: The Fishbone is a naturally spawning Item and the Shipwrecked DLC's counterpart to the Eye Bone. When it is picked up, it will summon Packim Baggims, the Shipwrecked version of Chester and Ro Bin. The Fishbone can spawn on any island, except the starting island. If Packim Baggims is killed, the Fishbone will take on a gray appearance.
items.beginnerTip: Spawns

items.name: Fishermerm's Hut
items.description: Fishermerm's Huts are naturally spawning Structures in Marsh Biomes in the Shipwrecked DLC. They spawn and shelter Fishermerms, and up to 2 Fishermerms can inhabit 1 hut. Fishermerms are active during Dusk and Night. If a Fishermerm living in a hut dies, a new one will spawn after 4 days from the hut. If hammered, the hut will drop 1 bundle of Boards, 1 pile Rocks, and 1 Tropical Fish.

items.name: Fishes
items.description: There are 2 basic Fish Food Items in Don't Starve; Fish and Eel (There are 16 additional types in the Shipwrecked DLC and 13 additional types in Don't Starve Together). Fish can be obtained by Fishing in Ponds on either the Surface World or the Caves, and as a drop from Merms / Merm Heads. Eels, however, can only be fished from Ponds found in the Ruins. Both types of Fish are a subtype of Meat, and as such, can be used as Meat fillers in the Crock Pot and be eaten by Wigfrid. In Don't Starve Together Ocean Fishes can be fished from the Ocean with the Sea Fishing Rod.

items.name: Fishing Rod
items.description: Go fishing. For fish.
items.beginnerTip: Allows the player to catch Fish and Trinkets.

items.name: Fishsticks
items.description: Fishsticks is a Meat Food item cooked in the Crock Pot by combining 1 Fishes and exactly 1 Twig. It takes 40 seconds to cook.

items.name: Fishsticks/DST
items.description: Fishsticks is a Meat Food item cooked in the Crock Pot by combining at least 0.25 value of Fishes and exactly 1 Twig. It takes 40 seconds to cook.

items.name: Fist Full of Jam
items.description: Fist Full of Jam is a Fruit Food Item cooked in a Crock Pot by adding any Fruits except Dragon Fruit, which will lead to a Dragonpie instead. However, adding more than 2.5 units of Fruits may result in Fruit Medley instead. It takes 10 seconds to cook.

items.name: Fist Full of Jam/DST
items.description: Fist Full of Jam is a Fruit Food Item cooked in a Crock Pot by adding any Fruits except Dragon Fruit, which will lead to a Dragonpie instead. However, adding more than 2.5 units of Fruits may result in Fruit Medley instead. It takes 10 seconds to cook.

items.name: Flare
items.description: Light the way for your trusted friends.
items.beginnerTip: Creates a temporary marking on the Map that is visible to all players.

items.name: Flat Stone Turf
items.description: The foundation of a solid village.

items.name: Fleshy Bulb
items.description: A Fleshy Bulb is an item dropped by Lureplants when killed. When planted by the player, it will spawn a new Lureplant. If the newly spawned Lureplant is killed, it will also drop a Fleshy Bulb. Despite being plant material, Fleshy Bulbs cannot be eaten and do not spoil.

items.name: Fleshy Bulb/DST
items.description: Costs an arm, but not a leg.

items.name: Flint
items.description: Flint is an item used to craft basic tools. It can be found on the ground or by mining smooth or gold veined Boulders with the Pickaxe. Flint is not flammable and easy to find on the surface, although eventually it can be used up. More can be found by venturing into a Cave, however.

items.name: Flint/DST
items.description: Flint is an item used to craft basic tools. It can be found on the ground or by mining smooth or gold veined Boulders with the Pickaxe. Flint is one of the first and most needed items in the game and should be sought after as soon as a new game starts. It is recommended to always have a decent number of Flint at all times in the case the player needs to make basic Tools such as an Axe or a Pickaxe. Combat wise, the Spear can be built.

items.name: Floaty Boaty Knight
items.description: The Floaty Boaty Knight is a hostile Mob in the Shipwrecked DLC.

items.name: Floor
items.description: No summary is available; see the linked wiki page.

items.name: Floral Shirt
items.description: Fun in the sun. Or on Casual Fridays.
items.beginnerTip: Delays overheating in Summer/Dry Season. Raises sanity over time.

items.name: Floral Shirt/DST
items.description: Fun in the sun. Or on Casual Fridays.
items.beginnerTip: Delays overheating in Summer/Dry Season. Raises sanity over time.

items.name: Flour
items.description: Ground wheat.

items.name: Flower
items.description: Flowers are the good version of Evil Flowers, found in Grasslands, Forests, or Savanna biomes. They cannot be found in Marshes or Rockyland. When picked, they restore 5 Sanity and produce Petals, which, when eaten, restore 1 Health. There are 10 different kinds of Flowers, but they all have the same effect.

items.name: Flower Headband
items.description: The Flower Headband is an item added to The Forge in Don't Starve Together.

items.name: Flower Salad
items.description: The Flower Salad is a Vegetable Food item introduced in the Reign of Giants DLC. It is cooked in the Crock Pot by combining 1 Cactus Flower and 2.0 units of Vegetables, with Cactus Flowers contributing to Flower Salad's Vegetable condition. It takes 10 seconds to cook.

items.name: Flower Salad/DST
items.description: The Flower Salad is a Vegetable Food item introduced in the Reign of Giants DLC. It is cooked in the Crock Pot by combining 1 Cactus Flower and 2.0 units of Vegetables, with Cactus Flowers contributing to Flower Salad's Vegetable condition. It takes 10 seconds to cook.

items.name: Flower/DST
items.description: Flowers are found in Grasslands, Forests, or Savanna biomes. They cannot be found in Marshes or Rockyland. When picked, they restore 5 Sanity and produce Petals, which, when eaten, restore 1 Health. There are 10 different kinds of Flowers, but they all have the same effect.

items.name: Flytrap Stalk
items.description: The Flytrap Stalk is a Food Item exclusive to the Hamlet DLC. It is dropped only by fully grown Snaptooth Flytraps and when consumed, restores 12.5 Hunger and depletes the player's Sanity by 10. Flytrap Stalks cannot be cooked or used in the Crock Pot, but can be dried on a Drying Rack to turn them into Stalking Sticks (the Hamlet equivalent of the Walking Cane), or used to craft the Bug B'Gone repellent and the Root Trunk.
