items.name: Forge Portal
items.description: The Forge Portal is a Structure exclusive to The Forge event. It serves as an enemy spawner that generates the rounds in the challenge. Forge Portals cannot be blocked or destroyed by the players.
items.beginnerTip: Spawns enemy mobs.

items.name: Forging Hammer
items.description: The Forging Hammer is an item added to The Forge in Don't Starve Together. Available immediately from strength-based characters such as Wolfgang, WX-78, and Winona.
items.beginnerTip: User hits a spell-circle-sized area, stunning and doing 30 damage to anything inside. (Anvil Strike makes all hit mobs aggro on user. Classified as electric damage.)

items.name: Fossils
items.description: Fossil Fragments are Don't Starve Together exclusive items, introduced in A New Reign. They are dropped by Stalagmites at a 10% rate and by Spilagmites with 100% rate. They can also rarely drop from Boulderboughs when planted in certain Caves biomes, and have a small chance to be dropped from the Great Depths Worm.
items.beginnerTip: Can build an Odd Skeleton.

items.name: Fountain of Youth
items.description: The Fountain of Youth is a naturally-spawning object. It can be found on an isolated island, reachable only by going through ruins with an artichoke above the entrance. The Fountain can be interacted with to obtain Magic Water, but doing so will spawn the Pugalisk from the nearby Ominous Carving.

items.name: Fresh Fruit Crepes
items.description: Fresh Fruit Crepes is a Warly-specific Food Item cooked in the Portable Crock Pot by adding 1.5 units of Fruits, 1 Butter, and 1 Honey. It takes 40 seconds to cook and restores 60 , 150 , and 15 when eaten.

items.description: Go fishing. For fish.

In DST, RoG, and Shipwrecked, Fruit Medley decreases the perceived temperature by 1 degrees per second for 5 seconds.

items.name: Guides/Physical Damage Absorption
items.description: This guide will explain how the game calculates the amount of damage that is absorbed by the various types of armor, using an example. The percentage values wouldn't be added together, as that would actually give the player Health back when they were hit. Therefore, a 'Decision Tree' must be calculated. It should be noted that the order the armor is equipped will make a difference in which armor will lose the most Durability first. Whatever item is equipped last will be the item to take the most significant chunk of the damage as it is utilized first in the damage calculation (see the scenario at the bottom for a sample situation).

items.description: The Gunpowder Barrel is a naturally spawning object introduced in the Shipwrecked DLC. They can occasionally be found in the Ocean biome. Attacking them will cause them to ignite. The barrels explode 3 to 6 seconds after being ignited. The explosion deals 400 fire damage to the player and Mobs if they are within 6 range (1.5 tiles), and creates Big Waves.

items.description: A handful of gunpowder.

items.name: Hail
items.description: Hail is an Item in the Shipwrecked DLC. It falls from storms during the Hurricane Season. It can be made into Ice to restore hunger and health. It must be turned in to Ice in order to be used in a crafting or Crock Pot recipe.

items.name: Halberd

items.name: Hard Shell Tacos
items.description: Hard Shell Tacos is a Crock Pot dish introduced in the Hamlet DLC. It requires exactly two Weevole Carapaces and one Vegetable.

items.name: Harp Statue
items.description: The Harp Statue is a Structure that can be mined with a Pickaxe for 2-3 Marble. It looks like a headless angel with a harp in its hands.

items.name: Harpoon
items.description: The Harpoon is a ranged Weapon in the Shipwrecked DLC. It can be obtained from an exploding White Whale Carcass or can be found in X Marks the Spot treasure chests. When this weapon is used to attack, it will be thrown by the player and deal 200 damage upon hitting the target. The Harpoon will land next to its target and can be picked up. __NOTOC__
items.beginnerTip: Throw-able, can be picked back up

items.name: Hay Wall
items.description: The Hay Wall is the weakest of the four Walls, a craftable Item and a deployable Structure that prevents the player's and Mobs' movement. Once built, it can be repaired or upgraded to a second tier with another piece of Hay Wall or enough Cut Grass. It can be attacked and destroyed, leaving a destroyed Hay Wall. Hammering the wall will yield two Cut Grass from the second tier and one Cut Grass from other tiers. It has a maximum of 100 health and 50 health when first built before upgrades. The Hay Wall is highly flammable and one should exercise caution when fighting Red Hounds near it, or during a Reign Of Giants Summer. If burned, they will drop one Ash.

items.name: Hay Wall/DST
items.description: The Hay Wall is the weakest of the four Walls, a craftable Item and a deployable Structure that prevents the player's and Mobs' movement. Once built, it can be repaired or upgraded to a second tier with another piece of Hay Wall or enough Cut Grass. It can be attacked and destroyed, leaving a destroyed Hay Wall. Hammering the wall will yield two Cut Grass from the second tier and one Cut Grass from other tiers. It has a maximum of 100 health and 50 health when first built before upgrades. The Hay Wall is highly flammable and one should exercise caution when fighting Red Hounds near it, or during Summer. If burned, they will drop one Ash. __NOTOC__

items.description: The Hippopotamoose Antler is a Hamlet exclusive Item dropped by the Hippopotamoose. It can be used to craft the Bird Whistle.

items.name: Hollow Stump
items.description: The Hollow Stump is a naturally-spawning object from the Reign of Giants DLC, found only in a Deciduous Forest Biome. It is a large stump with a hole, with yarn hanging from its branches and a ball of yarn on the side. It is the home of a Catcoon.

items.name: Hollow Stump/DST
items.description: The Hollow Stump is a naturally-spawning object from the Reign of Giants DLC, found only in a Deciduous Forest Biome. It is a large stump with a hole, with yarn hanging from its branches and a ball of yarn on the side. It is the home of a Catcoon. Spawned Catcoons wander within 7.5 tiles radius of their Hollow Stump.

items.name: Honey
items.description: Honey is a Sweetener Food item created by Bees. Honey may be obtained by killing a Bee or Killer Bee, by destroying a Beehive or Killer Bee Hive, or by harvesting a Bee Box. Honey provides 3 health points and 9 hunger points when consumed.

items.name: Honey Ham
items.description: Honey Ham is a Meat Food item produced in Crock Pot by combining more than 1.5 units of Meats and 1 Honey. It takes 40 seconds to cook. Honey Ham is a well-rounded food providing 30 (as much as a Honey Poultice) and 75 .

items.name: Honey Nuggets
items.description: Honey Nuggets is a Meat Food item cooked in the Crock Pot by combining 1 Honey and any Meats. However, adding more than 1.5 unit of Meats will result in Honey Ham instead. It takes 40 seconds to cook.

items.name: Honey Nuggets/DST

items.name: Horizon Expandinator
items.description: The Horizon Expandinator is an item that can be equipped to the head. It increases the radius of your vision and allows you to move the camera away from the player even further. At night, it will drain the player's sanity. It is dropped from the Scrappy Werepig.

items.name: Horn
items.description: A Horn is an Item introduced in the Shipwrecked DLC. It has a 33% chance to be dropped when a Water Beefalo is killed. It can be used to craft Horned Helmet and Dripple Pipes.

items.name: Horned Helmet
items.description: Shell out for some poison protection.|protection=85%
items.beginnerTip: Protects the player from getting poisoned by physical contact.

items.name: Hot Dragon Chili Salad
items.description: The Hot Dragon Chili Salad is a Don't Starve Together and Warly specific Food item cooked in the Portable Crock Pot by combining one Dragon Fruit, one Pepper, and two fillers.
items.beginnerTip: Increases temperature by 40 degrees for 5 minutes.

items.name: Hound
items.description: Hounds are Monsters that attack periodically in packs. They attack every 3–13 days and can also spawn from Hound Mounds. At least two Hounds will typically appear during an attack, which is signaled by growling noises heard for a short time. The player will also comment on the growling three times until it stops, and the Hounds attack. More Hounds will spawn at a time as the game progresses.

items.name: Hound Mound
items.description: Hound Mounds are naturally spawning objects formed in both Sandbox Mode and Adventure Mode, though it is more likely to be found in the latter. They house up to 3 Hounds which spawn in 5 second intervals until the mound is empty. Hounds that are killed will gradually regenerate at a rate of 1 every 30 seconds.

items.name: Hound Mound/DST
items.description: Hound Mounds are naturally spawning objects that can commonly be found in the Desert Biome, often in a cluster. They house 2 to 3 Hounds, which spawn in 30 second intervals until the mound is empty. Hounds that are killed will gradually regenerate at a rate of 1 every 3 minutes.

items.name: Hound/DST
items.description: Hounds are Monsters that periodically attack in packs. At least two Hounds will appear during an attack, which is signaled by growling noises heard for a short time. They can also spawn from Hound Mounds. If a player encounters a Varg, it will call two Hounds to help attack the player. Depending on the season, these Hounds can be normal, Blue Hounds and Red Hounds. If it was a Possessed Varg, the Hounds that were killed will transform into Horror Hounds.

items.name: Houndius Shootius
items.description: Keep the nasties away. By killing them.
items.beginnerTip: Can be placed as a Structure

items.name: Houndius Shootius/DST
items.description: Houndius Shootius is a craftable Item found in the Ancient Pseudoscience Filter. It requires 1 Guardian's Horn, 1 Deerclops Eyeball, and 5 Thulecite to craft, and can only be crafted near an Ancient Pseudoscience Station. Like all items from the Ancient Pseudoscience Filter, Houndius Shootius cannot be prototyped and Characters always need to be near an Ancient Pseudoscience Station to craft them again.

items.name: House Expansion Permit
items.description: Add that den you've always talked about.
items.beginnerTip: Allows the construction of an additional room in the Slanty Shanty.

items.name: Howling Conch
items.description: The gales come early.
items.beginnerTip: Starts Strong Winds. Starts Rain.

items.description: Ice Cream is a Food Item in the Reign of Giants DLC. It is cooked in a Crock Pot by combining 1 Ice, 1 Dairy product, and 1 Sweetener.
items.beginnerTip: Lowers temperature by 15 degrees over 15 seconds.

items.name: Ice Cream/DST
items.description: Ice Cream is a Food Item in the Don't Starve Together. It is cooked in a Crock Pot by combining 1 Ice, 1 Dairy product, and 1 Sweetener. No Meats, Vegetables, Eggs, or Inedibles can be added. Fruits are an acceptable filler.
items.beginnerTip: Lowers temperature by 15 degrees over 15 seconds.

items.name: Ice Cube
items.description: Science, on the rocks.
items.beginnerTip: Prevents overheating in Summer or Dry Season. Increases wetness over time. Walking speed reduced by 10%.

items.description: Science, on the rocks.
items.beginnerTip: Prevents overheating in Summer. Increases wetness over time. Walking speed reduced by 10%.

items.name: Ice Fishing Hole
items.description: The Ice Fishing Hole is a naturally spawning object exclusive to Don't Starve Together. It can be found on a Ice Sheet in the Rough Ocean. Unlike other fishing locations, while fishing with a Sea Fishing Rod at the Ice Fishing Hole, there is simply a 20% chance each second for the player to hook a Deep Bass. On the third fish caught, a Frostjaw spawns.
items.beginnerTip: Can be used to fish in with a Sea Fishing Rod.

items.name: Ice Flingomatic
items.description: Saves plants, puts out fires, fueled by flame.
items.beginnerTip: Extinguishes fires Revives withering plants

items.name: Ice Floe
items.description: The Ice Floe is a surface that makes up the Ice Sheet island and can be spawned during the battle with Crab King. As an icy surface the player is at risk of slipping and falling if any speed boosts are applied. Ice Floes will break after some time. When it will be destroyed depends on where the surface is located. If it is the naturally occurring Ice Sheet the surface will start slowly collapsing after defeating the Frostjaw starting from the edges. The Ice Floe will also grow on the island in winter, thereby creating an island with a diameter of 11 turf vertically/horizontally and 6 turf diagonally. In spring it will slowly collapse until an area of only 5 turf vertically/horizontally and 3 turf diagonally are left. If the surface was spawned by the Crab King it will last for a variable duration depending on how many Blue Gems have been inserted.
items.beginnerTip: Exists for some time before collapsing. After breaking, spawns

items.name: Iced Tea
items.description: Iced Tea is a Crock Pot dish introduced in the Hamlet DLC, produced by combining two Orange Pikos, a Sweetener, and Ice. It also can be obtained by cooking Tea in the Crock Pot, and waiting a Day for it to cool down.
items.beginnerTip: Grants a speed boost.

items.name: Infernal Staff
items.description: The Infernal Staff is an item added to The Forge event in Don't Starve Together. Dropped by the last enemy killed on wave 7.

items.name: Infroggles

items.beginnerTip: Grants Infrared Vision and removes blurriness.

items.name: Infused Iron
items.description: Infused Iron is a resource introduced in the Hamlet DLC. It is exclusively obtained from the Large Iron Hulk and used solely to craft the Living Artifact. Infused Iron spoils and will turn into regular Iron Ore after two days..

items.name: Infused Moon Shard
items.description: Infused Moon Shards are a resource exclusive to Don't Starve Together, introduced in Return of Them.

items.description: Small capacity, but keeps stuff fresh.

items.name: Inviting Formation
items.description: The Inviting Formations are naturally spawning objects exclusive to Don't Starve Together, introduced in Return of Them. One of each type will spawn on the Lunar Island in the Lunar Mine biome.

items.name: Iridescent Gem
items.description: The Iridescent Gem is a Don't Starve Together exclusive item, introduced in A New Reign. It can be acquired in three ways: by using a Deconstruction Staff on the Moon Caller's Staff, by picking them from the naturally-spawning Ornate Pedestals in the Ancient Archive biome, or by crafting it through Wilson's alchemy.

items.name: Iron Key
items.description: No summary is available; see the linked wiki page.

items.name: Iron Ore
items.description: Iron Ore is a resource exclusive to the Hamlet DLC. It can be found lying around in the Painted Biome and in Thunderbirds' Nests. It can also be obtained from mining Iron Hulks and Gnat Mounds which makes it renewable. Another way to obtain iron ore is through trawling in Hamlet Lilly Ponds (3.92% chance).

items.name: Iron Thing
items.description: The Iron Thing is one of the four Things in the Hamlet DLC. It is the Hamlet version of the Ring Thing.

items.name: Jelly Salad
items.description: Jelly Salad is a Crock Pot Food Item exclusive to Don't Starve Together. It is cooked by combining 2 Leafy Meat and a Sweetener value of at least 2.0. It takes 40 seconds to cook. It counts as a Meat item so Wigfrid will eat it, but Wurt will not.

items.name: Jelly-O Pop
items.description: Jelly-O Pop is a Crock Pot dish exclusive in the Shipwrecked DLC. It is made from any form of Jellyfish (Dead/Cooked Jellyfish and Dried Jellyfish), 1 Ice and 1 Inedible.
items.beginnerTip: Lowers temperature by 40 degrees for 10 seconds

items.name: Jellybeans
items.description: Jellybeans are a Crock Pot Food item exclusive to Don't Starve Together, introduced in A New Reign. They are produced by combining at least 1 Royal Jelly and 3 fillers, excluding Inedibles and Monster Foods (which will result in Taffy), and produce 3 Jellybeans.

items.name: Jellyfish
items.description: Jellyfish are passive Mobs found in the Shipwrecked DLC. They float around in the shallow Ocean, sometimes in groups. New ones will spawn every 60 seconds to replace those who are lost. They will not attack the player if they are approached, but if they are attacked with a melee Weapon, they will automatically shock the player, doing 5 points of Health damage. They will not actively attack the player. Once killed, their carcass will float in the water until picked up.

items.name: Juicy Berries
items.description: Juicy Berries are a Food Item exclusive to Don't Starve Together, they can be found on Juicy Berry Bushes. Harvesting a Juicy Berry Bush yields 3 Juicy Berries, which will fall to the ground instead and need to be picked up. __NOTOC__

items.name: Juicy Berry Bush
items.description: Juicy Berry Bushes are Plants exclusive to Don't Starve Together. They are a variant of Berry Bushes. When generating a new world, either all regular Berry Bushes (including those being part of Set Pieces) will be replaced by Juicy Berry Bushes, or no Juicy Berry Bushes will be present at start. The same applies to the Caves, though they do not have to share the same berry bush type as the surface world. They can also be spawned randomly on the Wilderness and Endless modes.

items.name: Jungle Burr
items.description: Jungle Burrs are seeds dropped by Rainforest Trees in the Hamlet DLC. They are only dropped during the Lush Season when the Rainforest Trees bloom and Strong Winds blow, or the trees are chopped down. Burrs can then be planted to grow into a new tree. They cannot be planted on Rocky Turf, Wooden Flooring, Stone Road Turf, Flat Stone Turf, Lawn Turf, and Cultivated Turf.
items.beginnerTip: Can be planted

items.name: Jungle Tree
items.description: Jungle Trees are a type of Tree found only in the Jungle biome in the Shipwrecked DLC. They are by far the largest trees. When chopped down they yield Logs and Jungle Tree Seeds. Chopping any size Jungle Tree has a 50% chance of trying to spawn Snakes. While there is a chance to get no snakes, a maximum of 1 to 3 Snakes can be spawned depending on the size of the Tree. After day 3 Poison Snakes can be encountered this way. If the medium-sized and fully grown Jungle Trees didn't try to spawn Snakes (even if no Snakes were actually spawned), they will spawn a food item. This food item for medium-sized Jungle Trees is always an Egg, while fully grown Jungle Trees drop either Eggs or Bananas with equal likelihood. Like most trees, the player may use a Shovel to dig up the stump to obtain an extra Log.

items.name: Jungle Tree Seed
items.description: Jungle Tree Seed is an Item dropped from Jungle trees in the Shipwrecked DLC. Jungle Tree Seeds can be planted to create Jungle Trees. They can also be used as a low-level Fuel item. Planted saplings will not appear on the Map until they have progressed into the small tree stage.
items.beginnerTip: Can be planted.

items.name: Jungle Turf
items.description: Jungle Turf is one of the Turf Items exclusive to the Shipwrecked DLC, acquired by digging Jungle tiles with a Pitchfork. Like other Turfs, it can be placed on any bare ground tile or used as fuel.

items.name: Kabobs
items.description: Kabobs is a Meat Food item cooked in the Crock Pot by adding 1 Meats and exactly 1 Twig. It takes 40 seconds to cook.

items.name: Kabobs/DST
items.description: Kabobs is a Meat Food item cooked in the Crock Pot by adding 1 Meats and exactly 1 Twig. It takes 40 seconds to cook. Adding more than 1 Monster Food or Twig will result in Wet Goop, while adding any Fishes will result in Fishsticks.

items.name: Kelp Fronds
items.description: Kelp Fronds are a Vegetable Food Item exclusive to Don't Starve Together, introduced in Return of Them. They are harvested from Bull Kelp plants (in the Ocean and in the Rocky Beach Biome) and from Ocean Debris. When eaten, they restore a bit of Hunger, but reduce both the player's Health and Sanity.

items.name: Key to the City
items.description: The Key to the City is an Item exclusive to the Hamlet DLC. It can be acquired by opening the respective Royal Gallery Exhibit with a Royal Gallery Key in the Pig Queen Palace. The Key to the City serves as a portable crafting station, unlocking the City Planning Tab when being held in the inventory or standing next to it. City Planning Tab is not accessible when one is in interior. Town Houses crafted with the Key to the City, will give 1 Oinc every 10 days, if My City Hall is built.
items.beginnerTip: Grants access to the City Planning Tab.

items.name: Kitchen sets
items.description: Everything you need to set up a cookpot.

items.name: Koalefant Trunk
items.description: A Koalefant Trunk is a Meat Food item dropped by Koalefants. It can be used to craft a Breezy Vest.

items.name: Koalefant Trunk/DST
items.description: A Koalefant Trunk is a Meat Food item dropped by Koalefants. It can be used to craft a Breezy Vest.

items.name: Krampus Sack
items.description: The Krampus Sack is a Backpack item. It is an extremely rare drop from Krampus, with only a 1% chance to drop from their small loot table.
items.beginnerTip: +14 inventory slots

items.name: Krampus Sack/DST
items.description: The Krampus Sack is a Backpack item. It is an extremely rare drop from Krampus, with only a 1% chance to drop from their small loot table. It also has a 10% chance to drop from bundled supplies received from Klaus's Loot Stash.
items.beginnerTip: +14 inventory slots

items.name: Krissure
items.description: Krissures are objects found in the Shipwrecked DLC. After a player has dug up a Magma Pile, a Krissure may appear and erupt. Krissures will alternate between dormant and erupting states. It can be used as a Light source, but it may burn if a player stands too close. Note that it's the initial burst of krissure that sets things on fire, not the lasting flame itself. The player can cook Food over an erupting Krissure. Flooded Krissures do not erupt. Krissures can be removed using coconades explosion .
items.beginnerTip: Produces Light and Heat.

items.name: Lamp
items.description: Lamps are structures exclusive to the Hamlet DLC. They can be found in many rooms within a Mant Hill. They provide light in otherwise dark rooms of the Mant Hill. Each Lamp provides a bit less light than that given off by a Miner Hat. Lamps can be mined for Honey, though they are not renewable.

items.name: Lantern
items.description: Refuelable, bright, portable.|dischargeRate=32px|link=Fuel#Light Bulb Fuel 7.8 min
items.beginnerTip: Provides light when carried or placed

items.name: Lantern/DST
items.description: Refuelable, bright, portable.|dischargeRate=32px|link=Fuel/DST#Light Bulb Fuel 7.8 min
items.beginnerTip: Provides light when carried or placed

items.name: Large Ornate Chest
items.description: A Large Ornate Chest spawns when the Ancient Guardian is killed. This chest contains substantially more loot than its smaller counterpart. Each item in the pool has a chance to appear individually.

items.name: Large Ornate Chest/DST
items.description: A Large Ornate Chest spawns when the Ancient Guardian is killed. This chest contains substantially more loot than its smaller counterpart. 7-9 of the items are guaranteed to be chosen. The Ancient Key is found in the Large Ornate Chest upon the first defeat only.

items.name: Lava Pool
items.description: Lava Pools are created when Dragoon Eggs hit land during Volcano eruptions in the Dry Season of the Shipwrecked DLC. They create light and heat while they are burning. They can ignite nearby objects and cause Overheating. They can also be used to cook Food items while they are burning. After burning 75% of the total dusk and night time, they will run out on their own. They cannot be refueled to make them last longer. If they are let to run out, they will drop 2 Rocks, 2 Ashes, and 1 Charcoal. Otherwise, they can be extinguished directly with Ice (but not Hail or other fire extinguishers), and will yield 1 Obsidian instead.

items.name: Lavae
items.description: The Lavae is a Mob exclusive to Don't Starve Together. It has 500 health and spawns from the Dragonfly. Anything that comes into direct contact with or is next to a Lavae will burst into flames, including the player. The Lavae is immune to fire.

items.name: Lavae Egg
items.description: The Lavae Egg is an Item exclusive to Don't Starve Together. It has a 33% chance of being dropped by a slain Dragonfly. It may also be acquired when opening a Loot Stash with Klaus' Stag Antler.
items.beginnerTip: Hatches into a Dragonfly Larva.

items.name: Lawn Turf
items.description: Fully tamed grass.

items.name: Leafy Meat
items.description: Raw= |-| Cooked= Leafy Meat is a meat food item obtained by harvesting a Lureplant. When a Lureplant has not devoured anything else, it will dangle this item to lure prey into its field of Eyeplants. If another Meat is eaten by the Eyeplants, then the Lureplant will dangle that instead.

items.name: Leafy Meat/DST
items.description: Leafy Meat is a meat food item obtained by harvesting a Lureplant. When a Lureplant has not devoured anything else, it will dangle this item to lure prey into its field of Eyeplants. If another Meat is eaten by the Eyeplants, then the Lureplant will dangle that instead.

items.name: Leafy Meatloaf
items.description: Leafy Meatloaf is a Crock Pot recipe exclusive to Don't Starve Together introduced in Return of Them. It's made of 2 Leafy Meat and any fillers. It was added in the Troubled Waters update, alongside other Leafy Meat and Barnacle based dishes.

items.name: Leaky Shack/DST
items.description: A Leaky Shack is a naturally occurring Structure found in a Marsh biome. It is similar to in appearance to a Pig House, but in a dilapidated state. Their main purpose is spawning and housing Merms. Leaky shacks can hold up to four Merms and spawn a Merm every four days if any Merms are killed. Typically only one Merm per Leaky Shack will be outside during the day. However, If that Merm engages in combat or if the house is struck with a Hammer, the rest of the Merms will emerge to help it fight. When Dusk comes, all Merms will leave their home to wander around in the vicinity.

items.name: Lesser Glow Berry
items.description: A Lesser Glow Berry is a Fruit Food Item found in Don't Starve Together. It is obtained by picking a Mysterious Plant in the Caves. It takes 4 days for a Lesser Glow Berry to regrow. It restores 3 and 12.5 at the cost of 10 .
items.beginnerTip: Player emits light upon consumption.

items.name: Lever Thing
items.description: The Lever Thing is one of the four Things in the Hamlet DLC. It is the Hamlet version of the Crank Thing.

items.name: Lichen
items.description: Lichen is a Food item in Don't Starve. It is classified as a Vegetable, and can only be obtained in the Ruins by harvesting Cave Lichen. Lichen cannot be cooked at a Fire Pit, Campfire, or Star Caller's Staff, but it can be used as an ingredient in a Crock Pot. Lichen regrows after 5 days.

items.name: Lichen/DST
items.description: Lichen is a Vegetable Food item. It can only be obtained by harvesting Cave Lichen in the Ruins. Lichen cannot be cooked at a Fire Pit, Campfire, or Star Caller's Staff, but it can be used as an ingredient in a Crock Pot. Lichen regrows after 5 days.

items.name: Life Giving Amulet
items.description: Protects you from death.
items.beginnerTip: Converts Hunger to Health. Resurrects the player on death and puts nearby mobs to sleep.

items.name: Life Giving Amulet/DST
items.description: Protects you from death.
items.beginnerTip: Converts Hunger to Health. Resurrects the player and puts nearby mobs to sleep.

items.name: Life Jacket
items.description: Safety first!
items.beginnerTip: Prevents player from drowning.

items.name: Light Bulb
items.description: A Light Bulb is a Food Item obtained by harvesting a Light Flower or as a drop from a Slurper or Big Tentacle.
items.beginnerTip: Provides small area of light when placed on the ground.

items.name: Light Bulb/DST
items.description: A Light Bulb is a Food Item obtained by harvesting a Light Flower or as a drop from a Slurper, a Big Tentacle or a Bulbous Lightbug. Additionally, Light Bulbs are dropped by Skittersquids and Crustashines, making them available on servers which are not connected to a Caves world. Since Light Flowers regrow every 3 days, Light Bulbs are fully renewable, meaning an unlimited supply of fuel for Lanterns and Miner Hats.
items.beginnerTip: Provides small area of light when placed on the ground.

items.name: Light Flower
items.description: Light Flowers are plants that serve as sources of light that can normally be found in Caves and Ruins. They are generated all over the caves but mostly spawn in Cave Swamp, and Wilds in the Ruins.

items.name: Light Flower/DST
items.description: Light Flowers are plants that serve as sources of light that can normally be found in Caves and Ruins. They are generated all over the caves but mostly spawn in Muddy biome.

items.name: Lightning Conductor
items.description: An electrifying addition to your mast.
items.beginnerTip: Lightning protection when atop a Mast.

items.name: Lightning Rod
items.description: Protection from strikes.
items.beginnerTip: Harnesses lightning.

items.name: Lightning Rod/DST
items.description: Protection from strikes.
items.beginnerTip: Harnesses lightning.

items.name: Limestone
items.description: Stone, with a hint of lime.

items.name: Limestone Suit
items.description: Sartorial reef.|protection=70%
items.beginnerTip: Reduces speed by 10%.

items.name: Limpet Rock
items.description: Limpet Rocks are a naturally spawning objects in the Shipwrecked DLC. They are common in Beach biomes and yield one Limpets each. They can be also mined for Rocks and Flint. If the player does not mine them, they will replenish themselves over 3 days, making them a good food source.

items.name: Limpets
items.description: Limpets are a Fish Food Item in the Shipwrecked DLC. They can be found growing naturally on Limpet Rocks, and as long as the Limpet Rock is not mined down, the Limpets will replenish themselves over 3 days. They can also be found on Wrecks and will replenish themselves over 2 days if the Wreck is not hammered. They can be used as an ingredient in several Crock Pot recipes, and give 0.5 Fish Value. __NOTOC__

items.name: Living Artifact
items.description: Lets just mix em and see what happens.
items.beginnerTip: Immune to Poison, Freezing, Overheating, Fog and Hay Fever. Offers Night vision.

items.name: Living Log
items.description: Put yourself into your work.

items.name: Living Log/DST
items.description: Living Logs are Items dropped by Treeguards, Poison Birchnut Trees and Mush Gnomes. They can also be obtained by chopping down Totally Normal Trees, the stump of Totally Normal Tree can be dug for another Living Log. Wormwood can always "craft" Living Logs at the cost of 20 Health.

items.name: Living Staff
items.description: The Living Staff is an item added to The Forge event in Don't Starve Together. Dropped from the last killed Pit Pig during the inferno on the third wave.

items.name: Lobster Bisque
items.description: Lobster Bisque was a Crock Pot recipe introduced to Don't Starve Together in Return of Them. It is made from Wobster and Ice. Since the Crock Pot will not accept Dead Wobster or Delicious Wobster, a living Wobster must be used.

items.name: Lobster Dinner
items.description: Lobster Dinner was introduced in Don't Starve Together along the She Sells Sea Shells update. It is cooked by adding 1 Wobster and 1 Butter. It takes 20 seconds to cook. It restores 37.5 , 60 , and 50 , making it one of the best food items to restore both Health and Sanity.

items.name: Log
items.description: Logs are basic building materials with multiple purposes. They can be Refined into Boards, which opens up more recipes.

items.name: Log Raft
items.description: Boat at your own risk.
items.beginnerTip: Sailing Speed: 4

items.name: Log Suit
items.description: Protects you from some damage.|protection=80%

items.name: Log Suit/DST
items.description: Protects you from some damage.

items.name: Log/DST
items.description: -|Normal=

items.name: Loot Stash
items.description: The Loot Stash is a naturally-spawning object exclusive to Don't Starve Together, introduced in A New Reign. It can be found in the Deciduous Forest or in the Mosaic Biome. A Loot Stash will spawn 1-3 days after the beginning of every Winter or spawn on day 1 during the Winter's Feast event. The spawn location of the Loot Stash changes with each passing Winter, it will despawn 1-3 days after the beginning of Spring and will respawn at the start of the next winter. (or after 20 days have passed during the Winter’s Feast event.) Attempting to open the Loot Stash with a Deer Antler will drop Bone Shards and summon Klaus. Using the Stag Antler on the Loot Stash will properly unlock it, causing it to drop 4 Bundled Supplies.

items.name: Lotus Flower
items.description: Lotus Flowers are edible Vegetable Items exclusive to the Hamlet DLC. They can be harvested from Lotus Plants found in the Lily Pond Biome. Raw or cooked, Lotus Flowers take 10 Days to spoil, and cannot be used in a Crock Pot. The Lotus Flower regrows in 5 days after it has been harvested.

items.name: Lucky Beast
items.description: Lucky Beast Head=
items.beginnerTip: Restores sanity over time when worn and dancing.

items.name: Lucky Hat
items.description: Sniff out treasures.
items.beginnerTip: Periodically creates a new X Marks the Spot

items.name: Lucky Whistle
items.description: Blow the whistle on wild hounds.

items.name: Lucy the Axe
items.description: Lucy the Axe is a character-specific item that Woodie begins the game with. Lucy has infinite durability and increased effectiveness (one swing at tree is worth two "chops" of regular axe) and in Woodie's hands who has faster innate chopping animation, cuts Trees extraordinarily fast. Lucy is a sentient being, and although it's not known if this is real or just Woodie's imagination, this is likely the former, as in DST, others can see her quotes. When equipped, Lucy will speak a line such as 'I missed you', 'Did you miss me?' and 'You came back!'.
items.beginnerTip: Infinite durability. Reduces chops required to chop a tree by half. Gives friendly advice.

items.name: Lucy the Axe/DST
items.description: Lucy the Axe is a character-specific item that Woodie begins the game with. Lucy has infinite durability and increased effectiveness (one swing at tree is worth two "chops" of regular axe) and in Woodie's hands who has faster innate chopping animation, cuts Trees extraordinarily fast. Lucy is a sentient being, and although it's not known if this is real or just Woodie's imagination, this is likely the former, as others can see her quotes. When equipped, Lucy will speak a line such as 'I missed you', 'Did you miss me?' and 'You came back!'.
items.beginnerTip: Has infinite durability. Reduces the amount of chops required to chop a tree by half. Gives friendly advice.

items.name: Lumpy Evergreen
items.description: Lumpy Evergreens are a variant of the typical Evergreen with lumpy and wilted-looking branches. Unlike normal Evergreens, the Lumpy variety does not produce Pine Cones, leading Characters to wonder how it reproduces at all. They still have a life-cycle, growing to huge trees and then reverting to small ones. Also like normal trees, lumpy ones can become Treeguards, which will have the lumpy appearance as opposed to the standard treeguard look. Like other trees, the stumps of the Lumpy Evergreen variety can be dug up with a Shovel or Regal Shovel to get an additional Log.

items.name: Lumpy Evergreen/DST
items.description: -|Generic=

items.name: Lunar Altars
items.description: The Lunar Altars are three types of altars created by inserting the respective pieces into Celestial Fissures. If all three Lunar Altars are built close to each other, within 5 tiles, the Mysterious Energy will appear. After spawning, the Mysterious Energy will release a pulse, completely replacing the current day with a Full Moon and causing moonstorms to appear on the map. During these full moons, Enlightenment will replace Sanity.
items.beginnerTip: Grants access to the Celestial Filter. Required to spawn

items.name: Lunar Experiment
items.description: There's a change brewing.
items.beginnerTip: Can be used to change some items and mobs into Lunar counterparts.

items.name: Lunar Funcap
items.description: It's like eating all kinds of mushrooms.
items.beginnerTip: Periodically spawns Lunar Mushroom Spores Items held in the player's inventory or equip slots receive +50% spoilage rate. Grants the player immunity to damage from Lunar Mushroom Spores.

items.name: Lunar Mushtree
items.description: Lunar Mushtrees are naturally generated objects exclusive to Don't Starve Together. They act as light sources inside the Lunar Grotto. With each Axe hit, the tree spawns a Lunar Spore. They drop two Logs and one Moon Shroom, the stump can be dug for 1 Log.

items.name: Lunar Wobster
items.description: The Lunar Wobster is a Mob exclusive to Don't Starve Together, introduced in Return of Them. Lunar Wobsters spawn from Moon Glass Mound during Dusk and Night.

items.name: Lune Tree
items.description: Lune Trees are Trees exclusive to Don't Starve Together, introduced in Return of Them. They are found in the Lunar Forest and Lunar Baths Biome on the Lunar Island. Additional Lune Trees can also be found on the Hermit Island.

items.name: Lune Tree Blossom
items.description: Lune Tree Blossoms are Items exclusive to Don't Starve Together, introduced in Return of Them. They are obtained by chopping Lune Trees. Additionally, they can be found naturally on the ground in Lunar Forest.

items.name: Lureplant
items.description: The Lureplant is a hostile plant which is so named for its behavior of dangling meats to attract prey. Like Krampus, a Lureplant has its own inventory, which is filled with the items its Eyeplants (see below) have stored but not yet digested. It has the capability of storing and digesting just about anything that can fit in the player's inventory.

items.name: Lureplant/DST
items.description: The Lureplant is a hostile, stationary plant named for its habit of dangling meats to attract prey. It has no attack of its own. Instead, it grows a field of Eyeplants around itself, which bite creatures that come close and grab loose items for it. Like Krampus, a Lureplant has its own inventory, which holds whatever its Eyeplants have collected until the Lureplant digests it.

items.name: Lush Carpet
items.description: Super Super soft.

items.name: Luxury Fan
items.description: Luxuriously soft, luxuriously large.
items.beginnerTip: Cools the character down and puts out fires

items.name: Luxury Fan/DST
items.description: Luxuriously soft, luxuriously large.
items.beginnerTip: Cools the character down and puts out fires

items.name: Machete
items.description: Hack stuff!
items.beginnerTip: Hacks down Bamboo Patches and Viney Bushes.

items.name: Mad Scientist Lab
items.description: Mad science has no limits. Except sanity.
items.beginnerTip: Unlocks Mad Science Filter.

items.name: Magic Flower
items.description: The Magic Flower is a plant exclusive to the Hamlet DLC. It is created by planting Magic Water and will give off light as well as raise the player's Sanity (roughly 0.6/second) in exchange for Hunger (roughly -0.5/second) when they are standing close to it.
items.beginnerTip: Converts hunger to sanity. Resurrects the player on Death.

items.name: Magic Seal
items.description: The Magic Seal is an Item introduced in the Shipwrecked DLC. It is dropped by the Sealnado's Seal form, regardless of whether it is killed or spared. It can be used to craft the Howling Conch and the Sail Stick.

items.name: Magic Water
items.description: Magic Water is an item exclusive to the Hamlet DLC. It can be obtained by interacting with the Fountain of Youth. Interacting with the Fountain also spawns the Pugalisk from Ominous Carving. Magic Water can be planted to grow a Magic Flower that regenerates Sanity at the cost of Hunger when the player stands close to it. Eating the Magic Water will cure Poison.

items.name: Magiluminescence
items.description: Pull power from the heavens.
items.beginnerTip: Provides light while worn. Raises Sanity over time. Increases speed by 20%.

items.name: Magiluminescence/DST
items.description: Pull power from the heavens.
items.beginnerTip: Provides light while worn. Raises Sanity over time. Increases speed by 20%.

items.name: Magma
items.description: Magma is an environmental feature found in the Desert biome and exclusive to Don't Starve Together. These pools are a part of a Set Piece found in the Desert, which serves as a spawn point for the Dragonfly. They are used by the Dragonfly to spawn Lavae.

items.name: Magma Pile
items.description: Magma Piles are naturally-spawning Structures in the Magma Field and Volcano Biomes in the Shipwrecked DLC. They are piles of igneous rocks which may be dug using a Shovel, using 4% of the Shovel's durability per dig. They must be dug 6 times to be removed, and 2-3 items will drop every 2 shovel digs. The gold-flecked Magma Pile has a chance to drop Gold Nuggets, while the regular one can drop Nitre. Both types also drop Rocks, Flint, and very rarely, red or blue Gems. Sometimes a Krissure, a sort of flaming geyser, will erupt after digging up a pile. This chance is higher while in the Volcano than in the Magma Field. Upon a Krissure's eruption, the final dropped items will be scattered about half a screen away. Magma Piles in Volcano Biome are renewable, after they are dug, they would regrow to full in a year at the same location, if a Krissure did not erupt after being dug.

items.name: Magma Turf
items.description: Magma Turf is one of the Turf Items exclusive to the Shipwrecked DLC, acquired by digging Magma Field tiles with a Pitchfork. Like other Turfs, it can be placed on any bare ground tile or used as fuel. It can also be used to craft Cobblestones, which are placeable Roads.

items.name: Magnifying Glass
items.description: See things from a different perspective.
items.beginnerTip: Investigates Peculiar Objects. Can light things on fire.

items.name: Malbatross Bill
items.description: The Malbatross Bill is an Item exclusive to Don't Starve Together, introduced in Return of Them. It is dropped by the Malbatross upon death.
items.beginnerTip: Moves a Boat Faster than a normal Oar or Driftwood Oar.

items.name: Malbatross Feather
items.description: The Malbatross Feather is an Item exclusive to Don't Starve Together, introduced in Return of Them. It is dropped by the Malbatross. It is also possible to obtain Malbatross Feathers by destroying a Sunken Chest. Malbatross Feathers are required to craft the Feathery Canvas. They can also be used to craft a Malbatross Quill Float

items.name: Mandrake
items.description: Rooted= |-| Picked= A Mandrake is a very rare, passive Mob found in Grasslands and Caves. They are very useful, and on average only 2-5 Mandrakes will spawn per World. They often spawn together in the same area, so finding one will usually result in finding them all. Mandrakes can be used to make the Pan Flute. They can also be used to make Mandrake Soup in a Crock Pot.

items.name: Mandrake Soup
items.description: Mandrake Soup is a Vegetable Food item cooked in the Crock Pot by adding 1 Raw Mandrake. It takes 60 seconds to cook.

items.name: Mandrake Soup/DST
items.description: Mandrake Soup is a Vegetable Food item cooked in the Crock Pot by adding 1 Raw Mandrake. It takes 60 seconds to cook.

items.name: Mandrake/DST
items.description: Rooted= |-|Picked= A Mandrake is a passive Mob found in Mandrake Forests. They are very rare and only 2-5 Mandrakes will spawn per World. They usually spawn in the same area and always on Grass Turf. No Mobs will eat Mandrakes that are still planted in the ground.

items.name: Mangrove Tree
items.description: Mangrove Trees are a type of Tree in the Shipwrecked DLC. They are found growing in the waters of the Mangrove biome and can only be accessed by Boat or Raft. They have a distinctive appearance with a bulbous trunk and roots that begin above the waterline.

items.name: Mant Mask
items.description: A face only a Mant could love.|protection=80%

items.name: Mant Suit
items.description: Walk a mile in a Mant's carapace.

items.name: Manure
items.description: Manure is an important resource for Farming. It is generated renewably by several creatures in the world, most notably Beefalo which make lots of it in herds for easy collection, but also including Koalefants, Pigs, and Splumonkeys. It can stack up to a maximum of 20 in the Inventory or on the ground and does not spoil over time.

items.name: Manure/DST
items.description: Manure is an important resource for Farming. It is generated renewably by several creatures in the world, most notably Beefalo which make lots of it in herds for easy collection, but also including Koalefants, Pigs, and Splumonkeys. It can stack up to a maximum of 20 in the Inventory or on the ground and does not spoil over time.

items.name: Marble
items.description: Marble is a Mineral resource which is obtained by mining Marble Pillars, Harp Statues, and Maxwell Statues with any type of pickaxe, or by using a Touch Stone. It is used to make Checkerboard Flooring and Marble Suits.

items.name: Marble Pillar
items.description: Marble Pillars are naturally spawning Structures found around the Wooden Thing in a Chess biome in Sandbox Mode or in various Chess biomes in Adventure Mode. Usually, there are Clockwork Monsters and Evil Flowers near them. They can be mined with a Pickaxe or the Pick/Axe to acquire 2-3 Marble pieces (2 + 33% chance to get 1 extra). The pickaxe requires 10 hits to break a Marble Pillar down, whereas the Pick/Axe only requires 8. Though it may use a lot of durability off a pickaxe, it is recommended to mine Marble Pillars so the player can make a Marble Suit for fighting.

items.name: Marble Pillar/DST
items.description: The Marble Pillars are naturally spawning Structures found in Chess Set Pieces, Marble Sculptures Set Pieces, or rarely in the Maxwell's Cemetery Set Piece. Depending on which Set Piece they spawn in, there could be Clockwork Knights, Clockwork Bishops, Clockwork Rooks, or Evil Flowers near them. They can be mined with any Pickaxe to acquire 2-3 Marble (2 + 33% chance to get 1 extra). A regular Pickaxe requires 10 hits to break a Marble Pillar down, whereas a Pick/Axe only requires 8.

items.name: Marble Sculptures
items.description: Incomplete Rook Sculpture=
items.beginnerTip: Unlocks / / in .

items.name: Marble Shrub
items.description: A Marble Sprout is a sapling exclusive to Don't Starve Together, introduced in A New Reign. It grows from a Marble Bean, can be dug out by Shovel/Regal Shovel and drop a Marble Bean.

items.name: Marble Statues
items.description: Comedy=
items.beginnerTip: Unlocks in ,

items.name: Marble Suit
items.description: It's heavy, but it will protect you.|protection=95%
items.beginnerTip: Reduces speed by 30%.

items.name: Marble Suit/DST
items.description: It's heavy, but it will protect you.|protection=95%
items.beginnerTip: Reduces speed by 30%.

items.name: Marble Tree
items.description: The Marble Tree is a naturally-spawning Structure that often appears in Adventure Mode, in a Chess Biome, or around the Wooden Thing. It usually spawns on Checkerboard Flooring, surrounded by Evil Flowers.

items.name: Marble Tree/DST
items.description: The Marble Tree is a naturally-spawning Structure that often appears in Chess Biome. It usually spawns on Checkerboard Flooring, surrounded by Evil Flowers.

items.name: Marble/DST
items.description: Marble is a Mineral resource. It is obtained by mining Marble Pillars, Marble Statues, Marble Sculptures, Harp Statues, and Maxwell Statues with any type of pickaxe, or by using a Touch Stone.

items.name: Marsh Turf
items.description: Marsh Turf is one of the Turf items, acquired by digging Marsh tiles with a Pitchfork. These turfs can commonly be found at the Marsh biome and rarely at the Mosaic biome. Like other Turfs, it can be placed on any bare ground tile, or it can be used as a good burning fuel for a Campfire or Fire Pit.

items.name: Marsh Turf/DST
items.description: Home is where the marsh is.

items.name: Masonry Oven
items.description: It's all fired up for the holidays.
items.beginnerTip: Grants access to the Winter's Feast Cooking Filter.

items.name: Maxwell Statue
items.description: Maxwell Statues are naturally-spawning Structures that can be found in various Set Pieces, although they are most common in Chess biomes in Survival Mode. They were constructed by Maxwell during his time on the Nightmare Throne, as a monument to himself — however, now that Charlie has replaced him as ruler of The Constant, they only serve as an ironic mockery of his past actions. They are often guarded by local Clockwork Monsters. When mined using a Pickaxe or similar tool, explosive, Old Bell, or Weather Pain, they drop 2-3 Marble.

items.name: Maxwell Statue/DST
items.description: The Maxwell Statue is a naturally-spawning Structure that can be found in various Set Pieces, particularly in Chess Biomes. It can be mined with a Pickaxe to obtain Marbles. Gunpowder, Slurtle Slime and Weather Pain can also be used to destroy the Statue.

items.name: Maxwell's Tooth Trap
items.description: Maxwell's Tooth Trap is a Trap found only in Adventure Mode. It is similar to a normal Tooth Trap, though it will trigger if the player and any other Mobs step on it, dealing 60 damage. It can't be picked up, and it will disappear once activated. They sit on the ground, just like a normal Tooth Trap planted by the player and are easy to see and avoid if they are watched out for.
items.beginnerTip: Deals 60 damage when triggered.

items.name: Meadow Turf
items.description: Meadow Turf is one of the Turf Items exclusive to the Shipwrecked DLC, acquired by digging Meadow tiles with a Pitchfork. Like other Turfs, it can be placed on any bare ground tile or used as fuel.

items.name: Meat
items.description: Meat is a Food item dropped by numerous fleshy creatures (Pigs, Beefalo, Deerclops etc.) It can be used to make the Ham Bat, or as an ingredient in multiple Crock Pot Recipes. It also can be dried on a Drying Rack for 2 days to make Jerky. Its less-filling alternative is a morsel, which only provides 12.5 hunger.

items.name: Meat/DST
items.description: Meat is a Food item dropped by numerous fleshy creatures(Pigs, Beefalo, Deerclops etc.) It can be used to make the Ham Bat, or as an ingredient in multiple Crock Pot Dishes. It also can be dried on a Drying Rack for 2 days to make Jerky. Its less-filling alternative is a morsel, which only provides 12.5 hunger.

items.name: Meatballs
items.description: Meatballs is a Meat Food item cooked in the Crock Pot by combining any Meats and fillers excluding Inedibles. However, adding 3.0 units of Meats will result in Meaty Stew instead. It takes 15 seconds to cook.

items.name: Meatballs/DST
items.description: Meatballs is a Meat Food item cooked in the Crock Pot by combining any Meats and fillers excluding Inedibles. However, adding 3.0 units of Meats will result in Meaty Stew instead. It takes 15 seconds to cook.

items.name: Meated Nettles
items.description: The Meated Nettles are a Food Item exclusive to Hamlet. They can be cooked in a Crock Pot with at least two Nettles and a Meat value of at least one. Filler cannot be Inedibles. Adding Honey will result in Honey Nuggets. Adding more than one Monster Food will result in Monster Lasagna.
items.beginnerTip: Grants immunity to Hayfever for 600 seconds

items.name: Meaty Stew
items.description: Meaty Stew is a Crock Pot food item cooked by adding 3.0 units of Meats. It takes 15 seconds to cook. It is one of the most filling food items in the game, restoring an astounding 150 .

items.name: Meaty Stew/DST
items.description: Meaty Stew is a Crock Pot food item cooked by adding 3.0 units of Meats. It takes 15 seconds to cook. It is one of the most filling food items in the game, restoring an astounding 150 .

items.name: Melonsicle
items.description: The Melonsicle is a Fruit Food item introduced in the Reign of Giants DLC. It is inexplicably cooked in the Crock Pot by combining 1 Raw Watermelon, 1 Ice, and 1 Twig.
items.beginnerTip: Lowers temperature by 10 degrees over 10 seconds.

items.name: Melonsicle/DST
items.description: The Melonsicle is a Fruit Food item. It is inexplicably cooked in the Crock Pot by combining 1 Raw Watermelon, 1 Ice, and 1 Twig. No Meats, Vegetables, or Eggs should be added.
items.beginnerTip: Lowers temperature by 10 degrees over 10 seconds.

items.name: Merm Flort-ifications
items.description: True warriors live within.

items.name: Merm Head
items.description: Merm Heads are decorative structures usually found around Pig Villages or randomly in Swamps. They are severed Merm heads on sticks planted in the ground, similar to Pig Heads.

items.name: Merm Head/DST
items.description: Merm Heads are decorative structures usually found around Pig Villages or randomly in Swamps. They are severed Merm heads on sticks planted in the ground, similar to Pig Heads.

items.name: Mermhouse
items.description: Deconstructing a Mermhouse with a Hammer yields 1-2 Rocks, 1 Board, and 1 Fish.

items.name: Message in a Bottle
items.description: A Message in a Bottle is a naturally spawning Item exclusive to the Shipwrecked DLC. It can be found lying on Beaches or floating in the Ocean, and appears as a regular bottle with a piece of paper inside. Once the message has been read, it will turn into an Empty Bottle.
items.beginnerTip: Reveals a treasure's location on the Map.

items.name: Message in a Bottle/DST
items.description: The Message in a Bottle is an item found naturally in the Coastal Ocean, and can also spawn every 1 to 2 days 10 Tiles from the players in the Ocean. The spawning bottle will need 1.25 tiles of clear space in the Ocean, and must be at least 8.75 tiles from any flotsam. The spawning attempt will happen even if the player is on land, but the attempt will fail and retry every 60 seconds.
items.beginnerTip: Reveal Crabby Hermit and Sunken Chest on the Map.

items.name: Metal Potato Thing
items.description: The Metal Potato Thing is one of four Things used on the Wooden Thing to travel to the next world. It spawns naturally in every world in its own Set Piece. It is located near some Basic Farms, which are surrounded by some Grass and Twigs, a Shovel, and unpicked Carrots.

items.name: Midsummer Cawnival/Prize Booth
items.description: See what prizes are in store.
items.beginnerTip: Can be placed as a Structure.

items.name: Milkmade Hat
items.description: The Milkmade Hat is an item exclusive to Don't Starve Together, introduced in Return of Them. It is obtained by cooking 1 Naked Nostrils, 1 raw Kelp Fronds, 1 Dairy, and any filler (Twigs, Eggs, Carrots, etc).
items.beginnerTip: Restore up to 187.5 over 4 minutes.

items.name: Milky Whites
items.description: Milky Whites is a Dairy Food Item exclusive to Don't Starve Together, introduced in the An Eye for An Eye update. It is dropped by the Eye of Terror. It can be used as a filler in most Crock Pot recipes.

items.name: Miner Hat
items.description: Light up the night with your noggin.
items.beginnerTip: Provides light while worn.

items.name: Miner Hat/DST
items.description: Light up the night with your noggin.
items.beginnerTip: Provides light while worn.

items.name: Mini Glacier
items.description: Mini Glaciers are naturally occurring objects found in the Reign of Giants DLC. When mined, they will drop Ice and Rocks. Mini Glaciers are only at their fullest during the Winter and will begin to melt in the Spring. By Summer, all that will be left is a puddle of water, and the player will have to wait until Autumn for them to slowly begin to freeze again. If exposed to a heat source (such as a Campfire) Mini glaciers will melt, reducing down to the puddle state. Once the heat source is gone, and if the ambient temperature is low enough, the Mini Glacier will freeze again. It will return to the maximum state allowed by the current temperature. When mined, Mini Glaciers make a different sound from boulders.

items.name: Mini Glacier/DST
items.description: Mini Glaciers are naturally occurring objects found in the Don't Starve Together. When mined, they will drop Ices. Mini Glaciers are only at their fullest during the Winter and will begin to melt in the Spring. By Summer, all that will be left is a puddle of water, and the player will have to wait until Autumn for them to slowly begin to freeze again. If exposed to a heat source (such as a Campfire) Mini glaciers will melt, reducing down to the puddle state. Once the heat source is gone, and if the ambient temperature is low enough, the Mini Glacier will freeze again. It will return to the maximum state allowed by the current temperature. When mined, Mini Glaciers make a different sound from boulders.

items.name: Mini Sign
items.description: The Mini Sign is a craftable Item located in the Structures Tab. 1 Board is used to craft 4 Mini Signs, requiring a Science Machine to prototype. By placing an item near a Mini Sign, the player can draw that item on it once by using a Feather Pencil.

items.name: Mini Sign/DST
items.description: The Mini Sign is a craftable Item found in the Decorations Filter and Structures Filter. 1 Board is used to craft 4 Mini Signs, requiring a Science Machine to prototype. By placing an item near a Mini Sign, the player can draw that item on it once by using a Feather Pencil.

items.name: Miniature Tree
items.description: A little piece of the Cawnival.
items.beginnerTip: Can be placed as a Structure.

items.name: Miss Sow's Floral Arrangements
items.description: There's a little green thumb in everyone.
items.beginnerTip: Sells Farming utensils.

items.name: Misshapen Bird
items.description: The Misshapen Bird is a hostile mob exclusive to Don't Starve Together, introduced in Eye of the Storm update. It attacks players that come within range by lobbing a projectile in an arc. The projectile deals damage in a small area around where it lands. This can lead to a Misshapen Bird damaging itself and dying as a result.

items.name: Moggles
items.description: Grants the wearer Smell-E-Vision.
items.beginnerTip: Grants Nightvision.

items.name: Moggles/DST
items.description: Grants the wearer Smell-E-Vision.
items.beginnerTip: Grants Night Vision.

items.name: Molten Darts
items.description: Molten Darts is an item added to The Forge in Don't Starve Together.

items.name: Monster Food
items.description: right Monster Foods are food items which have a monster food value, meaning they are typically poisonous and cause damage to Health and Sanity when eaten; however, these effects can be lessened by cooking them. Monster foods will create Monster Lasagna when more than one is used in a Crock Pot, except when Twigs are added as an ingredient or another recipe with higher priority matches the ingredients used.

items.name: Monster Lasagna
items.description: Monster Lasagna is a Meat Food item cooked in the Crock Pot by combining 2 Monster Food items, which include Monster Meat, Monster Jerky, Durians, and Jellyfish. It takes 10 seconds to cook.

items.name: Monster Lasagna/DST
items.description: Monster Lasagna is a Meat Food item cooked in the Crock Pot by combining 2 Monster Food items, which include Monster Meat, Monster Jerky, Durians, and Jellyfish. It takes 10 seconds to cook.

items.name: Monster Meat
items.description: Monster Meat is a Food Item obtained by killing most Monsters. Most monsters will drop Monster Meat at least 50% of the time, otherwise dropping their special resources (for example Spiders also drop Silk and Spider Gland). It counts both as Monster Food and Meat.

items.name: Monster Meat/DST
items.description: Monster Meat is a Food item obtained by killing most Monsters. Most monsters will drop Monster Meat at least 50% of the time, otherwise dropping their special resources (for example Spiders also drop Silk and Spider Gland).

items.name: Monster Tartare
items.description: Monster Tartare is a Warly-specific Food Item cooked in the Portable Crock Pot by adding 2 Monster Foods, 1 Vegetables, and 1 Eggs. It takes 40 seconds to cook.

items.name: Monster Tartare/DST
items.description: Monster Tartare is a Warly-specific Food Item cooked in the Portable Crock Pot by adding 2 Monster Foods. It takes 10 seconds to cook.

items.name: Moon Caller's Staff
items.description: The Moon Caller's Staff is a Don't Starve Together exclusive Item. It acts similarly to the Star Caller's Staff, with the difference of having 50 uses and creating a Polar Light, that lasts 2 Days and cools the players down, as opposed to warming them like the Dwarf Star. If a Deconstruction Staff is used to break this staff, it will drop 4 Nightmare Fuel, 2 Living Logs and an Iridescent Gem.
items.beginnerTip: Spawns a Polar Light. Can be placed in a Moon Stone for infinite Polar Light.

items.name: Moon Crater Turf
items.description: The cratered surface of the moon.

items.name: Moon Glass
items.description: The Moon Glass is a naturally-spawning object exclusive to Don't Starve Together, introduced in Return of Them. It is found on the Lunar Island mostly in the Lunar Mine, Lunar Baths and above Vitreoasis in Lunar Grotto Biomes. It can be mined for two Moon Shards and 25% to get 1 extra.

items.name: Moon Moth Wings
items.description: Moon Moth Wings are a Food item exclusive to Don't Starve Together, introduced in Return of Them. They are dropped by Moon Moths and take 6 Days to spoil.

items.name: Moon Quay Beach Turf
items.description: A patch of sand, with a faint scent of bananas.

items.name: Moon Rock
items.description: Moon Rocks are Items exclusive to Don't Starve Together. They are obtained by mining crash-landed Meteors, which have the appearance of sharp rocks striped with jagged blue cracks, or Suspicious Moonrock sculptures. Mining a Meteor Boulder will yield a Rock, a Flint, and 2 Moon Rocks. There is a 60% chance for a third, and a 30% chance for a fourth Moon Rock.

items.name: Moon Shard
items.description: Moon Shards are a resource exclusive to Don't Starve Together, introduced in Return of Them.

items.name: Moon Shroom
items.description: The Moon Shroom is a Vegetable Food item that is exclusive to Don't Starve Together. It can be harvested from Lunar Mushtrees or Naked Mole Bat Burrows, both inside the Lunar Grotto. Eating it raw will restore 12.5 and 10 . It also applies 6.6 seconds of Grogginess, slowing down the player.
items.beginnerTip: Puts the player to sleep (Raw)

items.name: Moon Stone
items.description: The Moon Stone is a naturally spawning object in Don't Starve Together. It can usually be found in its own Set Piece in a dense Evergreen forest surrounded by several Suspicious Moonrocks, Moon Rubble and Fireflies. It can be damaged, but not completely destroyed, and is not flammable.
items.beginnerTip: Turns a Star Caller's Staff into a Moon Caller's Staff. Spawns Hounds and Werepigs.

items.name: Moonblind Crow
items.description: The Moonblind Crow is a hostile mob exclusive to Don't Starve Together, introduced in Eye of the Storm update. It attacks players by pecking them when they come within range.

items.name: Moose/Goose Egg
items.description: The Moose/Goose Egg is an object in the Reign of Giants DLC. During Spring, Moose/Goose will wander off to lay an egg. The egg radiates electricity and can be struck with a Hammer 4 times to cause it to hatch, otherwise if the Moose/Goose is left alone, it will hatch on its own. Each strike with the Hammer deals 10 damage to the player. A Weather Pain can be used to hatch the egg from a distance without taking damage. 5 Moslings will hatch from the egg and attack if the player gets too close.

items.name: Moose/Goose Egg/DST
items.description: The Moose/Goose Egg is an object in the Don't Starve Together. During Spring, a number of Moose/Goose will appear and lay an egg. If the Moose/Goose Egg is left alone, it will hatch after 2 days and spawn 5 Moslings. The egg can also be hammered 4 times to break, but each hit will strike the player with 10 electricity damage. This damage can be avoided by wearing Lightning proof Clothes or using a Weather Pain.

items.name: Moqueca
items.description: Moqueca is a Warly-specific Food item cooked in the Portable Crock Pot, exclusive to Don't Starve Together. It requires at least 0.25 Fishes, a Toma Root and an Onion to cook. Fillers cannot be Inedibles.

items.name: Morning Star
items.description: Morning light for a nighttime fight.|dischargeRate=32px|link=Fuel#None Fuel 6 min
items.beginnerTip: Emits light. Does more damage to wet targets.

items.name: Morning Star/DST
items.description: Morning light for a nighttime fight.
items.beginnerTip: Emits light. Does Electric damage.

items.name: Morsel
items.description: A Morsel is a meat food item that is dropped by Rabbits, Redbirds, Crows, Snowbirds, Smallbirds, Baby Beefalo (as Baby and Toddler), Splumonkeys, Moleworms, Buzzards, Prime Apes, and Pengulls when they are killed. A Morsel can be used in several Crock Pot recipes as a meat filler, and can be dried on a Drying Rack for 1 day to produce a Small Jerky. Like other meats, a morsel can be eaten by a Pig to have them follow the player, or can be given to the Pig King in exchange for a Gold nugget. It has a meat value of 0.5.

items.name: Morsel/DST
items.description: A Morsel is a meat food item that is dropped by Rabbits, Redbirds, Crows, Snowbirds, Smallbirds, Baby Beefalo (as Baby and Toddler), Splumonkeys, Moleworms, Buzzards, Prime Apes, and Pengulls when they are killed. A Morsel can be used in several Crock Pot recipes as a meat filler, and can be dried on a Drying Rack for 1 day to produce a Small Jerky. Like other meats, a morsel can be eaten by a Pig to have them follow the player, or can be given to the Pig King in exchange for a Gold nugget. It has a meat value of 0.5.

items.name: Mosaic Flooring
items.description: Mosaic Flooring is a turf type exclusive to Don't Starve Together. It was added in A Little Drama Update alongside with lush carpet and Ruins turfs. It can be found near the Stage Set Piece or crafted using a single piece of Marble for four turf. It comes in three different colours.

items.name: Mosling
items.description: The Mosling is a small baby bird in the Reign of Giants DLC, spawned from an Egg on a nest made by a Moose/Goose during Spring. Nearby Moslings will form a herd centered around a single nest. They will roam around eating various Food they can find, including foods from Crock Pots and drying racks. When Spring ends, the Moslings will take flight and ascend into the sky. If killed, a Mosling will increase the player's Naughtiness level by 6.

items.name: Mosling/DST
items.description: The Mosling is a Mob in the Don't Starve Together, spawned from an Egg on a nest made by a Moose/Goose during Spring. Nearby Moslings will form a herd centered around a single nest. They will roam around eating various Food they can find, including foods from Crock Pots and drying racks. When Spring ends, the Moslings will take flight and ascend into the sky. If killed, a Mosling will increase the player's Naughtiness level by 6.

items.name: Mosquito
items.description: A Mosquito is a hostile Mob that spawns from Ponds, at Dusk and Night, in Marsh Biomes. Mosquitoes are fast-moving and aggressive.

items.name: Mosquito Sack
items.description: The Mosquito Sack is the blood-storing sac of Mosquitoes, with a 50% chance to drop upon its death.
items.beginnerTip: Healing properties

items.name: Mosquito Sack/DST
items.description: The Mosquito Sack is the blood-storing sac of Mosquitoes, with a 50% chance to drop upon its death.
items.beginnerTip: Healing properties

items.name: Mosquito/DST
items.description: A Mosquito is a hostile Mob that spawns from Ponds, at Dusk and Night, in Marsh Biomes. Mosquitoes are fast-moving and aggressive.

items.name: Mossy Turf
items.description: Mossy Turf is a Turf Item exclusive to the Hamlet DLC, spawning in the Suburbs Biome. Like other Turfs, it can be placed on any bare ground tile or used as fuel.

items.name: Mud Turf
items.description: Mud Turf is one of the Turf items, acquired by digging Mud Turf tiles with a Pitchfork. Like other Turfs, it can be placed on any bare ground tile, or it can be used as fuel.

items.name: Mud Turf/DST
items.description: A patch of muddy ground.

items.description: Blue Spore=

items.description: Mushrooms are naturally generated objects.
