items.name: Mushtree
items.description: Mushtrees are naturally generated objects that act as light sources inside Caves.

items.name: Mushtree/DST
items.description: Blue Mushtree=

items.name: Mussel
items.description: Mussels are a Fish Food Item introduced in the Shipwrecked DLC. They can be harvested from Mussel Beds that are found in the Shallow Ocean using a Mussel Stick or a Trawl Net. Mussels can be used as an ingredient in Crock Pot recipes. Warly needs them to cook Mussel Bouillabaise in his Portable Crock Pot. Additionally, Mussels can also be used to craft a new Mussel Bed that can be planted in the Ocean by the player.

items.name: Mussel Bed
items.description: Mussels are naturally spawning objects introduced in the Shipwrecked DLC. They appear as clusters of three oval shadows in the Shallow Ocean that the player can move towards in a Boat. In order to harvest them, the player can craft a Mussel Stick and wait a minimum of one day, then the Mussel Stick will be coated in Mussels. When harvested, this results in one, three, or six Mussels, depending on how long the player left the stick in the Mussel Bed. The Mussel Bed and stick are consumed by this.

items.name: Mussel Bouillabaisse
items.description: Mussel Bouillabaise is a Warly specific Food item exclusive to the Shipwrecked DLC. It is cooked in the Portable Crock Pot by adding 2 Raw Mussels and 2.0 units of Vegetables and takes 40 seconds to cook.

items.name: Mussel Stick
items.description: Mussels stick to it!
items.beginnerTip: Attract Mussels for harvest.

items.name: Mutated Fungal Turf
items.description: The mutated fungal floor of a cave.

items.name: Naked Nostrils
items.description: Naked Nostrils are Food items exclusive to Don't Starve Together. They are dropped by Naked Mole Bats upon death.

items.name: Napsack
items.description: A throwable pouch full of sleep.

items.name: Nasty Spear Trap
items.description: -| Nasty Spear Trap= |-| Busted Spear Trap=

items.name: Navigadget
items.description: The Navigadget is an item exclusive to Wheeler from the Hamlet DLC. It can hold any item that can be in a player's inventory, such as Logs, Rocks, Gold Nuggets, Meat, Carrots, and Lost Relics. Once the item is placed in the Navigadget, a compass will appear beneath the player with a red arrow pointing towards either the nearest instance of the item, the nearest structure that can be mined to obtain the item, or the nearest mob that drops that item. The Navigadget can act as an extra slot since it will keep the item placed inside once the Navigadget is removed from the player's hand slot.
items.beginnerTip: Locate items.

items.name: Nectar
items.description: Nectar is a Food Item exclusive to the Hamlet DLC, dropped by any levels of Snaptooth Seedlings and Snaptooth Flytraps.

items.name: Neon Quattro
items.description: Neon Quattro are a Fish Food Item introduced in the Shipwrecked DLC. They can be obtained by stocking Fish Farms with Roe, together with Purple Groupers, Pierrot Fish and Tropical Fish. They can be used in the Crock Pot, and count as 0.5 units of Meat and 1 unit of Fish. They are specifically required to cook the Tropical Bouillabaisse. Neon Quattro cannot be dried using a Drying Rack.

items.name: Nettle Rolls
items.description: Nettle Rolls are a Crock Pot dish introduced in the Hamlet DLC. They require at least 3 Nettles to cook, and a filler, which cannot be a Mandrake. Adding Vegetables as filler may result in Ratatouille, while adding Fruits as filler may result in Fist Full of Jam.
items.beginnerTip: Negates the effects of Hay Fever for 720 seconds.

items.name: Nettle Vine
items.description: -|Vine=

items.name: Night Armor
items.description: Protects your body, but not your mind.
items.beginnerTip: Decreases sanity by 10% of total damage taken.

items.name: Night Armor/DST
items.description: Protects your body, but not your mind.
items.beginnerTip: Decreases sanity by 10% of total damage taken.

items.name: Nightcap
items.description: A cap for your sleepy head.

items.name: Nightmare Amulet
items.description: Induce insanity.
items.beginnerTip: Induces insanity effects.

items.name: Nightmare Amulet/DST
items.description: Induce insanity.
items.beginnerTip: Induces insanity effects.

items.name: Nightmare Fissure
items.description: Nightmare Fissures are objects that appear in the Ruins and rarely in Caves, more specifically, on Stalagmite Terrain. They act identical to Nightmare Lights, but do not drain sanity. Depending on the phase of the Nightmare Cycle, they emit more or less light - the greater the light radius, the higher the chance of spawning Shadow Creatures.

items.name: Nightmare Fissure/DST
items.description: Nightmare Fissures are objects that appear in the Ruins and rarely in Caves, more specifically, on Stalagmite Terrain. They act identical to Nightmare Lights.

items.name: Nightmare Fuel
items.description: Evil residue used by the foolish and crazy.
items.beginnerTip: Used for dark and ancient magic.

items.name: Nightmare Fuel/DST
items.description: Nightmare Fuel is a refined item used in the ways of dark and ancient magic. It requires a Prestihatitator to prototype and costs 4 Dark Petals to craft. It can also be obtained as a drop from various mobs and objects.
items.beginnerTip: Used for dark and ancient magic.

items.name: Nightmare Light
items.description: Nightmare Lights are light sources found within the Ruins. They cannot be opened or destroyed with a Hammer. Instead, the amount of light they emit depends on the current state of the Nightmare Cycle that the Ruins are in; the more extreme the magical state, the more the Nightmare Lights open up.

items.name: Nightmare Light/DST
items.description: Nightmare Lights are light sources found within the Ruins. They cannot be opened or destroyed with a Hammer. Instead, the amount of light they emit depends on the current state of the Nightmare Cycle that the Ruins are in; the more extreme the magical state, the more the Nightmare Lights open up.

items.name: Nightmarish Bird Whistle
items.description: Strikes fear into even the biggest birds.
items.beginnerTip: Disables the natural spawning of the BFB.

items.name: Nitre
items.description: Nitre is a Mineral resource obtained by mining smooth Boulders, which will drop at least one (along with other minerals) upon being mined. It also occasionally falls during underground Earthquakes. It can be used to craft Salt Licks and Gunpowder. __NOTOC__

items.name: Nitre Formation
items.description: A Nitre Formation is an object in Don't Starve Together that forms in Blue Ponds (characterized by their color, Algae and Eels) in the Caves as a result of Acid Rain. This process solidifies the pond and causes the player to not be able to use a Fishing Rod on it until the formation is destroyed. If mined, the Nitre Formation drops 3-4 Nitre.They will regrow as long as acid rain is falling.

items.name: Nitre/DST
items.description: Nitre is a Mineral resource obtained by mining smooth Boulders, which will drop at least one (along with other minerals) upon being mined. It also occasionally falls during underground Earthquakes. It can be used to craft Salt Licks and Gunpowder.

items.name: No-Eyed Deer
items.description: -|No antlers=

items.name: Nox Helm
items.description: The Nox Helm is an item added to The Forge in Don't Starve Together.
items.beginnerTip: +15% physical damage

items.name: Nutrient
items.description: Nutrients are a feature exclusive to Don't Starve Together and introduced in Return of Them. Nutrients are present in the ground of Farm Soil. They are important components in the growth of Farm Plants.

items.name: Oar
items.description: Row, row, row your boat.
items.beginnerTip: Moves a Boat.

items.name: Obsidian
items.description: Obsidian is an Item found in the Shipwrecked DLC. It is used to craft improved versions of most Tools and some Weapons. It can be acquired by destroying Obsidian Boulders on the Volcano using explosives such as Gunpowder or Coconade or extinguishing a Lava Pool with Ice. Obsidian can also be obtained by mining intact Dragoon Eggs.

items.name: Obsidian Armor
items.description: Hot to the touch.
items.beginnerTip: Absorbs 70% of physical damage. Grants immunity to fire damage. Ignites attackers.

items.name: Obsidian Axe
items.description: Like a regular axe, only hotter.
items.beginnerTip: Reduces the amount of chops required to chop a tree. Gains charges for heat and light outside of Hurricane Season. Increased damage when charged. Emits light when charged.

items.name: Obsidian Fire Pit
items.description: The fieriest of all fires!
items.beginnerTip: Provides light while burning. Burns fuel longer than normal fires. Is not affected by Strong Winds.

items.name: Obsidian Machete
items.description: No summary is available; see the linked wiki page.

items.name: Obsidian Spear
items.description: How about a lil fire with your spear?
items.beginnerTip: Ignites target outside Hurricane Season. Increased damage when charged. Emits light when charged.

items.name: Obsidian Workbench
items.description: The Obsidian Workbench is a naturally spawning Structure introduced in the Shipwrecked DLC. It is found inside the Volcano. It functions similarly to the Ancient Pseudoscience Station, and allows players to craft items from the Volcanic Tab while they are near the workbench. If the player is wearing a Brain of Thought, they can craft Volcanic items without being near the workbench.
items.beginnerTip: Grants access to the Volcanic Tab.

items.name: Ocean
items.description: In the original Don't Starve and Reign of Giants content, the Ocean acts as a barrier, and during Winter, a place for Pengulls to spawn before they hop onto shore. No living thing can cross the ocean, not even flying mobs like Batilisks and Bees. Flotsams can be found in the ocean, and it is the only object the player can interact with in the ocean.

items.name: Ocean Fishes
items.description: Ocean Fish are passive Mobs in Don't Starve Together, introduced in Return of Them. A new school of fish appears every 15 to 60 seconds in the vicinity of players in the Ocean. There are seventeen species of fish in the ocean, each with its specific location, Food value, and Weight. __TOC__

items.name: Oinc
items.description: Oinc is the currency used in the Hamlet DLC to purchase Items from Pig Shops. Players can acquire them by exchanging items with various Pig Traders (see page for more information).
items.beginnerTip: Can be used to purchase items from Pig Traders.

items.name: Old Bell
items.description: This isn't just any bell.
items.beginnerTip: Summons a giant creature to smash things in its path.

items.name: Ominous Carving
items.description: The Ominous Carving is a Structure exclusive to the Hamlet DLC. When the Magic Water is taken from the Fountain of Youth, the Pugalisk will spawn from the Ominous Carving. After the Pugalisk leaves the carving and was killed, the carving will close.
items.beginnerTip: Spawns Pugalisk when is activated.

items.name: One-man Band
items.description: Even crazy musicians amass a following.

items.name: One-man Band/DST
items.description: Even crazy musicians amass a following.

items.name: Onion
items.description: The Onion is a vegetable food item in Don't Starve Together. Onions can be farmed with a small chance to appear from normal Seeds or directly planted using Pointy Seeds. Feeding an Onion to a bird in a Birdcage will produce 1 Pointy Seeds, as of the "Reap What You Sow" update.

items.name: Orange Gem
items.description: The Orange Gem is an item used to craft two Ancient items in Don't Starve. It can be used to craft The Lazy Forager, which automatically collects items, and The Lazy Explorer, which teleports the player a short distance across the screen.

items.name: Orange Gem/DST
items.description: The Orange Gem is an item used to craft two Ancient items in Don't Starve Together. It can be used to craft The Lazy Forager, which automatically collects items, and The Lazy Explorer, which teleports the player a short distance across the screen.

items.name: Orange Moonlens
items.description: No summary is available; see the linked wiki page.

items.name: Ornate Chest
items.description: An Ornate Chest is a Structure found in the Labyrinth biome and Atrium of the Ruins. Ornate Chests are usually surrounded by Dangling Depth Dweller webbing.

items.name: Ornate Chest/DST
items.description: An Ornate Chest is a Structure found in the Labyrinth biome of the Ruins and Atrium. Ornate Chests are usually surrounded by Dangling Depth Dweller webbing.

items.name: Overgrown Statue
items.description: The Overgrown Statue is a naturally spawning object that spawns in a Set Piece with 4 Briars around it. It can be mined with a Pickaxe for 2-3 Marbles. The Overgrown Statue looks exactly like the Harp Statue with vines, but after mining it, it leaves behind residue on the ground, marking the respawning point for Briars.

items.name: Packet of Seeds
items.description: Unusual crop seeds. Plant in tilled soil.

items.name: Painted Sand Turf
items.description: Painted Sand Turf is a Turf Item exclusive to the Hamlet DLC. Like other Turfs, it can be placed on any bare ground tile or used as fuel. It spawns naturally in the Painted Biome and can be acquired with a Pitchfork.

items.name: Palace
items.description: The Palace is a Structure exclusive to the Hamlet DLC which spawns in a Pig City on a separate island from the starting island. To get to the second island the player must go through the palace Pig Ruins (The one with a pig on the top). The Palace is surrounded by four elegant-looking Watch Towers. The Watch Towers can be deconstructed using a Deconstruction Staff for 4 Pig Skins, 2 Halberds and 3 Cut Stones.

items.name: Palm Leaf
items.description: Palm Leaves are a resource in Shipwrecked DLC. They can be obtained by chopping down Palm Trees.

items.name: Palm Tree
items.description: Palm Trees are a variety of Tree found in Beach biomes in the Shipwrecked DLC. When chopped down with an Axe, they yield Logs and Palm Leaves. Fully-grown Palm Trees will grow Coconuts, which will also drop when the tree is cut down. The Coconuts can be planted to create Palm Tree Saplings, which grow into new Palm Trees. They can also be split into 2 halves with a Machete, allowing them to be used as food, however they can no longer be planted once split. As with almost all trees (with the exception of the Mangrove Tree), the stump may be dug up with a Shovel to yield another Log.

items.name: Palm Treeguard
items.description: Palm Treeguards are hostile Boss Monsters in the Shipwrecked DLC. They are the Palm Tree equivalent of Treeguards, and, like Treeguards, may spawn as a result of cutting down a nearby Palm Tree. Assuming enough palm trees are nearby, a minimum of two Palm Treeguards always appear when the spawn condition is met. With growing day count, the maximum number of Treeguards spawned rises - to four from day 30, to five on day 80.

items.name: Palmcone Tree
items.description: Palmcone Trees are Plants exclusive to Don't Starve Together, introduced in The Curse of Moon Quay update. It can be found on Moon Quay Island. They are renewable through the Palmcone Sprouts dropped from an Unnatural Portal.

items.name: Pan Flute
items.description: Music to soothe savage beasts.
items.beginnerTip: Puts nearby mobs to sleep.

items.name: Pan Flute/DST
items.description: Music to soothe savage beasts.
items.beginnerTip: Puts nearby mobs to sleep.

items.name: Papyrus
items.description: For writing things
items.beginnerTip: Used to make Books among other things

items.name: Papyrus/DST
items.description: For writing things
items.beginnerTip: Used to make Books among other things

items.description: -| Parrot=

items.name: Particulate Purifier
items.description: Keep nasty airborne particulates away!
items.beginnerTip: Protects the player from poisonous gas clouds.

items.name: Peagawk
items.description: The Peagawk is a Mob exclusive to the Hamlet DLC. It is typically encountered in the Wild Plains and Rainforest Biome with its tail feathers arranged in a way to resemble a bush with many blinking eyes. It eats Vegetables off the ground.

items.name: Peagawk Plume
items.description: The Peagawk Plume is an Item dropped by Peagawks in the Hamlet DLC. They can be obtained either by killing the bird or by picking its feathers while it is distracted. A single Peagawk can provide up to seven Plumes the first time it is picked. A bald Peagawk will regrow one Plume after one Day, and cannot regrow more than one Plume, no matter how much time has passed. 2 Plumes are also received when digging a Secret Bandit Camp.

items.name: Pearl's Pearl
items.description: Pearl's Pearl is an item exclusive to Don't Starve Together, introduced in Return of Them. It can be obtained from the Crabby Hermit by following her questline.
items.beginnerTip: Socket in Crab King to loot Inactive Celestial Tribute

items.name: Pebble Crab
items.description: The Pebble Crab is a passive Mob exclusive to The Gorge event in Don't Starve Together.

items.name: Peg Leg
items.description: The Peg Leg is a Weapon exclusive to the Shipwrecked DLC. It does the same damage as a Spear and has one third of its uses, 50. One can find it in X Marks the Spot chests.

items.name: Pepper
items.description: The Pepper is a Vegetable Food item in Don't Starve Together. Pepper can also be Farmed by planting Seeds for a chance of growing them or by using Lumpy Seeds. When eaten raw, Pepper restores 9.5 Hunger. In addition, it reduces Health by 20 and Sanity by 15. They take 15 days to spoil and can also be used by Warly to produce Chili Flakes in the Portable Grinding Mill.

items.name: Petals
items.description: Petals are a Vegetable Food Item obtained by picking Flowers, which are commonly found in Grassland Biomes. They restore 5 Sanity when picked and 1 Health point when eaten. Like other vegetables, they can be fed to Pigs to produce Manure. No variant of petals may be used in a Crock Pot.

items.name: Petals/DST
items.description: Petals are a Vegetable Food Item obtained by picking Flowers, including Roses, which are commonly found in Grassland Biomes. They restore 5 Sanity when picked and 1 Health point when eaten. Like other vegetables, they can be fed to Pigs to produce Manure. No variant of petals may be used in a Crock Pot, unless they have been dried.

items.name: Petrified Tree
items.description: Petrified Trees are a variant of Trees found in Don't Starve Together. They yield Rocks, Flint, or Nitre when mined with a Pickaxe, and therefore are alternatives to Boulders to obtain these resources.

items.name: Petrifying Bones
items.description: Petrifying Bones are an object introduced in the Hamlet DLC. They appear after the Pugalisk has been killed, at the spot where its head fell to the ground. They can then be dug up with a Shovel to receive a Pugalisk Skull. On the Map, the Petrifying Bones will be marked with a red x, similar to the Secret Bandit Camp.

items.name: Petrifying Tome
items.description: The Petrifying Tome is an item added to The Forge in Don't Starve Together. Available immediately from Maxwell and Wickerbottom.

items.name: Pew-matic Horn
items.description: The Pew-matic Horn is a Ranged Weapon item exclusive to Wheeler from the Hamlet DLC. It can be loaded with almost any item in the game, but one can only put one kind of item at a time, with no limit to stack amount. The amount of damage depends on the item. The item is destroyed upon shooting.

items.name: Pherostone
items.description: The Pherostone is a naturally spawning Item exclusive to the Hamlet DLC. The Pherostone can be found once per world in the Ancient Pig Ruins, more specifically the ones that have an Mant statue on top of the Ruinous Entrance in the Gas Rainforest.
items.beginnerTip: Translates Mant speech.

items.name: Phlegm
items.description: Phlegm is an edible Item obtained by killing a Ewecus. When eaten, it will restore Hunger and reduce Sanity. Phlegm cannot be used as Fuel or Fertilizer, added to the Crock Pot, fed to Pigs, Birds, animals in the inventory, or used as bait in Traps or Bird Traps. However, Pigs will still eat Phlegm left on the floor, so it could be used in a Pig farm as a substitute for Powdercake since it does not spoil.

items.name: Phlegm/DST
items.description: Phlegm is an edible Item obtained by killing a Ewecus. When eaten, it will restore Hunger and reduce Sanity. Phlegm cannot be used as Fuel or Fertilizer, added to the Crock Pot, fed to Pigs, Birds, animals in the inventory, or used as bait in Traps or Bird Traps. However, Pigs will still eat Phlegm left on the floor, so it could be used in a Pig farm as a substitute for Powdercake since it does not spoil.

items.name: Phobic Experiment
items.description: Liquid courage.
items.beginnerTip: Protects players from sanity loss caused by totally normal bats.

items.name: Pierogi
items.description: Pierogi is a Meat Food Item cooked in the Crock Pot by adding 1 Egg, more than 0.25 Meat Units and more than 0.25 Vegetable Units. It takes 20 seconds to cook.

items.name: Pierogi/DST
items.description: Pierogi are a Meat Food Item cooked in the Crock Pot by adding at any Meat, 1 Egg, and 0.5 Vegetable. It takes 20 seconds to cook.

items.name: Pierrot Fish
items.description: Pierrot Fish are a Fish Food Item introduced in the Shipwrecked DLC. They can be obtained by stocking Fish Farms with Roe, together with Purple Groupers, Neon Quattro Fish and Tropical Fish. They can be used in the Crock Pot, and count as 0.5 units of Meat and 1 unit of Fish. They are specifically required to cook the Tropical Bouillabaisse. Pierrot Fish cannot be dried using a Drying Rack.

items.name: Pig Head
items.description: Pig Heads are decorative structures usually found around Touch Stones, Rundown Houses, and Merm villages. They are the severed heads of Pigs on sticks, similar to Merm Heads, the latter being often found in Pig Villages.

items.name: Pig Head/DST
items.description: -|Generic=

items.name: Pig Skin
items.description: A Pig Skin can be obtained by killing a Pig, Werepig, or Guardian Pig, or by deconstructing a Pig House with a Hammer or Deconstruction Staff or Pig Head with a Hammer.

items.name: Pig Skin/DST
items.description: A Pig Skin can be obtained by killing a Pig, Werepig, or Guardian Pig, or by deconstructing a Pig House with a Hammer or Deconstruction Staff or Pig Head with a Hammer.

items.name: Pig Torch
items.description: A Pig Torch is a naturally occurring Structure found in a Pig Fortress or near the Pig King in Adventure and Survival Mode. Pig Torches are protected by Guardian Pigs. If a Guardian Pig has been killed, the Pig Torch will respawn another Guardian Pig off-screen after 4 days. Guardian Pigs will occasionally refuel the Pig Torch, making the light brighter. A Pig Torch will eventually burn out if there are no Guardian Pigs left to refuel it. Other Guardian Pigs will not refuel a Pig Torch that is not their own.

items.name: Pig Torch/DST
items.description: A Pig Torch is a naturally occurring Structure found in Pig Guard Berry Fields. Pig Torches are protected by Guardian Pigs. If a Guardian Pig has been killed, the Pig Torch will respawn another Guardian Pig off-screen after 4 days. Guardian Pigs will occasionally refuel the Pig Torch, making the light brighter. A Pig Torch will eventually burn out if there are no Guardian Pigs left to refuel it. Other Guardian Pigs will not refuel a Pig Torch that is not their own.

items.description: For all your handy needs.

items.name: Pine Cone
items.description: Pine Cones can be planted to grow into Evergreen trees. It takes from 7.5 to 10 game hours for them to grow from saplings into small trees. They can also be used as a low-level fuel item. Planted saplings will not appear on the Map until they have progressed into the small tree stage.

items.name: Pith Pike
items.description: The Pith Pike is an item added to The Forge in Don't Starve Together. Available immediately from Wigfrid when playing as her.

items.name: Plants
items.description: This page lists the numerous Plants in Don't Starve, its DLCs and Don't Starve Together. Each one has their own unique use. Most plants are native to one biome, but can be found elsewhere if their frequency is increased using custom World Settings.

items.name: Platapine Quill
items.description: Platapine Quills are Items exclusive to the Hamlet DLC which are dropped by Platapines. Three of them are required to craft the Bird Whistle.

items.name: Poison Balm
items.description: The excruciating pain means it's working.
items.beginnerTip: Cures Poison.

items.name: Poison Birchnut Tree
items.description: When cutting down a fully sized Birchnut Tree that drops Birchnuts from day 3 and after, there is a small chance that other Birchnut Trees in the area will "awaken" and begin attacking anything in the area, unless it is Winter. This chance increases with the number of days survived from 3% on day 3 to 33% on day 70. After enough time passes (minimum one day,) Poison Birchnut Trees will calm down and return to their normal state. The player can also plant Birchnuts nearby to attempt to pacify them.

items.name: Poison Birchnut Tree/DST
items.description: When cutting down a fully sized Birchnut Tree that drops Birchnuts from day 3 and after, there is a small chance that other Birchnut Trees in the area will "awaken" and begin attacking anything in the area, unless it is Winter. This chance increases with the number of days survived from 3% on day 3 to 33% on day 70. After enough time passes (minimum one day,) Poison Birchnut Trees will calm down and return to their normal state. The player can also plant Birchnuts nearby to attempt to pacify them.

items.name: Poison Dartfrog Legs
items.description: Poison Dartfrog Legs are a Meat Food Item exclusive to Don't Starve: Hamlet DLC. Eating Poison Dartfrog Legs raw or cooked will restore a little bit of hunger, though it will poison the player. It also cannot be used as an ingredient in the Crock Pot.

items.name: Poison Spear
items.description: Jab'em with a sick stick.
items.beginnerTip: Poisons target.

items.name: Poisonous Hole
items.description: Poisonous Holes are naturally occurring objects present in Tidal Marsh biomes in the Shipwrecked DLC.

items.name: Pomegranate
items.description: A Pomegranate is a rare Fruit that can be Farmed from Farm Plots by planting Seeds for a 5% chance of growing, or using Pomegranate Seeds (Windblown Seeds). It can be used as an ingredient in several Crock Pot recipes. Feeding a Pomegranate to a Bird in a Birdcage will produce 1–2 Pomegranate Seeds with a 50% chance to also drop a regular seed.

items.name: Pomegranate/DST
items.description: A Pomegranate is a Fruit item that can be used as an ingredient in several Crock Pot recipes. When used in a Crock Pot, it provides 1 Fruit value. Feeding a Pomegranate to a Bird in a Birdcage will produce 1 Windblown Seeds.

items.name: Pond
items.description: Ponds are small bodies of water that usually spawn in Grasslands, Forests, Marshes, and Ruins.

items.name: Pond/DST
items.description: Ponds are small bodies of water that usually spawn in Grasslands, Forests, Marshes, and Ruins.

items.name: Portable Crock Pot
items.description: The Portable Crock Pot is a character-specific Item that Warly begins the game with. It acts as a Crock Pot that can be moved and replaced. It must be placed on the ground to cook anything.

items.name: Portable Grinding Mill
items.description: The Portable Grinding Mill is a craftable Item exclusive to Don't Starve Together. It can only be crafted and used by Warly, requiring 2 Gold Nuggets, 2 Electrical Doodads, and 4 Twigs. Like the Portable Crock Pot, it can be held in a player's inventory and can be placed as a Structure. When it is placed, it acts as a Crafting station and grants access to the Seasonings Filter.
items.beginnerTip: Portable. Grants access to the Seasonings Filter.

items.name: Potato
items.description: The Potato is a Vegetable Food Item exclusive to Don't Starve Together. Potatoes can be Farmed by planting Seeds with a moderate chance of growing them, by planting Fluffy Seeds, or by rummaging through a Junk Pile for a low chance at one.

items.name: Potted Fern
items.description: Make a pot and stick a fern inside.

items.name: Potted Fern/DST
items.description: Make a pot and stick a fern inside.

items.name: Potter's Wheel
items.description: Marble will be like clay in your hands.
items.beginnerTip: Unlocks the Sculptures Filter.

items.name: Powdercake
items.description: Powdercake is a Food item cooked in a Crock Pot by combining 1 Corn, 1 Honey, and 1 Twig. It takes 10 seconds to cook. It takes the longest time to rot out of all foods and was implemented as a joke.

items.description: Put your mind at ease.
items.beginnerTip: Restores the players' sanity on consumption and over time.

items.name: Puffed Potato Soufflé
items.description: Puffed Potato Soufflé is a Warly-specific Food Item cooked in the Portable Crock Pot, that is exclusive to Don't Starve Together. It requires two Potatoes and an Egg, and takes 40 seconds to cook. The filler can not be Inedible or Meats.

items.name: Puffy Vest
items.description: Warm enough for winter storms.
items.beginnerTip: Restores sanity over time. Delays freezing during Winter.

items.name: Puffy Vest/DST

items.name: Pugalisk Skull
items.description: The Pugalisk Skull is an Item exclusive to the Hamlet DLC. The Pugalisk Skull is dropped when the player uses a Shovel to dig up the Petrifying Bones dropped by the Pugalisk. It can be used to craft the Pugalisk Wand.

items.name: Pugalisk Wand
items.description: Wield the gaze of the Pugalisk!
items.beginnerTip: Creates hypnotic rays that freeze Mobs.

items.name: Pumpkin
items.description: A Pumpkin is an uncommon Vegetable that can be Farmed from Farm Plots by planting Seeds for a 11% chance of growing or using Pumpkin Seeds (Sharp Seeds). It can be used as an ingredient in several Crock Pot recipes, particularly Pumpkin Cookies. Feeding a Pumpkin to a Bird in a Birdcage will produce 1–2 Pumpkin Seeds, and half the time 1 regular Seeds. In Don't Starve Together, you will always get 1 Pumpkin Seed. It can also be combined with Fireflies (caught with a net) to create a Pumpkin Lantern.

items.name: Pumpkin Cookies
items.description: A Pumpkin Cookie is a Food item cooked in a Crock Pot by combining 1 Pumpkin and 2 Honey (or Honeycombs). It takes 40 seconds to cook.

items.name: Pumpkin Cookies/DST
items.description: A Pumpkin Cookie is a Food item cooked in a Crock Pot by combining 1 Pumpkin and 2 Honey (or Honeycombs). It takes 40 seconds to cook.

It can be used as an ingredient in several Crock Pot recipes, particularly Pumpkin Cookies. It can also be combined with Fireflies (caught with a net) to create a Pumpkin Lantern.

items.name: Purple Gem
items.description: By your colors combined!

items.name: Purple Grouper
items.description: Purple Groupers are a Fish Food Item introduced in the Shipwrecked DLC. They can be obtained by stocking Fish Farms with Roe, together with Pierrot Fish, Neon Quattro Fish, and Tropical Fish. They can be used in the Crock Pot, and count as 0.5 units of Meat and 1 unit of Fish. They are specifically required to cook the Tropical Bouillabaisse. Purple Groupers cannot be dried using a Drying Rack.

items.name: Purple Moonlens
items.description: No summary is available; see the linked wiki page.

items.name: Quacken Beak
items.description: The Quacken Beak is an Item exclusive to the Shipwrecked DLC. It can be obtained by defeating the Quacken. In fact, despite being apparently taken from the Quacken's body, the Quacken Beak is rewarded inside the Chest of the Depths, which the Quacken drops when defeated. It can be used to craft the Quackering Ram and the Quacken Drill.

items.name: Quackering Ram

items.name: Queen Womant
items.description: The Queen Womant is a Boss Monster exclusive to the Hamlet DLC. She can be accessed by going to the deepest part of a Mant Hill.

items.name: Queen's Visage
items.description: The Queen's Visage is a Hat Item exclusive to Don't Starve Together. It is the mask worn by Shrouded Queen. After beating Umbral Abomination for the first time, it can be found in the Ancient Gateway after leaving the arena.

items.name: Rabbit
items.description: A Rabbit is a passive Mob commonly found in Grassland, Forest, and Savanna biomes. They drop 1 Morsel when killed, while their Beardling counterparts can drop Monster Meat, Nightmare Fuel, or Beard Hair. Rabbits are cowardly creatures and will run away screaming if the player gets too close. They will also run straight to their Rabbit Holes at dusk or if they witness the death of a nearby Rabbit. Digging up a Rabbit Hole with a Shovel will evict any Rabbit inside and prevent them from hiding again, but Rabbit Holes will not respawn and thus can't produce more Rabbits.

items.name: Rabbit Earmuffs
items.description: A fuzzy little bit of warmth.
items.beginnerTip: : Protects against the Queen Womant's tail-tuba attack.

items.name: Rabbit Earmuffs/DST
items.description: A fuzzy little bit of warmth.

items.name: Rabbit Hole
items.description: Rabbit Holes are the home and spawning place for Rabbits. They run back to their holes at dusk, or when they are frightened. When a Rabbit is captured or killed, another will eventually respawn from the hole. A Rabbit Hole can be dug up with a Shovel to force a Rabbit out; however, this will destroy the hole, preventing future Rabbits from spawning there. If a Rabbit is caught outside its hole after dark for any reason, it will fall asleep.

items.description: The Radish is a Vegetable Food Item exclusive to the Hamlet DLC. Radish can be Farmed by planting Seeds in a Farm. When eaten raw, Radish restore 12.5 Hunger and 1 Health. They take 15 days to spoil and can be used in a Crock Pot. Radish are required to make Spicy Vegetable Stinger.

items.name: Raw Fish
items.description: Raw Fish is a Food Item found in the Shipwrecked DLC and Don't Starve Together. Both White Whales and Blue Whales drop 4 Raw Fish upon death. Also, the Tiger Shark drops 8 Raw Fish when killed.

items.name: Raw Fish/DST
items.description: Raw Fish and Fish Steak were added to Don't Starve Together in the Return of Them beta branch. Any large Ocean Fish variant will drop Raw Fish. Additionally, Gnarwails and Rockjaws drop 4 Raw Fish when killed.

items.description: Rawling is an Item exclusive to the Shipwrecked DLC. It is a sentient basketball that while carried, will comment on player actions. It speaks in red text, much like Lucy the Axe. When speaking a squeaking noise can be heard. It will also restore 2 /min while equipped in the hand slot. It can also be thrown, and throwing it restores 1 .

items.name: Red Cap
items.description: The Red Cap is a Vegetable food item that can be harvested from Red Mushrooms or Red Mushtrees. Eating it raw will restore 12.5 at the cost of 20 , making it unviable as a major food source for every character except for Wormwood, whose Health is unaffected by food. Still, Red Caps are a viable last resort against starvation since 12.5 will delay starvation by long enough to make up for the 20 penalty. Red Caps can be used as a Crock Pot filler without any health penalty. Red Caps can be dropped on the ground to indirectly damage Mobs if they eat it.

Still, Red Caps are a viable last resort against starvation since 12.5 will delay starvation by long enough to make up for the 20 penalty. Red Caps can be used as a Crock Pot filler without any health penalty. Red Caps can be dropped on the ground to indirectly damage Mobs if they eat it.

items.name: Red Gem
items.description: The Red Gem is an Item used to craft several Magical items. It can be used to craft the Fire Staff, Night Light, Life Giving Amulet, and Purple Gem.

items.name: Red Gem/DST
items.description: The Red Gem is an Item used to craft several Magical items. It can be used to craft the Fire Staff, Night Light, Life Giving Amulet, and Purple Gem.

items.name: Red Lantern
items.description: A fortuitous lantern to light your way.

items.name: Red Moonlens
items.description: No summary is available; see the linked wiki page.

items.name: Regal Scepter
items.description: The Regal Scepter is an Item introduced in the Hamlet DLC. It is found in the Pinacle Biome and can be given to the Pig Queen in exchange for a Royal Gallery Key. It can also be used as an infinitely durable weapon, though it only does 10 damage per hit.
items.beginnerTip: Can be traded for a Royal Gallery Key

items.name: Regular Jungle Tree
items.description: The Regular Jungle Tree is a variant of Tree found in Jungle Biomes in the Shipwrecked DLC. Much like the Totally Normal Tree, it drops 2 Living Logs when cut, and the stump may be dug up with a Shovel to obtain another Living Log. Because it drops no seeds, it cannot be replanted. It is usually found along with some Evil Flowers encircling the tree.

items.name: Relic
items.description: Relics (and Broken Relics) are the remains of the Ancient Civilization found in the Ruins. Broken Relics can be repaired with Rocks to restore 20 sanity. When destroyed, they can drop various items.

items.name: Relic Thing
items.description: The Relic Thing is one of the four Things in the Hamlet DLC. It is the Hamlet version of the Metal Potato Thing.

items.name: Relic/DST
items.description: Relics (and Broken Relics) are the remains of the Ancient Civilization found in the Ruins and in the Ancient Archive. Broken Relics can be repaired with Rocks, Cut Stone and Stone Wall to restore 5 Sanity. Smashing it (but not destroyed) and repairing it again will gain 5 Sanity again.

items.name: Resplendent Nox Helm
items.description: The Resplendent Nox Helm is an item added to The Forge in Don't Starve Together. It drops in the middle of the tenth wave from a random enemy unit with a 50% chance, a flowering wreath may drop instead. If not dropped, it is guaranteed to drop from the Great Furnace Warrior Hog.

items.name: Riled Lucy
items.description: Riled Lucy is Woodie's starting item in The Forge event.

items.name: Ring Thing
items.description: The Ring Thing is an item and one of four Things used on the Wooden Thing to travel to the next world. It spawns naturally in every world in its own Set Piece. It is encircled by Evil Flowers.

items.name: Ro Bin Gizzard Stone
items.description: The Ro Bin Gizzard Stone is an Item exclusive to the Hamlet DLC that spawns from the hatched Stone Egg along with Ro Bin. As long as the Gizzard Stone is in the player's Inventory, the Ro Bin will always follow them, similar to the Eye Bone attracting Chester.
items.beginnerTip: Attracts Ro Bin.

items.name: Rock Den
items.description: The Rock Den is a naturally spawning object exclusive to Don't Starve Together, introduced in A New Reign. It is a small cave with two eyes looking out and is frequently found in the Mosaic Biome.
items.beginnerTip: Unlocks the Critters Filter.

items.name: Rock Lobster
items.description: Rock Lobsters are neutral Mobs found in Caves. They eat all minerals except for Marble, all of which can be given to them to befriend them. They grow over time, slowly regenerate their health, and come in a variety of colors. They are also immune to the freezing effect of the Ice Staff.

items.name: Rock Thing
items.description: The Rock Thing is one of the four Things in the Hamlet DLC. It is the Hamlet version of the Box Thing.

items.name: Rocks/DST
items.description: Rocks are a resource which can be found on the surface and in the Caves. They are used to craft several Items and Structures, and can also be Refined to Cut Stones.

items.name: Rocky Beach Turf
items.description: A patch of pebbled beach.

items.name: Rocky Turf
items.description: Rocky Turf is one of the Turf items, acquired by digging Rockyland tiles with a Pitchfork. Like other Turfs, it can be placed on any bare ground tile or it can be used as fuel. It can also be used to craft Cobblestones, which are placeable Roads.

items.name: Rocky Turf/DST
items.description: A chunk of rocky ground.

items.name: Roe

items.name: Sand
items.description: Sand is a resource found in the Shipwrecked DLC. Sand can be obtained by digging Sandy Piles found on the Beach biomes with a Shovel. Each use of Shovel will yield one pile of Sand, and full size Sandy Piles can be dug twice. Sandy Piles regenerate over time, making Sand renewable. Sand is an important resource early in the game, as it is required for crafting Chimineas, Buoyant Chimineas and Sandbags, which are structures that greatly help in surviving Hurricane Season and Monsoon Season respectively. It can also be used to craft a Sand Castle or a Sea Lab. Sand can also be refined into Empty Bottles.

It can be obtained using the Tree Tapping Kit by attaching it to a Sugarwood Tree. After 2 minutes, the bucket will fill up and can be collected for Sap.

items.name: Sapling
items.description: Saplings are small Plants found commonly in Grasslands and Forests. They can be picked to provide 1 Twig, after which they will need 4 days to regrow. Saplings can be dug up with a Shovel and replanted in a new location (typically closer to a base camp). Saplings can't be planted on Checkerboard Floorings, Wooden Floorings, Cobblestones, Carpeted Floorings, Rocky Turfs, Sandy Turfs, and Cave Rock Turfs, unless it has been planted before these turfs were placed. Unlike Grass Tufts and Berry Bushes, Saplings don't require fertilization to regrow after being replanted. This is similar to Spiky Bushes, which can be harvested without fertilization.

In DST, using at least 1 Eel is mandatory, otherwise the resulting meal will be Surf 'n' Turf which requires 2.5 Meat value. Currently, Eel is the only Fish with more Fish value than Meat value (1.0 Fish value and 0.5 Meat).

items.name: Seashell
items.description: A Seashell is a resource found in the Shipwrecked DLC. They are used in the crafting of several recipes. They can be found frequently in Beach biome, near the shore. Once picked, it will be eligible to regenerate at its original spawn point after 2 days, and will then regenerate when the Tides at night reach that spot. If the spawn location of the Seashell is Flooded during Monsoon Season, the Seashell will not spawn.

Seaweed can be used in the Crock Pot and is also used in several crafting recipes. It can be dried on Drying Racks to acquire Dried Seaweed. __NOTOC__

items.name: Seeds
items.description: Seeds are a Food Item commonly left on the ground by Birds. While they can be eaten, Seeds are primarily used for Farming by planting them in a farm plot to grow crops. When planted, Seeds have a chance to grow into Corn, Carrot, Pumpkin, Eggplant, Pomegranate, Durian or Dragon Fruit (see Farming for further information). Birds, Tallbirds, Smallish Tallbirds, Smallbirds, and Pigs can eat Seeds and will pick Seeds up if they find them on the ground. Pigs that eat Seeds don't produce Manure. Seeds can be used to bait Bird Traps.

On some occasions, the player will have to retrieve the items from the set piece in order to escape the danger.

Shark Fins cannot be cooked but can be used in Crock Pot recipes, and have a food value of 0.5 Meat and 1 Fish. They will not be eaten by Mobs that consume edible items on the ground and cannot be fed to Wildbores. They also cannot be given to the Yaarctopus.

Note that destroying a Potter's Wheel which has taken any Sketches will also drop the Sketches. Sketches can be erased at a Cartographer's Desk to get one Papyrus. items.name: Slurper
items.description: The Slurper is a creature found only in the Ruins, in Wilds, Village and rarely in the Mushtree Forest biome. It attacks by rolling to and biting the target and then jumping up and engulfing the player's head with its mouth.
items.beginnerTip: Emits light.

items.name: Slurper Pelt
items.description: The Slurper Pelt is an item with a 50% chance to be dropped by Slurpers. It can be used to craft a Belt of Hunger. Like meat items, a Slurper Pelt can be used to befriend a Pig, or it can be exchanged with the Pig King for a Gold Nugget. However, Bunnymen don't count it as meat, and won't mind if a player has one/picks one up.

Slurtles/Snurtles emerge from the mound after earthquakes to eat the fallen Rocks, Flint, Nitre, Gold, and Gems. Snurtles rarely spawn from the Mound and flee immediately instead of attacking the player. Snurtles, when given the opportunity, will eat Earthquake items in the same fashion as the Slurtle.

items.name: Slurtle Slime

It is very explosive and can trigger Earthquakes when ignited. It deals 50 damage per charge (It can be exploded in stacks) and is a very good alternative to Gunpowder as it can be easily farmed by feeding Slurtles minerals, though it deals less damage on exploding. Additionally, it can be used to refuel a Lantern or a Miner Hat by 9.5%.

items.name: Spicy Chili
items.description: Spicy Chili is a Meat Food item included in the Reign of Giants DLC. It can be cooked in the Crock Pot by combining 1.5 units of Meats and 1.5 units of Vegetables, except Peppers, which will result in Stuffed Pepper Poppers. No fillers are available for this recipe.
items.beginnerTip: Increases temperature by 15 degrees over 15 seconds.

items.name: Spicy Chili/DST

items.beginnerTip: Increases temperature by 15 degrees over 15 seconds.

items.name: Spicy Vegetable Stinger
items.description: Spicy Vegetable Stinger is a Crock Pot Food Item exclusive to the Hamlet DLC. It requires either a Radish/Asparagus, an Ice, and 1.5 additional Vegetables (total vegetable value of the recipe = 2.5 including Radish/Asparagus or Toma Root in Don't Starve Together). It takes 10 seconds to cook. Because it requires 4 ingredients to make, there cannot be fillers.

items.name: Spider Den
items.description: A Spider Den is a nest in which Spiders and Spider Warriors spawn and live. Spiders emerge in search of food at Dusk and return to their Dens at dawn. The number of Spiders that live in a Den varies depending on its size (see table below). When a Den reaches its final stage, it evolves into a Spider Queen. Spider Dens are surrounded by a creep-like substance called Sticky Webbing, which slows down anything caught in it, aside from Spiders. Sticky Webbing will grow on any surface except a small area around a Rabbit Hole.

The number of Spiders that live in a Den varies depending on its size (see table below). When a Den reaches its final stage, it evolves into a Spider Queen. Spider Dens are surrounded by a creep-like substance called Sticky Webbing, which slows down anything caught in it, aside from Spiders. Sticky Webbing will grow on any surface except a small area around a Rabbit Hole.

items.name: Spider Eggs
items.description: Get a little help from your friends.

items.name: Spider Eggs/DST
items.description: Get a little help from your friends.

items.name: Spider Gland
items.description: A Spider Gland is a healing item dropped by Spiders when killed or a Spilagmite when mined. It restores 8 Health when used by the players or when used on Mobs (including hostile enemies). Spider Glands can be used to craft Healing Salve.
items.beginnerTip: Healing properties

items.name: Spider Queen
items.description: The Spider Queen is an aggressive Boss Monster added to the game in the Long Live the Queen update. She has 1250 health and attacks by biting and stabbing with her sharp claws, doing 80 damage with each attack.

items.name: Spider Queen/DST
items.description: The Spider Queen is an aggressive Boss Monster added to the game in the Long Live the Queen update. She has 2500 health and attacks by biting and stabbing with her sharp claws, doing 80 damage with each attack.

items.name: Spiderhat
items.description: The Spiderhat is a Hat Item dropped by Spider Queens that allows the player to control Spiders. This also works for all the Spiders in Caves, but they will not follow the player in or out of the caves. However, Spider Queens will see through this disguise and will attack the player regardless. The hat only lasts for 2 minutes (6 game hours), degrading while equipped.

The hat only lasts for 2 minutes (6 game hours), degrading while equipped.

items.name: Spiky Bush
items.description: The Spiky Bush is an in-game flora commonly found in Marsh and Desert biomes. It acts as a source of Twigs, like Saplings. Spiky Bushes are not affected by Winter cold and will regrow after 4 game days during both Summer and in Winter. Harvesting Twigs from a spiky bush damages by 3 points.

items.name: Spiky Bush/DST
items.description: The Spiky Bush is an in-game flora commonly found in Marsh and Desert biomes. It acts as a source of Twigs, like Saplings. Spiky Bushes are not affected by Winter cold and will regrow after 4 game days during both Summer and in Winter. Harvesting Twigs from a spiky bush damages by 3 points.

items.name: Spiky Tree
items.description: Spiky Trees are found only in the Marsh. Instead of dropping Logs when chopped like other trees, Spiky Trees drop Twigs with only a 20% chance to drop a Log. Also, these trees do not have a life-cycle (changing size over time). There is also no way to replant them. Like other trees, the stumps of the Spiky variety can be dug up with a Shovel or Regal Shovel to get an additional log.

items.name: Spiky Tree/DST
items.description: Spiky Trees are found only in Marsh and Desert biomes. Instead of dropping Logs when chopped like other trees, Spiky Trees drop Twigs with only a 20% chance to drop a Log. Also, these trees do not have a life-cycle (changing size over time). There is also no way to replant them. Like other trees, the stumps of the Spiky variety can be dug up with a Shovel or Regal Shovel to get an additional log.

items.name: Spilagmite
items.description: A Spilagmite is a different kind of Spider Den found only in Caves. It spawns Cave Spiders and Spitters. Spiders will regularly spawn from a Spilagmite at a rate of 1 approximately every 4 minutes, unless something makes them spawn differently (e.g. something walks on the webbing or an earthquake occurs).

items.name: Spilagmite/DST
items.description: A Spilagmite is a different kind of Spider Den found only in Caves. It spawns Cave Spiders and Spitters. Spiders will regularly spawn from a Spilagmite at a rate of 1 approximately every 4 minutes, unless something makes them spawn differently (e.g. something walks on the webbing or an earthquake occurs).

items.name: Spiral Spear
items.description: The Spiral Spear is an item added to The Forge in Don't Starve Together (an unlockable item in the 2018 Crucible). Dropped by the last enemy of wave 9.

items.name: Splumonkey Pod
items.description: The Splumonkey Pod is an object found in Ruins, most commonly in the Village Biome. It appears as a large wooden monkey head idol with Cave Banana "hair" and a gaping mouth. Splumonkeys spawn from the Splumonkey Pod, with a maximum of four Splumonkeys out at a time. Splumonkey Pods will spawn a Splumonkey every 30 seconds and if one or more have been killed, will regenerate Splumonkeys every 120 seconds.

items.name: Splumonkey Pod/DST
items.description: The Splumonkey Pod is a Structure found in Ruins, most commonly in the Village Biome. It appears as a large wooden monkey head idol with Cave Banana "hair" and a gaping mouth. Splumonkeys spawn from the Splumonkey Pod, with a maximum of four Splumonkeys out at a time. Splumonkey Pods will spawn a Splumonkey every 30 seconds and if one or more have been killed, will regenerate Splumonkeys every 120 seconds.

items.name: Spoiled Fish
items.description: Spoiled Fish is an item introduced in the Shipwrecked DLC. Dead Dogfish and Dead Swordfish will turn into Spoiled Fish instead of Rot if left to spoil. It is also possible to pick one up in a Trawl Net. Giving Packim Baggims a Dead Dogfish or a Dead Swordfish will result in it spitting out a Spoiled Fish. Spoiled Fish can be Hammered to get 2 Bone Shards.

items.name: Sprouting Stone Fruit
items.description: Sprouting Stone Fruit is an item exclusive to Don't Starve Together. It can be obtained by mining a Stone Fruit, but the chance of receiving a Sprouting Stone Fruit is fairly low, 1%. Sprouting Stone Fruits can be planted to grow a Stone Fruit Bush, and this Stone Fruit Bush doesn't need to be fertilized.

items.name: Stag Antler
items.description: The Stag Antler is an Item exclusive to Don't Starve Together, introduced in A New Reign. It is dropped by Klaus when he's killed, and is used to open the Loot Stash. As long as the Stag Antler exists in a world, Klaus can not be spawned by using a Deer Antler on the Loot Stash.

items.name: Stalacmite Throne
items.description: Stalacmite Throne is an object exclusive to the Hamlet DLC. It is found after killing Queen Womant. It can be mined for 8 Rocks, 2~6 Flints, 0~4 Nitres, 0~2 Gold Dust, 0~4 Gold Nuggets and 0~2 Blue Gems.

items.name: Stalagmite
items.description: A Stalagmite is the Underground equivalent of a Boulder. It can be mined using either a Pickaxe, Opulent Pickaxe, or Pick/Axe. Stalagmites drop various minerals when mined.

items.name: Stalagmite/DST
items.description: A Stalagmite is the Underground equivalent of a Boulder. It can be mined using any pickaxe, such as a Pickaxe, Opulent Pickaxe, or Pick/Axe. Stalagmites drop various minerals when mined.

items.name: Stalking Stick
items.description: The Stalking Stick is an equippable Item exclusive to the Hamlet DLC. Just like the Walking Cane, it is a speed increasing item, which can also be used as a weapon. It is made by drying a Flytrap Stalk on a Drying Rack. It increases the character's movement speed by 30% while equipped (which is 5 percent points faster than the Walking Cane). It has a durability of three in-game days, and it can be repaired to 100% durability by a Sewing Kit.
items.beginnerTip: 30% faster movement speed

items.name: Steamed Ham Sandwich
items.description: The Steamed Ham Sandwich is a Crock Pot Food Item exclusive to the Hamlet DLC.

items.name: Steel Wool
items.description: Steel Wool is an Item obtained by killing an Ewecus. It is a major crafting ingredient of the War Saddle and the Brush. It can also be burned, providing the same burn time as a Log.

items.name: Steel Wool/DST
items.description: Steel Wool is an Item obtained by killing an Ewecus. It is a major crafting ingredient of the War Saddle and the Brush. It can also be burned, providing the same burn time as a Log. In Don't Starve Together, Steel Wool is required to adopt an Ewelet at the Rock Den.

items.name: Stinger
items.description: A Stinger is an item commonly dropped by a Bee or Killer Bee when killed. It is an ingredient in Sleep Darts.

items.name: Stinger/DST
items.description: A Stinger is an item commonly dropped by a Bee or Killer Bee when killed. Stingers can be obtained by either killing Bees or Killer Bees with Weapons, or with the help of other Mobs, or by catching Bees or Killer Bees with a Bug Net then murdering them in the inventory. If the player or any mob attacks a Bee (including catching them with the Bug Net) remaining members of the same Bee Hive (or Bee Box) will emerge as Killer Bees and all members of the hive in the vicinity will target the attacker.

items.name: Stone Egg
items.description: The Stone Egg is an naturally spawning Item exclusive to the Hamlet DLC. It is found at the BFB's nest and can be grown slowly until hatching into Ro Bin along with the Ro Bin Gizzard Stone. It will take 3 days for the egg to hatch, so long as it stays within the required heat conditions.
items.beginnerTip: Hatches into Ro Bin and the Ro Bin Gizzard Stone.

items.name: Stone Fruit
items.description: The Stone Fruit is an Item exclusive to Don't Starve Together, introduced in Return of Them. Picking a Stone Fruit Bush yields 3 Stone Fruits at a time, though if left on the bush for too long, the Stone Fruits will appear cracked and picking the bush will yield nothing. Stone Fruits can also fall during Earthquakes in the Lunar Grotto.

items.name: Stone Fruit Bush
items.description: Stone Fruit Bushes are Plants exclusive to Don't Starve Together that can be found on the Lunar Island. They can be harvested to obtain 3 Stone Fruit.

items.name: Stone Plug
items.description: The Stone Plug is a Naturally spawning Structure exclusive to Hamlet DLC. It is a unique object which can exclusively be found inside the BFB's Caves; it mainly acts as an obstacle which has to be mined in order to exit these caves.
items.beginnerTip: Can be mined to exit the BFB's Caves

items.name: Stone Slab
items.description: Stone Slabs are objects exclusive to the Hamlet DLC. The slab can be flipped for a chance to find various resources. One item or mob can be found underneath each Stone Slab that is flipped.
items.beginnerTip: Flipping the slab yields item based on the biome.

items.name: Striking Carving
items.description: Striking Carvings are Traps found only within the Ancient Pig Ruins introduced in the Hamlet DLC. Each one in a room will shoot a Blow Dart which has 34 damage when Lost Relics in the room are chiseled or mined, or when the player steps on a Pressure Plate. Striking Carvings eventually regenerate their Blow Darts. They can be disarmed with Disarming Tools, dropping a Blow Dart, ceasing to function and changing the appearance to look broken.
items.beginnerTip: Shoots a Blow Dart when triggered.

items.name: Striking Statue
items.description: Striking Statues are variants of the Striking Carving Trap in the Hamlet DLC that take the form of a small pig. Like those, they are only found in the Ancient Pig Ruins and triggered when Lost Relics in the room are chiseled or mined, or when the player steps on a Pressure Plate. In addition to shooting Blow Darts which have 34 damage each, these statues start to rotate clockwise when triggered.
items.beginnerTip: Rotates. Shoots Blow Darts when triggered.

items.name: Stuffed Eggplant
items.description: Stuffed Eggplant is a Vegetable Food Item cooked in the Crock Pot with 1 Eggplant, 1 different vegetable and 2 fillers. It takes 40 seconds to cook.

items.description: Stuffed Fish Heads is a Crock Pot recipe exclusive to Don't Starve Together introduced in Return of Them. It is made of 1 Barnacles and at least 1 other Fishes with a total value of at least 1.0, filler can be anything.

items.name: Stuffed Night Cap
items.description: Stuffed Night Cap is a Meat Food Item exclusive to Don't Starve Together. It is cooked in the Crock Pot by combining 2 raw Moon Shrooms, 1 raw Monster Meat and a filler.

items.name: Stuffed Pepper Poppers
items.description: Stuffed Pepper Poppers are a Meat Food Item exclusive to Don't Starve Together. They are cooked in a Crock Pot by combining a Pepper and Meats with a total Meat value of 1.5 or below.
items.beginnerTip: Increases temperature by 15 degrees over 15 seconds.

items.name: Surf 'n' Turf
items.description: Surf 'n' Turf is a Meat item bundled with the Shipwrecked DLC (now available in Don't Starve Together). It is cooked in the Crock Pot by adding any Meats and Fishes with a total Fish/Seafood value of 1.5 or higher and a total Meat value of all the ingredients of 2.5 or higher. Because of the high requirements, this recipe requires either using a Wobster, which has fish value of 2, or using at least one ingredient that has both fish and meat values, such as Tropical Fish, Fish, Dogfish, Shark Fin, Raw Fish, Eel, or Swordfish, all of which have a fish value of 1 and meat value of 0.5. Multiple Monster Meats can be used in the recipe (as long as the recipe requirements are met) without the fear of making Monster Lasagna, since Surf 'n' Turf recipe has a higher priority than Monster Lasagna.

items.name: Sweet Potato
items.description: The Sweet Potato is a Vegetable Food item in the Shipwrecked DLC. Sweet Potatoes have exactly the same raw and cooked stats as carrots. Sweet Potatoes can be Farmed by planting Seeds for a 22.2% chance of growing or using Sweet Potato Seeds. It should be noted that Sweet Potatoes will only be available via farming in Worlds that are compatible with the Shipwrecked or Hamlet DLC.

items.name: Sweet Potato Souffle
items.description: Sweet Potato Souffle is a Warly-specific Food item cooked in the Portable Crock Pot by adding 2 Raw Sweet Potatoes and 2.0 units of Eggs. It takes 40 seconds to cook. Using Cooked Sweet Potatoes will result in Ratatouille instead.

items.name: Swinesbury City Hall
items.description: The Swinesbury City Hall is a naturally spawning Pig Shop Structure exclusive to the Hamlet DLC. It is found in Swinesbury Pig City and sells a variety of permits and contracts to the player.

items.name: Swordfish
items.description: Swordfish are hostile Mobs found in the Shipwrecked DLC. They spawn in the Deep Ocean from an invisible spawner. One will spawn in the same spot every 60–120 seconds, as long as the player is nearby.

items.name: Syrup
items.description: The Syrup is an item exclusive to The Gorge event in Don't Starve Together. It can be obtained by cooking 3 Saps in a Syrup Pot. It is used for cooking some of The Gorge Recipes.

items.name: Tall Grass
items.description: Tall Grass is a Plant exclusive to Don't Starve: Hamlet DLC, which can be found in the Plains and Rainforest Biomes. Just like the grass in the base game, it yields Cut Grass, but only with the help of a tool. Unlike Grass Tuft, Tall Grass take 4 days to regrow (Rain will reduce this time) and never withered because of high temperature. However, like Grass Tuft, Tall Grass do not grow during Winter.

items.name: Tallbird Egg
items.description: A Tallbird Egg is a large blue egg with white speckles. They can be found in Tallbird Nests, guarded by a single Tallbird, and will hatch into a new Tallbird (after a few days), if the mother is killed. Tallbird Eggs can be used as a Food item to restore 3 Health and 25 Hunger. They can also be used as an ingredient in a variety of Crock Pot Dishes, do not spoil and do not stack. A Tallbird Egg can be placed near a heat source, where it will become a Hatching Tallbird Egg and eventually hatch into a Smallbird.

items.name: Tallbird Egg/DST
items.description: A Tallbird Egg is a large blue egg with white speckles. They can be found in Tallbird Nests, guarded by a single Tallbird, and will hatch into a new Tallbird (after a few days), if the mother is killed. Tallbird Eggs can be used as a Food item to restore 3 Health and 25 Hunger. They can also be used as an ingredient in a variety of Crock Pot Dishes. The Tallbird Eggs do not spoil and do not stack. A Tallbird Egg can be placed near a heat source, where it will become a Hatching Tallbird Egg and eventually hatch into a Smallbird.

items.description: Tar is a resource Item introduced in the Shipwrecked DLC. It can be gathered from Tar Slicks using a Tar Extractor and is required for a variety of crafting recipes.

items.name: Tarnished Crown
items.description: The Tarnished Crown is an Item used to unlock the Shipwrecked character, Wilbur. It has a 10% chance to drop when any Prime Ape dies or any Prime Ape Hut is destroyed. The drop will not be available if Wilbur is already unlocked or a Tarnished Crown already exists in the world.
items.beginnerTip: Unlocks Wilbur as a playable character.

items.name: Tea
items.description: Tea is a Crock Pot dish introduced in the Hamlet DLC. It requires at least two Orange Pikos and 1 Sweetener, and excluding Meats, Vegetables, Twigs, and Ice. Adding ice will instead result in Iced Tea.
items.beginnerTip: Boosts temperature and speed.

items.name: Tea Tree
items.description: The Tea Tree is a tree type exclusive to Don't Starve: Hamlet DLC, found in the Cultivated Biome outside of the Hamlets. A fully grown Tea Tree yields 1 Twigs, 2 Seed Pods, and 2 Logs when chopped.

items.name: Tentacle
items.description: Tentacles are hostile Monsters that specifically spawn in Marshes or Caves, though they will not spawn on world-generated roads. Wickerbottom can summon Tentacles using On Tentacles, one of her self-published books.

items.name: Tentacle Spike
items.description: The Tentacle Spike is a Melee Weapon. It is a purple tentacle with spikes protruding from one end, similar to a spiked mace. It has a 50% chance to drop from Tentacles, which are found in Marshes and Caves, or Big Tentacles, which are found only in Caves. If a Big Tentacle has already dropped one, no other Big Tentacles can drop them for the rest of the Day.

items.name: Tentacle Spike/DST
items.description: The Tentacle Spike is a Melee Weapon. It is a purple tentacle with spikes protruding from one end, similar to a spiked mace. It has a 50% chance to drop from Tentacles, which are found in Marshes and Caves, or Big Tentacles, which are found only in Caves. If a Big Tentacle has already dropped one, no other Big Tentacles can drop them for the rest of the Day.

items.name: Tentacle Spots
items.description: Tentacle Spots are a rare item with a 20% drop chance from a killed Tentacle and a 40% chance from a killed Big Tentacle. They can be used to craft the Feather Hat, and Wickerbottom can use them to craft the Book, "On Tentacles". Tentacle Spots do not spoil and can also be burned as fuel in a Campfire or Fire Pit.

items.name: Tentacle Spots/DST
items.description: Tentacle Spots are a rare item with a 20% drop chance from a killed Tentacle and a 40% chance from a killed Big Tentacle. items.name: Varg

When tracking Suspicious Dirt Piles, there is a chance for a Varg to be found instead of a Koalefant or a Ewecus. This chance starts at 2.5% on Day one, and gradually increases to 16.5% chance on Day 100. When killed, the Varg drops around 4-6 Monster Meat and 1-3 Hound's Tooth.

items.name: Volt Goat Horn

Waffles are a difficult food to obtain due to needing butter, which has a 2% chance of dropping from butterflies. Eggs are also another factor which limits you from getting waffles early-game.

Walls can be made out of Grass, Boards, Stone, and Thulecite, in order of increasing material strength.

items.name: Walrus Camp

It's used as a base by these Mobs, known collectively as the MacTusk 'n' Son Scottish Nobleman Walrus Hunting Party. The Walrus Camp will only spawn mobs during Winter. Walrus Camps will spawn on all terrain, except Marsh Biomes. The igloo often appears near Maxwell's Door, and two or more will often spawn in a close vicinity to each other. The MacTusk Hunting Party will spawn about every 2.5-3 days from a fully functioning Walrus Camp.

Walrus Camps will spawn on all terrain, except Marsh Biomes. The MacTusk Hunting Party will spawn about every 2.5-3 days from a fully functioning Walrus Camp.

items.description: Water Beefalo, also known as Ox, are the Shipwrecked version of Beefalo. They have the same characteristics as Beefalo, with the only differences being that the Water Beefalo do not drop Beefalo Wool if killed, they run faster than regular Beefalo, and they drop Horns instead of Beefalo Horns. They are native to the Mangrove biome and are usually found with a small herd. While they spend most of their time in water, they can also walk on land.

It can be used as an ingredient in several Crock Pot recipes, particularly Melonsicles. Feeding a Watermelon to Birds in a Birdcage will produce 1–2 Watermelon Seeds. When eaten, it will also decrease the perceived temperature by 40 degrees for 5 seconds.

items.name: Watermelon/DST

items.name: Watery Grave
items.description: Watery Graves are naturally occurring structures found in the Shipwrecked DLC. They can be found in the dark colored ship graveyards in the Ocean and can be fished out of the water. Collecting them costs 10 Sanity. When retrieved, they have a 10% chance to spawn a Pirate Ghost. Otherwise, they will always yield a Seaweed. In addition, they may yield a Coral (75% chance) and a random Trinket (50% chance). If the Bone Key, one of the keys needed to unlock the playable Woodlegs character, does not exist in the world yet, each Watery grave will have a chance to contain it. This chance is equal to 1 / (Number of Watery Graves left in the world), meaning the key is guaranteed to be obtained by fishing all the Watery Graves.

It can also be dropped when any tier Spider Den or Spilagmite is destroyed or a Spider Queen is killed with the same chance. The skull will not drop if it already exists in the world or if Webber is already unlocked. Trapped Spiders will not drop the skull.

As an exception, the Eternal Fruitcake will be rejected by any character upon attempting to eat it, making it only useful for feeding other creatures (e.g. Pigs, to obtain Manure). All Winter Foods stack up to 40. Gingerbread Cookies, Sugar Cookies, Candy Canes, Eternal Fruitcakes and Chocolate Log Cakes can also be used to decorate Winter's Feast Trees.

items.name: Wobster
items.description: A Wobster is a catchable sea creature found in the Don't Starve: Shipwrecked DLC. Wobsters spawn from Wobster Dens, which house one Wobster each. Wobsters are nocturnal, and will only come out at Dusk, will stay out all through the Night, and will retreat back to their dens when the next day begins. Players who get too close will also cause them to be scared and go back to their dens.

items.name: Wobster Bisque
items.description: Wobster Bisque is a Crock Pot recipe introduced in the Shipwrecked DLC. It is made from Wobster and Ice. Since the Crock Pot will not accept Dead / Delicious Wobster, a living Wobster must be used.

items.name: Wobster Den
items.description: Wobster Dens are a naturally occurring structure from the Shipwrecked DLC. They are the home and spawning place for Wobsters, found only in the Shallow Ocean. Wobsters will come out of their holes at Dusk, staying into the night until dawn. They will retreat back if frightened. When a Wobster is captured or killed, another will respawn from the hole in a half to one and a half days.

items.name: Wobster Dinner
items.description: Wobster Dinner is a Crock Pot recipe introduced in the Shipwrecked DLC. It is cooked by adding 1 Wobster and 1 Butter. It takes 20 seconds to cook. It restores 60 , 37.5 , and 50 , making it one of the best food items to restore both Health and Sanity.

items.name: Wobster/DST
items.description: The Wobster was introduced to Don't Starve Together in Return of Them. They spawn from Wobster Mounds during Dusk and Night. They can be used alive in a Crock Pot for their 1.0 fish and 1.0 meat value. Aside from all the fish and meat dishes they can be used for, they have two exclusive recipes: Lobster Bisque and Lobster Dinner. While both recipes excel at healing by granting 60 HP, the latter also gives 50 sanity and is Maxwell's favorite dish, providing him with additional 15 Hunger upon consumption.

items.name: Wooden Potato Thing
items.description: The Wooden Potato Thing is the Shipwrecked equivalent to the Metal Potato Thing in both Sandbox Mode and Adventure Mode. It serves the same purpose as the Metal Potato Thing, and is used with the other Things on the Wooden Thing to create a portal that lets players generate a new World, deleting everything except the items in their inventory.

items.name: Wooden Thing
items.description: The Wooden Thing (commonly referred to as the Teleportato, when completed) is a unique Structure in Don't Starve. It spawns naturally in every world in its own Set Piece. It is guarded by 1 Clockwork Rook, 2 Clockwork Knights, and 2 Clockwork Bishops. The area is also surrounded by Evil Flowers and Marble Trees laid on a Chess Biome.

items.name: Woodlegs' Keys
items.description: Woodlegs' Keys are items found in the Shipwrecked DLC. They are used to free Woodlegs from his cage at the Volcano and can each be obtained in different ways. __TOC__

items.name: Wreck
items.description: A Wreck is a naturally occurring structure found in the Shipwrecked DLC. It can occasionally be encountered in the Ocean biome, on dark-colored "ship graveyard" tiles, and in the Coral Reef biome. It appears a broken down part of a sunken ship. It is covered with Limpets and can be harvested every 3 days to yield 1-3 Limpets. It can be hammered down to obtain 1 Boards, but doing so may summon a Pirate Ghost. __NOTOC__

items.name: X Marks the Spot
items.description: X Marks the Spot is an object in the Shipwrecked DLC that appears only after its location has been revealed by reading a Message in a Bottle. It appears as two X-crossed bones over disturbed soil. It can be dug up with a Shovel or shot with a Boat Cannon to reveal Bone Shards and a Chest containing several pieces of treasure. Players should be cautious as one treasure preset spawns 3 Snakes when dug up.

items.name: Yellow Gem
items.description: Transmute Orange Gems into Yellow Gems.

items.name: Yellow Gem/DST
items.description: The Yellow Gem is an item used to craft Ancient items. It is required in two main crafting recipes; the Magiluminescence and Star Caller's Staff. The Magiluminescence is an amulet that emits light, increases movement speed, and provides a Sanity boost when worn. The Star Caller's Staff summons a Dwarf Star that emits light and heat. It can also be used for Cooking Food.
